query: The built-in prompt in llm.py instructs the LLM Agent to use an incorrect name for the GetLiveContext tool (breaking GetLiveContext) ### The problem # Assist LLM tool names can differ from names referenced in built-in prompt ## The problem Since the LLM tool-namespacing changes introduced in Home Assistant 2026.9, the built-in instructions supplied to an Assist LLM can reference a tool name that does not match the actual name of the tool exposed to the LLM. A concrete example is `GetLiveContext`. The Home Assistant LLM platform defines the tool as: ```text homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` and its built-in dynamic prompt instructs the LLM to call: ```text homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` However, when the tool is exposed through the Assist API, it is additionally namespaced and the actual tool available to the LLM is: ```text assist__homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` This creates a situation where the LLM can receive an explicit instruction to call a tool whose exact name does not exist in its tool registry. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Run Home Assistant Core 2026.9.1 with a local LLM conversation agent. 2. Use an Ollama-based conversation agent with the Home Assistant/Assist tools available. 3. Ask the agent a question requiring live Home Assistant state, such as: > What is on? 4. When the model follows the built-in `GetLiveContext` instruction, it may attempt to call: ```text homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` 5. Home Assistant returns: ```text HomeAssistantError: Tool "homeassistant__GetLiveContext" not found ``` The correctly namespaced tool is: ```text assist__homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` and calling that exact name succeeds and returns the expected live context. I verified this directly with the same conversation agent: ```text homeassistant__GetLiveContext → Tool "homeassistant__GetLiveContext" not found assist__homeassistant__GetLiveContext → successful Live Context response ``` I also asked the LLM to enumerate its available tools using their exact names. The registry contained: ```text assist__homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` and did not contain: ```text homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` ## Why this appears to happen There appear to be two separate naming layers involved. The Home Assistant LLM platform defines the tool with the integration/domain prefix: ```text homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` The Assist API subsequently applies its own API namespace to tools, resulting in: ```text assist__homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` The built-in dynamic prompt, however, still contains the original tool name. This means the final LLM context can effectively contain: ```text Instruction: You MUST call homeassistant__GetLiveContext. Available tool: assist__homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` The `assist__` namespace may be completely intentional and useful. I am not suggesting that the namespace itself is incorrect. The problem is that the natural-language instructions and the actual tool registry can disagree about the canonical tool name. ## Impact This creates an unnecessary source of ambiguity and can cause failed tool calls even though the correct tool is available and functioning. It can also cause the LLM to spend additional reasoning/context processing trying to reconcile conflicting information, retrying failed tool calls, or explaining why a tool cannot be found. More generally, an internally generated instruction that contradicts the actual tool registry reduces the reliability and predictability of the Assist tool-calling system. ## Expected behavior Any tool name referenced in instructions supplied to an LLM should correspond to the canonical name actually exposed to that LLM. More generally, internally generated LLM instructions should not contain implementation-specific tool names that can become stale when the framework subsequently namespaces or transforms those tools. If the framework needs to instruct the model to use a tool, the tool name used in that instruction should ideally be derived from the same canonical tool definition/registry that is ultimately exposed to the model. ## Broader concern: internally generated hidden instructions This problem also highlights a broader architectural concern with the current Assist LLM implementation. Home Assistant injects internally generated instructions into the LLM context that are not visible in the administrator's configured system prompt. These instructions can materially affect the behavior of the LLM, yet the administrator has no supported way to inspect, modify, or disable them. This becomes particularly problematic when those instructions contain implementation-specific information, or when they contain behavioral instructions that may overlap with or conflict with the administrator's own system prompt. For example, internally generated instructions that tell the model how it should behave, how it should use Home Assistant tools, or that explicitly assert that particular tools exist are behavioral instructions rather than merely implementation metadata. I believe these internal instructions should either: 1. be exposed to the administrator so they can be inspected and modified; or 2. be reduced to the minimum instructions required for the Assist framework to function. In particular, tool metadata and tool names should ideally have a single canonical source of truth rather than being duplicated in independently maintained natural-language instructions. This would prevent exactly the type of inconsistency described in this report. There is already a separate feature discussion concerning administrator control over the hidden Assist system prompt: https://github.com/orgs/home-assistant/discussions/2322 I consider that discussion related but distinct from this bug. The feature request concerns administrator control over internally generated prompts; this report concerns a concrete functional inconsistency between an internally generated instruction and the actual tool registry. ## Relevant source The built-in Home Assistant LLM implementation is located at: `homeassistant/components/homeassistant/llm.py` It defines both the `GetLiveContext` tool and the dynamic instructions that tell the LLM how to use it. The Assist LLM framework subsequently applies API-level namespacing to the tools. The resulting tool name therefore differs from the name embedded in the original prompt. ## Environment * Home Assistant Core: 2026.9.1 * Home Assistant OS: 18.2 * Conversation agent: local Ollama * Installation: Home Assistant OS VM ## Summary The recent tool-prefix changes themselves may be correct. The bug is that the final tool name exposed to the LLM and the tool name referenced by Home Assistant's own generated instructions are not necessarily the same. In this case: ```text Built-in instruction: homeassistant__GetLiveContext Actual registered tool: assist__homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` One fails with `Tool not found`; the other works. The generated instructions and the final tool registry should remain consistent. --- [chat-example-1.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32137662/chat-example-1.txt) [chat-example-2.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32137663/chat-example-2.txt) ### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue? core-2026.9.1 ### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core? iCloud device_tracker location frozen after startup (battery still updates) — pyicloud ≥2.3.0 no longer locates implicitly

### The problem

The iCloud integration's `device_tracker` entities stop receiving fresh GPS locations after Home Assistant starts: the coordinates (and `gps_accuracy`, bit-for-bit identical float) stay frozen for hours or days, while the battery sensors of the same devices update correctly on every poll. In my recorder history a phone's iCloud tracker kept the exact same lat/lon/accuracy for ~10 hours across two real-world trips (a companion-app tracker on the same phone followed the trips correctly), then jumped to the correct position immediately after an HA restart.

Root cause: a behavior change in pyicloud 2.3.0 (PR timlaing/pyicloud#175). Before it, `AppleDevice.status()`/`.location` implicitly called `refresh_client()` which always sent `"shouldLocate": true`, so every `IcloudAccount.update_devices()` poll actively located the devices — that is what the integration has relied on since the pyicloud 1.x days. Since 2.3.0, reads are pure cache reads and the library's background monitor thread refreshes with `locate=False`; the only active locate happens once when the service is constructed (i.e. at HA startup / integration reload). Apple then keeps serving its cached location blob — battery stays fresh (devices push status to Apple on their own), GPS never refreshes. Reported upstream too: timlaing/pyicloud#360.

The bug therefore ships in every HA release since the pyicloud 2.3.0 bump (#161164, HA 2026.2). It is completely silent — no errors, nothing in logs.

Fix: call the (since pyicloud 2.x) public `refresh(locate=True)` in `IcloudAccount.update_devices()` before reading device status. One-line change; I have been running it in production and the very next poll after deploying it un-froze the stale trackers (fresh accuracy values on every subsequent poll, device correctly moved into the right zone). PR incoming.

core-2026.9.1 (present since core-2026.2, the pyicloud 2.3.0 bump)

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2026.1.x

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Apple iCloud

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/icloud

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Nothing - the failure is silent. Recorder history shows the symptom (battery changes each
30-min poll, GPS bit-for-bit identical):

09:28:07  lat=50.72648 lon=23.25166 gps_accuracy=9.280551647491146 battery=87
08:58:07  lat=50.72648 lon=23.25166 gps_accuracy=9.280551647491146 battery=97

```

### Additional information

Timeline of the regression:
- pyicloud 1.0.0 → 2.2.0: `AppleDevice.status()` / `.location` refreshed with `shouldLocate: true` on every access → each `update_devices()` poll actively located devices.
- pyicloud PR timlaing/pyicloud#175 (released in 2.3.0): removed the implicit refresh from `status()`/`location` and moved refreshing to a background thread that never passes `locate=True`.
- HA #161164 bumped to pyicloud 2.3.0 (core-2026.2) → locations freeze after startup for all users of this integration.

OurGroceries component makes too many concurrent networks requests

### The problem

Hello! I'm the developer of the OurGroceries mobile app. The HA "ourgroceries" component (`core/components/ourgroceries`) makes an unbounded number of concurrent calls to our service when deleting items. The `async_delete_todo_items()` method in `todo.py` does a `asyncio.gather` on every item to be deleted. Recently a user had 550 "done" items on their list and all 550 requests flooded our servers in a 3-second window, causing various problems with our service.

We've made a change (not yet deployed) to queue requests from the same user, and to limit the size of the queue to 15 requests. Beyond that, requests will receive a 429 Too Many Requests reply. I believe the HA code does not handle this reply (i.e., retry the delete), so most of the deletions will be dropped on the floor.

There are at least two options on the HA side:

query:
Blink integration repeatedly downloads duplicate MP4 clips on every coordinator refresh causing excessive bandwidth usage

### The problem

tl;dr: The current Blink integration downloads the same videos over and over again every 5 minutes, wasting massive amounts of bandwidth (nearly 1 TB/month for me and I'm sure Blink/Amazon isn't happy about it either). The culprit is that Home Assistant calls BlinkPy's refresh(force=True) on every scheduled refresh, which BlinkPy propagates as force_cache=True, causing already-cached videos to be downloaded again. There is a separate design question that may need to be addressed in another issue (which is whether the Blink integration should pre-fetch every new video at all when those videos are not stored or exposed for playback by default.)

## Summary

I discovered this after observing approximately **230 GB of downstream traffic from Blink (`rest-u###.immedia-semi.com`) to my Home Assistant host in approximately one week**.

My Blink account contains **14 cameras**, many of them newer 2K models. I am not using Home Assistant to archive Blink video, and I am not invoking `blink.save_video`, `blink.record`, `blink.save_recent_clips`, or other video-related actions. 

Investigation showed that normal five-minute Blink integration polling was downloading full motion-video MP4s. More importantly, I verified that **the same MP4 objects are downloaded repeatedly on successive polling cycles when no newer recording exists**.

This was confirmed both by the extremely high volume of traffic from the Home Assistant host to Blink's servers and by enabling `blinkpy.api` DEBUG logging and observing identical `cv_motion/<media_id>.mp4` URLs being requested repeatedly at five-minute intervals.

For example, multiple relatively inactive cameras were observed downloading a new MP4 after a motion event and then downloading that **exact same MP4 again on subsequent five-minute integration refreshes** when no new motion recording had occurred. Other cameras downloaded the same unchanged MP4 across several consecutive refresh cycles.

## Relevant code path

The behavior appears to result from the interaction between Home Assistant's routine use of `force=True` and BlinkPy's handling of that flag.

### Home Assistant forces every scheduled Blink refresh

`homeassistant/components/blink/coordinator.py` currently uses a 300-second polling interval:

```python
SCAN_INTERVAL = 300
```

and performs each scheduled refresh with:

```python
async def _async_update_data(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return await self.api.refresh(force=True)
```

Thus an ordinary scheduled integration update is not a normal BlinkPy refresh; it is always forced.

### BlinkPy turns `force=True` into `force_cache=True`

BlinkPy's `Blink.refresh()` has separate `force` and `force_cache` arguments:

```python
async def refresh(self, force=False, force_cache=False):
```

but when refreshing each Sync Module it does:

```python
await sync_module.refresh(force_cache=(force or force_cache))
```

Therefore, Home Assistant's routine:

```python
refresh(force=True)
```

ultimately results in:

```python
force_cache=True
```

being propagated into camera updates.

### BlinkPy deliberately preserves the previous video record

When checking for new videos, BlinkPy retains a camera's previous last record if no new motion recording has been found:

```python
# We want to keep the last record when no new motion was detected.
for camera in self.cameras:
    if len(self.last_records[camera]) == 0:
        if camera in last_record:
            self.last_records[camera].append(last_record[camera])
```

This means that after a camera has produced a qualifying clip, that old clip remains available as its `last_record` even when nothing new has happened.

### `force_cache=True` causes the retained MP4 to be downloaded again

In `blinkpy/camera.py`, the MP4 URL is obtained from that retained record.

BlinkPy appears to contain normal logic intended to avoid unnecessary video-cache updates:

```python
update_cached_video = False
if self._cached_video is None or self.motion_detected:
    update_cached_video = True
```

However, the actual download condition is:

```python
if clip_addr is not None and (update_cached_video or force_cache):
    response = await self.get_media(media_type="video")
    if response and response.status == 200:
        self._cached_video = await response.read()
```

Because Home Assistant's normal scheduled refresh ultimately supplies `force_cache=True`, the normal cache/update test is bypassed.

The result appears to be:

```text
camera records video
        |
        v
last_records[camera] contains MP4
        |
        v
MP4 downloaded
        |
        v
no subsequent motion
        |
        v
previous last_record retained
        |
        v
next five-minute HA refresh uses force=True
        |
        v
BlinkPy receives force_cache=True
        |
        v
same MP4 downloaded again
        |
        v
repeat
```

This behavior matches the observed network traffic and BlinkPy HTTP GET logging.

## Impact

There are **288 scheduled Blink refreshes per day** at a five-minute interval.

On my installation, the resulting traffic was approximately:

* **230 GB/week**
* approximately **1 TB/month** at the observed rate

The exact impact will obviously depend on camera count, resolution, clip length, and motion frequency. However, the problematic part is that after a video has been cached, an inactive camera can continue transferring that same multi-megabyte video every five minutes even though nothing has changed.

This also generates unnecessary media requests and unnecessary Blink server egress.

## Expected behavior

Routine Home Assistant polling should not re-download a video that is already cached and has not changed.

At minimum, the purpose of Home Assistant's `force=True` appears to need to be separated from BlinkPy's `force_cache=True` behavior.

If Home Assistant needs to bypass BlinkPy's ordinary API-refresh throttle so that the HA coordinator controls polling, that should not also require bypassing the media cache and downloading unchanged MP4 files.

The exact implementation is best determined by the maintainers, but an unchanged `clip_addr` / media ID should not result in repeated full-video transfers every five minutes.

## Related but separate design question: should videos be pre-fetched at all?

There is also a broader issue that I do **not** think needs to block resolution of the duplicate-download bug above.

Even if repeated downloads of unchanged clips are fixed, the integration currently appears to automatically download each newly detected Blink MP4 during routine polling.

That means Home Assistant can effectively act as a second consumer of every video generated by a Blink system, even when the user has never asked Home Assistant to retrieve, save, or archive that video.

The Home Assistant Blink camera entity exposes the cached still image but does not expose these automatically cached MP4s as directly playable media. Video-related behavior is instead available through explicit actions such as saving clips.

It therefore seems worth separately considering whether downloading every newly generated video should be the default behavior at all, or whether video retrieval should instead be:

* lazy/on-demand;
* triggered only by explicit video-related actions; or
* separately configurable.

For installations with many cameras, eagerly pre-fetching every Blink video can silently add substantial WAN traffic and Blink server egress even after the duplicate-download bug is fixed.

I am treating these as two distinct questions:

**This issue:** The same unchanged MP4 is demonstrably downloaded repeatedly during five-minute polling. This appears to be an implementation bug.

**Possible separate issue:** Should Home Assistant automatically pre-fetch every new Blink MP4 in the first place?

If maintainers consider the second concern distinct, I can open a separate issue for it.

## Reproduction

1. Configure the standard Home Assistant Blink integration with polling enabled.
2. Use a camera that has recently generated a motion recording.
3. Ensure no newer recording is generated.
4. Observe network requests made by the Home Assistant host during successive five-minute Blink refreshes.
5. The same `cv_motion/<media_id>.mp4` resource is retrieved repeatedly despite no change to the video.

I reproduced this independently on multiple cameras, including relatively inactive cameras where the transition from a newly generated recording to repeated retrieval of the unchanged recording was easy to observe.

query:
Ring reauthentication discards saved push listener credentials

### The problem

The Ring integration stores its Firebase/FCM listener credentials in the config entry under `listen_token`. Completing either the reauthentication flow or the reconfigure flow replaces the complete config-entry data mapping with only `username`, the new Ring API token, and `device_id`.

That silently deletes `listen_token`. On the next setup, the integration must create a new Google push-registration identity instead of checking in with the saved one. This makes a Ring account reauthentication unexpectedly reset a separate, working push identity and can leave the Ding/motion event entities unavailable if fresh GCM registration is rejected.

The problem is deterministic in current code:

1. Let the Ring integration persist listener credentials through its credentials-updated callback.
2. Complete Ring reauthentication or reconfiguration.
3. Inspect the updated config entry: `listen_token` is gone.
4. Reload starts the full FCM registration path instead of reusing the stored listener credentials.

Reauthentication should update only the Ring authentication fields. Reconfiguration may rotate the Ring `device_id`, but the independent FCM credentials can still be checked in and subscribed under the newly authorized Ring device; if check-in fails, the dependency already falls back to full registration.

Using `data_updates=` rather than `data=` in both flows preserves `listen_token` and any future unrelated config-entry fields while still replacing the three intended values.

2026.9.2; current `dev` at `2f79d1f` has the same behavior.

Ring

No diagnostics are attached because the affected config-entry fields contain credentials. The behavior is covered by config-flow regression tests that seed a sanitized `listen_token` value and verify it survives both successful flows.

query:
Live Context reports a light's brightness as 0-255 while the light tool accepts 0-100, so a model doing arithmetic on what it read sends an out-of-range value

### The problem

The live context and the light tool use different units for the same quantity, so a model that reads a light's brightness and computes a new value from it sends a number the tool refuses.

**What the model is shown.** `homeassistant__GetLiveContext` renders each exposed entity's interesting attributes, and `brightness` is one of them. The value is the state attribute exactly as stored, on the 0-255 scale, with no conversion (`homeassistant/components/homeassistant/llm.py` at tag 2026.9.2: the `interesting_attributes` set at lines 81-95, the attribute copy at lines 159-170, which stringifies `Enum`, `Decimal` and `int` values and changes nothing else). Inside core that rendering is read only by `GetLiveContext`'s `async_call` (line 253) and the Assist API's static prompt (line 328).

```yaml
- names: <one exposed light>
  domain: light
  state: 'on'
  attributes:
    brightness: '255'
```

**What the model must then send.** `HassLightSet`'s `brightness` slot is a percentage (`homeassistant/components/light/intent.py`, lines 37-45):

```python
"brightness": intent.IntentSlotInfo(
    service_data_name=ATTR_BRIGHTNESS_PCT,
    description="The brightness percentage of the light between 0 and 100, where 0 is off and 100 is fully lit",
    value_schema=vol.All(vol.Coerce(int), vol.Range(0, 100)),
),
```

A model asked for a relative change reads 255, halves it, and sends 127: correct arithmetic on the number it was shown, and a value `vol.Range(0, 100)` rejects.

**To reproduce:** expose one light at full brightness to a conversation agent that uses the LLM tool API and can call a tool, read the result and answer again. Ask it to make that light half as bright. The model calls `GetLiveContext`, is told `brightness: '255'`, and calls `HassLightSet` with `brightness: 127`. An absolute request ("set it to fifty percent") does not show it, because the model never reads the current value.

**What models actually sent**, over 529 requests per model with Home Assistant's own prompt and tools unchanged, temperature 0: Gemma 4 12B, asked five differently worded times to halve a light at 255, sent `brightness: 127` five out of five. Asked five times to take it down by twenty percent, it sent 191, 235, 180, 178 and 195, all arithmetic on the 0-255 scale, all outside the tool's range. The same model got every thermostat change right (69 and 66 from a target of 68) and five of five fan-speed changes right, because temperature and a fan's `percentage` read the same in the live context and in the tool. It is right whenever the two halves agree on the unit and wrong whenever they do not.

**The value really is refused.** On my instance (2026.9.2), `POST /api/intent/handle` with `{"name": "HassLightSet", "data": {"name": "<one exposed light>", "brightness": 127}}` was refused before any service call; the light did not change (log below). The same call with `brightness: 50` succeeded and the light read back 128. On the model's path, `IntentTool.async_call` (`homeassistant/helpers/llm.py` 255-296) calls `intent.async_handle` with no `try`, and `conversation/chat_log.py` 460-465 returns `{"error": "InvalidSlotInfo", ...}` to the model, so the conversation wastes a turn rather than doing nothing silently. The model measurements above were made against a harness that does not run the intent handlers; the refusal was confirmed separately against the real instance.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.9.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Home Assistant Core Integration (homeassistant), LLM API

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/homeassistant

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.intent] Received invalid slot info for HassLightSet: value must be at most 100 at 'brightness.value'
```

### Additional information

**Two ways to fix it, with what each costs.**

1. Render brightness as a percentage in the live context, so what the model reads is in the same units as what it must send. Cost: it changes what existing prompts show, so anything tuned to the raw 0-255 value could break.
2. Add a percentage field beside the raw one, for example `brightness_pct` alongside `brightness`. Cost: two values for one quantity, and the raw one is of no use to the model, since the only light tool takes a percentage and a person asking how bright a light is cannot use 255 either.

What I would do: ship the second now so nothing breaks, and deprecate the raw rendering with a removal release announced so anyone depending on it has time to move. I have the change with a test ready and will open a PR if that shape is acceptable.

**The general shape** is that the live context renders whatever unit the entity stores while the tools take percentages. Brightness is the case I measured. **A media player looks worse and quieter:** `volume_level` is rendered as the raw 0.0-1.0 float (the copy at llm.py 159-170 leaves a float alone), while `HassSetVolume`'s slot is `vol.All(vol.Coerce(int), vol.Range(min=0, max=100), lambda val: val / 100)` (`media_player/intent.py` 121-128; the relative handler at 411-419). A model that reads `volume_level: 0.5` and halves it sends 0.25, which `vol.Coerce(int)` turns into 0 and the range accepts: muted, not refused. Read in the source, not measured.

**A smaller separate bug** met while confirming the refusal: the REST endpoint answered HTTP 500, because `IntentHandleView.post` (`components/intent/__init__.py` 676-682) catches `IntentHandleError` and `MatchFailedError` but not their sibling `InvalidSlotInfo` (`helpers/intent.py` 152-177). Noted here; happy to file it separately.

Flo: water temperature publishes a constant placeholder (225 °F) on devices that do not measure it

### The problem

On a Flo Smart Water Shutoff with no water-temperature sensor, the Flo API does not omit `tempF` — it returns a constant placeholder. The integration passes it through, so `sensor.*_water_temperature` publishes a fixed **225 °F** indefinitely, carrying `SensorDeviceClass.TEMPERATURE` and `SensorStateClass.MEASUREMENT`. It is recorded, charted, and usable by automations and long-term statistics.

225 °F is above boiling and cannot occur in a supply line at atmospheric pressure.

### Evidence

Recorder data from one valve over nine days:

| entity | rows | distinct values |
|---|---|---|
| `*_water_temperature` | 70 | **2** — `225` (×60), `unavailable` (×10) |
| `*_water_flow` | 87 | 19 |
| `*_water_pressure` | 87 | 18 |

Flow and pressure vary normally across the same window, so the device is online and reporting. It does not measure temperature. The value was `225` while flow was `2.16 gal/min`, so it is not a zero-flow artifact.

### Code path

`homeassistant/components/flo/coordinator.py`:

```python
@property
def temperature(self) -> float:
    """Return the current temperature in degrees F."""
    return self._device_information["telemetry"]["current"]["tempF"]
```

`homeassistant/components/flo/sensor.py`:

```python
@property
def native_value(self) -> float | None:
    """Return the current temperature."""
    if self._device.temperature is None:
        return None
    return round(self._device.temperature, 1)
```

The only guard is for `None`. `FloTemperatureSensor(device, True)` is created for every non-`puck_oem` device whether or not the hardware measures temperature.

### Scope of what I tested

I do not run the core `flo` integration on this device. I reach the same API with my own client, which reads the identical field (`telemetry.current.tempF`). The core code path above is verified by reading it, not by observing core emit 225 on this hardware.

Distinct from #64150, which is a °C→°F conversion bug. There is no conversion here — the API returns Fahrenheit and the sensor declares Fahrenheit.

### Suggested fix

Reject physically impossible values rather than hard-coding one vendor sentinel, so a different placeholder is also caught:

```python
@property
def native_value(self) -> float | None:
    """Return the current temperature."""
    temperature = self._device.temperature
    if temperature is None or temperature >= 212:
        # Some valves have no temperature sensor and report a constant placeholder
        # (225 °F observed) instead of omitting the field. Water cannot reach boiling
        # in a supply line at atmospheric pressure.
        return None
    return round(temperature, 1)
```

`None` makes the entity unavailable instead of publishing a fixed number into history and automations.

2026.7.3

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

flo

### Link to integration documentation

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/flo/

+
+    def __init__(

+    ) -> None:

query:
Hive: setup forwards a filtered platform list but unload unloads all of them

### The problem

`async_setup_entry` forwards only the platforms that have devices:

```python
await hass.config_entries.async_forward_entry_setups(
    entry,
    [ha_type for ha_type, hive_type in PLATFORM_LOOKUP.items() if devices.get(hive_type)],
)
```

but `async_unload_entry` unloads the full constant:

```python
return await hass.config_entries.async_unload_platforms(entry, PLATFORMS)
```

This asymmetry has two independent consequences.

**1. Entity services disappear along with their devices.** `climate.py` and `water_heater.py` register their services *inside* the platform's `async_setup_entry`, after the device guard:

```python
devices = hive.session.deviceList.get("water_heater")
if devices:
    async_add_entities(...)

platform = entity_platform.async_get_current_platform()
platform.async_register_entity_service(SERVICE_BOOST_HOT_WATER, ...)
```

Because the platform is only forwarded when devices exist, an account that returns no water-heater device never registers `hive.boost_hot_water` at all. Automations calling it fail with `Action hive.boost_hot_water not found` and there is no other indication. Service availability should not be coupled to device discovery.

**2. Reload fails outright for any account missing a platform.** On an account with no Hive bulbs, unloading `light` raises `ValueError: Config entry was never loaded!`. The unload fails and the entry lands in `FAILED_UNLOAD`, which HA then refuses to reload (`Entry cannot be reloaded`), leaving the integration dead until a full restart. Reproduced on 2026.9.3 with an account whose setup logged `0 light`.

#176594 makes that second symptom non-fatal on `dev` (warn and return `True`), but it does not address the asymmetry — it converts it into a spurious warning on *every* reload for the common case of a user with no Hive bulbs or smart plugs.

Suggested fix: record the platforms actually forwarded (for example on `entry.runtime_data`) and unload exactly those.

Note that the obvious simplification — forwarding all of `PLATFORMS` unconditionally — is not safe as-is. `light`, `switch`, `sensor`, `climate` and `water_heater` all guard the empty case, but `binary_sensor.py` iterates unguarded and would raise `TypeError` if the key is absent rather than empty:

```python
devices = hive.session.deviceList.get("binary_sensor")
sensors.extend(... for dev in devices ...)   # for dev in None
```

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.9.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Not a regression — long-standing behaviour.

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Hive

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/hive

### Diagnostics information

Hive does not implement diagnostics, so none are available.

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml

```

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
10:19:00 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.hive] Error unloading entry *****@**** for light
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "homeassistant/config_entries.py", line 1046, in async_unload
    result = await component.async_unload_entry(hass, self)
  File "homeassistant/components/light/__init__.py", line 567, in async_unload_entry
    return await hass.data[DATA_COMPONENT].async_unload_entry(entry)
  File "homeassistant/helpers/entity_component.py", line 201, in async_unload_entry
    raise ValueError("Config entry was never loaded!")
ValueError: Config entry was never loaded!

# the entry is now unreloadable:
{"message": "Entry cannot be reloaded"}
```

### Additional information

Possibly the same root cause, both closed without diagnosis:

- #121726 — the Hive water heater keeps only its registry capability attributes (`min_temp`, `max_temp`, `operation_list`) after a reload, losing `supported_features` and `operation_mode`. That is the entity-registry-placeholder signature, i.e. the `water_heater` platform was not set up after the reload.
- #75639 — water heater entity absent entirely on a thermostat-only account.

Core-side context for the unload symptom: #176593 / #176594 (tolerance for unloading a never-loaded entry, merged to `dev` 2026-09-08, not present in any 2026.9.x tag) and #176652 (setup-side root cause, open). This issue is the integration-side asymmetry those leave in place.

Fix swallowed exceptions in lifx_cloud action handlers

The `lifx_cloud` integration catches exceptions in action handlers but only logs them instead of re-raising. This means the user gets no feedback in the UI when an action fails, and automations continue executing as if the action succeeded.

**Affected methods in `scene.py`:**
- `async_activate` (scene.py)

**How to fix:**

Replace the `except` blocks that only log with ones that raise `HomeAssistantError`:

```python
# Before (bad)

    _LOGGER.error("Failed: %s", err)

# After (good)
except SomeError as err:
    raise HomeAssistantError(
        translation_domain=DOMAIN,
        translation_key="failed_to_turn_on",
    ) from err
```

Add the corresponding translation keys to `strings.json`. After fixing, remove the `# pylint: disable-next=home-assistant-action-swallowed-exception` comments.

It happens because Home Assistant uses a User-Agend which is not accepted anymore by Microsoft.

For the original and most recent post on performance for large calendars:
a 7MB file in generally is not large generally, but an ICS file that large is likely going to going to face some performance issues with ical. The original ical design requirements were intended for small local calendars or even personal google calendars, and not necessarily able to handle a complex enterprise like calendar. Just want to set expectations here that other approaches might work better (e.g. caldav or something else that leverages a calendar server for support)

Even for the 1MB calendars this may be possible to make performant but there may be a bug in how ical interprets the office calendar format. Timed Todoist tasks are still exposed by Home Assistant as 24-hour calendar events. A task due at 13:00 is returned by `calendar.get_events` with an end time of 13:00 the following day, so the calendar card displays it across two dates.

Date-only Todoist tasks should remain all-day events. Timed tasks should receive a short default duration instead of spanning 24 hours because the Todoist API provides a due time, not a start/end interval.

This was originally reported by @r7o3gko8 in #92130. The screenshots below are reused from that original report, with credit to the reporter:

query:
Portainer image update entity becomes unknown after container recreate

### The problem

After a Docker container is recreated through Portainer, the Portainer integration's image update entity for that container becomes `unknown`.

Portainer itself still reports the image correctly. Reloading the Portainer integration immediately restores the correct update state.

### Reproduction

1. Have a running container with a working Portainer image update entity.
2. Recreate the container in Portainer.
3. The recreated container receives a new Docker container ID.
4. The corresponding Home Assistant update entity changes to `unknown`.

Example entity attributes after recreate:

```text
auto_update: false
installed_version: sha256:5027ca26d72d
in_progress: false
latest_version: null
title: matterbridge
```

The container health entity remains healthy.

### What happens internally

`PortainerImageWatcher` is instantiated with a 24-hour interval:

```python
watcher = PortainerImageWatcher(client, interval=timedelta(hours=24))
```

The coordinator reads image status from watcher results keyed by the current container ID:

```python
self.watcher.results.get((endpoint.id, container.id))
```

After a recreate, Docker sends a `start` event for the new container ID, but the watcher still only has a result keyed by the previous container ID. Therefore the coordinator gets no image status for the new ID and the update entity becomes `unknown`.

The Docker event listener receives the new container start event, but the current handler returns when the new container ID is not yet present in `_container_ids_by_endpoint`.

### Observed behavior

Before recreate:

```text
container id: 8470ec767273...
image update status: valid
```

After recreate:

```text
container id: cd72f79fd544...
image update status: unknown
latest_version: null
```

Reloading the Portainer integration runs the image watcher again and immediately fixes the state.

### Expected behavior

When a new container ID is detected after a recreate, the image status for that new container should be refreshed immediately instead of remaining unknown until the next 24-hour watcher run or an integration reload.

### Verified local workaround

A local test patch in `_async_handle_docker_event()` triggers an image watcher refresh when a `start` event contains an unknown container ID, followed by a coordinator refresh:

```python
if (
    event.action == "start"
    and actor_id is not None
    and container_name is None
    and self.watcher is not None
):
    await self.watcher._check_all()
    await self.async_request_refresh()
    return
```

After restarting Home Assistant with this patch, recreating the container no longer causes the update entity to become `unknown`.

This patch is only a proof of the fix. `_check_all()` checks all images and is private; ideally the watcher should expose a supported way to refresh only the affected container/image, or the integration should otherwise invalidate/refresh the watcher result for the new container ID.

SleepIQ deleting 2nd bed.

### The problem

### What happened
With two  Sleep Number beds on one SleepIQ account (each bed added at different
times, each with its own sleeper profile), the SleepIQ integration now
creates only ONE bed device. Every setup silently drops the second bed.

DEBUG level log entry:

2026-09-12 20:47:43.201 DEBUG homeassistant.components.sleepiq
Removing duplicate bed 'Person2s Bed' (id=-<redacted>),
keeping 'Person1s Bed' (id=-<redacted>) which has more foundation features

The two beds have completely distinct `bedId`s — they are not duplicates.
Deleting and re-adding the config entry does not help; the dedupe runs on
every setup. Also, both beds are the same model and have the same features.

### Reproduction steps
1. Configure the SleepIQ integration with an account that has access to two
   physical beds that share a sleeper profile (both beds visible in the
   SleepIQ app on the same login) with different sleepers on the beds.
2. Enable debug logging for `homeassistant.components.sleepiq` and reload
   the config entry.
3. Observe `Removing duplicate bed ... keeping ... which has more foundation
   features`. Only one bed's entities are ever created.

### What was expected
Both beds should be created as separate devices, each with its own entities.
### What actually happened
Only the bed with more foundation features (lights, actuators, foot warmers)
survives; the second bed and all its entities never appear.

### Environment
- HAOS, Core 2026.9.2, SleepIQ integration (built-in)
- SleepIQ account: two beds, two sleeper profiles, second bed added later

`_filter_duplicate_beds()` in `homeassistant/components/sleepiq/__init__.py`
groups beds whose sleeper-ID sets **intersect** (`if key & bed_sleeper_ids`)

was intended to collapse the spurious controller devices from

share an overlapping sleeper profile with "duplicate controllers," deleting a
real bed.

Only collapse beds that are true duplicates of the same physical hardware —
e.g. matching `bedId` or `macAddress` (controller identity) — never separate
beds that merely share a sleeper ID. Distinct `bedId`s must both be kept.

Home Assistant OS

SleepIQ

LIFX integration pins lifx-async==6.5.1, which predates the library's IPv6/Thread support

### The problem

`homeassistant/components/lifx/manifest.json` currently pins:

```
"requirements": ["lifx-async==6.5.1"]
```

`lifx-async` added IPv6/Thread device support in v6.6.0 (2026-08-27, commit a56bd2c "feat(network): support IPv6 and Thread devices end to end", and commit 79a5ce0 "feat(network): support IPv6 Thread devices in discovery and connections"). Version 6.5.1, which core currently pins, predates both of those commits.

Effect: a LIFX bulb reachable only via an IPv6 address (for example, one that has been commissioned onto a Thread network via Matter and is now reached through a border router's routed IPv6 address rather than its original IPv4/Wi-Fi address) cannot be added to the migrated lifx-async-based integration. In lifx-async 6.5.1, `UdpTransport.open()` in `lifx/network/transport.py` opens an unconnected socket with a hardcoded `family=socket.AF_INET` regardless of the peer's actual address, so any send to an IPv6 destination fails at the OS socket layer before any LIFX protocol bytes are exchanged.

This is a real regression relative to the integration's previous `aiolifx` backend. That library opens a connected socket per device (`create_datagram_endpoint(remote_addr=...)`), which lets asyncio infer the correct address family from the destination address automatically, with no explicit family handling needed. A device that can be added today by IPv6 address under the current `aiolifx`-based integration will silently fail to add the moment an install picks up the `lifx-async` migration (PR #177944), with no obvious cause visible from the UI — the config flow will just report "cannot connect".

Suggested fix: bump the pin to `lifx-async>=6.6.0` in `homeassistant/components/lifx/manifest.json`, and regenerate `requirements_all.txt` / `requirements_test_all.txt` via `python3 -m script.gen_requirements_all`.

I verified this by:
- Reading the lifx-async 6.5.1 source (the pinned version) and confirming `UdpTransport.__init__`/`.open()` hardcodes `family=socket.AF_INET` on every socket, with no per-peer family selection anywhere in `DeviceConnection`.
- Diffing lifx-async's release history and confirming v6.6.0 added a `family_for()`/`sockaddr_for()` helper that derives the socket family from the bind/peer address, with proper `IPV6_V6ONLY` handling for the IPv6 path.
- Confirming on a real Home Assistant 2026.9.3 instance (still on the pre-migration aiolifx-based integration) that a LIFX bulb reachable only by its Thread-routed IPv6 address adds successfully and polls/controls normally under aiolifx, which will regress once the lifx-async migration reaches that install.

query: Recorder: after a transient database outage, history graphs lose the "state at start of window" until Home Assistant is restarted ### The problem ## The problem When the recorder loses its database connection for more than ~0.3 s while a `state_changed` event is being processed, it recovers correctly and keeps recording — but from that moment until the next Home Assistant restart, **`include_start_time_state` is silently disabled for every history query**. The visible result is that every history/timeline bar starts at the entity's *first state change inside the shown window* instead of at the left edge, and any entity that did not change at all in the window renders as a completely empty row. The recorded data itself is intact; only the synthetic state at the start of the window is missing. This is not limited to a database that goes away for minutes. Any hiccup longer than three retries (`RETRIES = 3`, `QUERY_RETRY_WAIT = 0.1` in `recorder/util.py`) is enough, and neither `db_max_retries` nor `db_retry_wait` covers that code path — they apply to the commit path and to `retryable_database_job` only. In my case a Synology Hyper Backup job stops MariaDB for ~2 minutes every night, after that all my history graphs are broken until I restart HA. ## Cause 1. A `state_changed` event fails with `OperationalError`. `Recorder._process_one_task_or_event_or_recover` logs `Unhandled database error while processing task ...` and falls through to `self._reopen_event_session()`. 2. `_reopen_event_session()` → `_close_event_session()` → `self.states_manager.reset()`, which sets `_oldest_ts = None`. 3. `StatesManager._oldest_ts` is loaded from the database **only** in `Recorder._setup_run()`, which runs when the recorder starts. It is not reloaded on recovery. 4. The next recorded state therefore re-seeds it through `StatesManager.add_pending()`: ```python self._pending[entity_id] = state if self._oldest_ts is None: self._oldest_ts = state.last_updated_ts ``` That seeding is only correct when the `states` table is genuinely empty (fresh database). After `reset()` the table is *not* empty, so `_oldest_ts` ends up being "a few seconds ago" instead of "ten days ago". 5. `recorder/history/__init__.py::get_significant_states_with_session`: ```python if include_start_time_state and not ( oldest_ts := _get_oldest_possible_ts(hass, start_time) ): include_start_time_state = False ``` and `_get_oldest_possible_ts` returns `None` whenever `states_manager.oldest_ts >= start_time`. With `_oldest_ts` now pointing at the moment of recovery, every window reaching back further than that loses its start-time state — for all entities in the query at once. `recorder.disable` does not avoid it either: the 30 s `KeepAliveTask` keeps hitting the dead database and trips the same recovery path. ## Expected behaviour After the recorder recovers from a transient database error, history queries should keep returning the state at the start of the requested window, exactly as they did before the outage. ## To reproduce 1. Run Home Assistant with a MySQL/MariaDB recorder and at least 10 days of history. 2. Open a `history-graph` card with `hours_to_show: 24` containing a slowly-changing entity (e.g. `person.*`, a `binary_sensor`). The bars fill the full window. 3. Stop the database (or block its port) for ~10 seconds while entities are changing state. The log shows `Unhandled database error while processing task `. 4. Start the database again and wait for the recorder to recover. 5. Reload the dashboard. Every bar now starts at that entity's first state change after step 2; entities that have not changed since show an empty row. The History panel shows the same. 6. Restart Home Assistant — the graphs are correct again. ## Possible fix Reload the cached value when the event session is reopened, e.g. in `Recorder._open_event_session()`: ```python def _open_event_session(self) -> None: """Open the event session.""" self.event_session = self.get_session() self.event_session.expire_on_commit = False self.states_manager.load_from_db(self.event_session) ``` (That query can itself fail while the database is still down, so it probably needs to be guarded and retried rather than executed unconditionally.) An alternative that avoids the extra query is to make the invalidation explicit in `StatesManager`: distinguish "the states table is empty" from "the cached value was thrown away", and only let `add_pending()` seed `_oldest_ts` in the first case. `reset()` is documented as "Reset after the database has been reset or changed", but `_close_event_session()` also calls it for ordinary transient failures, where the database has not changed at all. ## Environment - Home Assistant Core 2026.8.2, Home Assistant Container (Docker) - Recorder on MariaDB 10.11.11 (`mysql://…`), `purge_keep_days: 10`, `commit_interval: 3` - Verified by reading the 2026.8.2 sources; behaviour reproduces every night on this install ### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue? core-2026.8.2 ### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core? _No response_ ### What type of installation are you running? Home Assistant Container ### Integration causing the issue recorder ### Link to integration documentation on our website https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/recorder/ ### Diagnostics information _No response_ ### Example YAML snippet ```yaml ``` ### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us? ```txt Trimmed; the host is redacted and the SQLAlchemy/MySQLdb half of the traceback is left out. This is the moment the recovery path is entered — the same burst repeats every night. 2026-08-18 03:06:51.263 ERROR (Recorder) [homeassistant.components.recorder.util] Error executing query: (MySQLdb.OperationalError) (2002, "Can't connect to server on '' (115)") 2026-08-18 03:06:51.364 ERROR (Recorder) [homeassistant.components.recorder.util] Error executing query: (MySQLdb.OperationalError) (2002, "Can't connect to server on '' (115)") 2026-08-18 03:06:51.364 ERROR (Recorder) [homeassistant.components.recorder.core] Unhandled database error while processing task Traceback (most recent call last): File ".../homeassistant/components/recorder/core.py", line 890, in _process_one_task_or_event_or_recover self._process_one_event(task) File ".../homeassistant/components/recorder/core.py", line 1037, in _process_one_event self._process_state_changed_event_into_session(event) File ".../homeassistant/components/recorder/core.py", line 1129, in _process_state_changed_event_into_session elif metadata_id := states_meta_manager.get(entity_id, session, True): File ".../homeassistant/components/recorder/table_managers/states_meta.py", line 59, in get return self.get_many((entity_id,), session, from_recorder)[entity_id] File ".../homeassistant/components/recorder/table_managers/states_meta.py", line 109, in get_many for metadata_id, entity_id in execute_stmt_lambda_element( File ".../homeassistant/components/recorder/util.py", line 167, in execute_stmt_lambda_element executed = session.execute(stmt) [...] MySQLdb.OperationalError: (2002, "Can't connect to server on '' (115)") Note the two `Error executing query` lines 0.1 s apart: that is `RETRIES = 3` / `QUERY_RETRY_WAIT = 0.1` in `recorder/util.py` giving up after ~0.3 s, after which `_process_one_task_or_event_or_recover` calls `_reopen_event_session()` and the cached `_oldest_ts` is lost. ToDo card: _async_write_ha_state unconditionally broadcasts full item list to all subscribers on every state write

### The problem

### Describe the issue you are experiencing

Every call to `_async_write_ha_state()` on a `TodoListEntity` unconditionally 
calls `async_update_listeners()`, which pushes the **complete todo item list** 
to every active WebSocket subscriber — even when only the item count changed,
or when an unrelated entity triggered a state refresh.

With multiple dashboard views or clients subscribed via `todo/item/subscribe`,
this causes a continuous flood of large WebSocket messages. On low-powered or 
slow clients (e.g. embedded wall panels), the 4096-message queue overflows 
within seconds, causing a disconnect → reconnect loop that never recovers.

### Describe the behavior you expected

`async_update_listeners()` should only broadcast when `todo_items` actually changed.
A diff-check (e.g. comparing item UIDs + status) before broadcasting would prevent 
spurious full-list pushes triggered by unrelated state writes.

Proposed minimal fix in `homeassistant/components/todo/__init__.py`:

    @callback
    @override
    def _async_write_ha_state(self) -> None:
        """Notify to-do item subscribers only when items changed."""
        super()._async_write_ha_state()
        new_items = self.todo_items
        if new_items != getattr(self, "_last_broadcast_items", None):
            self._last_broadcast_items = (
                list(new_items) if new_items is not None else None
            )
            self.async_update_listeners()

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Create a `local_todo` entity with a few items
2. Open a dashboard with the built-in Todo card on 2+ clients simultaneously
3. Have any high-frequency sensor (e.g. energy inverter) trigger state updates
4. Observe WebSocket errors: "Client unable to keep up with pending messages. Reached 4096 pending messages"
5. Observe: the "Last message" in the error is always the full todo item list payload


I opened the issue in the frontend-repo, but was closed with the comment to open it here
https://github.com/home-assistant/frontend/issues/53232

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.7.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Local ToDo

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/local_todo/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml

```

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt

```

### Additional information

Affected file: homeassistant/components/todo/__init__.py
Lines: _async_write_ha_state (line ~330) and async_update_listeners (line ~315)

The WebSocket handler `websocket_handle_subscribe_todo_items` registers a 
listener via `entity.async_subscribe_updates()`. Since `_async_write_ha_state` 
always fires `async_update_listeners()`, every state write — including those 
from the scheduler, coordinator, or other integrations — triggers a full list 
broadcast to all subscribers.
hints:
The unconditional broadcast is real, but the reproduction steps do not match how `local_todo` behaves, and the label is probably pointing at the wrong integration.

### The broadcast itself

Confirmed in `todo/__init__.py`:

```python
@callback
@override
def _async_write_ha_state(self) -> None:
    """Notify to-do item subscribers."""
    super()._async_write_ha_state()
    self.async_update_listeners()
```

Every state write pushes the whole item list to every subscriber, with no comparison against what was sent last.

### Why an unrelated sensor cannot cause this on local_todo

`local_todo` sets `_attr_should_poll = False` and only writes state from its own item operations:

```python
_attr_should_poll = False
...
await self.async_update_ha_state(force_refresh=True)   # after create/update/delete/move
```

A high frequency energy sensor updating in the background does not reach that entity, so step 3 of the reproduction cannot be what drives the flood on a pure `local_todo` setup.

### Where the flood actually comes from

4 of the 12 todo platforms are coordinator based: `google_tasks`, `ourgroceries`, `picnic`, `todoist`. `CoordinatorEntity` writes state on every refresh whether or not anything changed:

```python
@callback
def _handle_coordinator_update(self) -> None:
    """Handle updated data from the coordinator."""
    self.async_write_ha_state()
```

For those, every poll cycle pushes the complete list to every open subscriber, forever, even on an unchanged list. That is a much better fit for what you are seeing than a local file backed list, and it is the strongest argument for your proposal.

So this belongs to `todo` rather than `integration: local_todo`, and it would be worth checking which todo integrations you actually have loaded.

### On the proposed fix

The diff check is reasonable, `TodoItem` is a dataclass so `==` compares by value. One caveat on the snippet: `list(new_items)` stores references to the same item objects. If an integration mutates its items in place rather than rebuilding them, the stored "previous" list mutates with them and the comparison silently reports no change, dropping a broadcast that should have happened. `async_update_listeners` already shallow copies for exactly this kind of reason, so the cached copy should do the same.

Also worth noting that `todo_items` would then be read twice per write, once for the comparison and once inside `async_update_listeners`, so it is worth confirming that property is cheap in the coordinator based platforms before landing this.

The main problem here is the high frequency update sensor causing a large number of updates which would fill the queue. The todo issue doesn't seem like it would fill the queue, but the warning may indicate the todo integration was the last integration to send a message.

That said, the todo updates can also be minimized in two ways:
(a) send fewer unnecessary updates. that makes sense to not trigger updates when there are no changes.
(b) make them smaller/incremental e.g. just stream diffs. Not sure it is worth it to make the protocol more complex right now to do this.

MCP Server OAuth metadata does not advertise PKCE S256, preventing ChatGPT connector setup

### The problem

I am trying to connect Home Assistant's native Model Context Protocol Server to ChatGPT using my Home Assistant Cloud / Nabu Casa external URL.

The Home Assistant MCP Server is installed and configured with Assist access.

In ChatGPT, I create a custom MCP connector using:

Server URL: https://<my-nabu-casa-url>/api/mcp
Authentication: OAuth

ChatGPT immediately rejects the connector with:

OAuth authorization server metadata must advertise PKCE support with code_challenge_methods_supported containing S256.

The same Home Assistant MCP endpoint and OAuth setup works successfully with Claude. Claude can connect through Nabu Casa, authorize against Home Assistant, list the Home Assistant MCP tools and retrieve live Home Assistant entity states.

This therefore appears to be specifically related to the OAuth Authorization Server Metadata exposed by Home Assistant.

Home Assistant's /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server metadata does not currently advertise:

"code_challenge_methods_supported": ["S256"]

The MCP authorization specification requires clients capable of PKCE to verify PKCE support through authorization server metadata. When code_challenge_methods_supported is absent, the client must treat PKCE as unsupported and refuse to continue.

This makes the native Home Assistant MCP Server impossible to add to ChatGPT even though the MCP endpoint itself is working.

Steps to reproduce
Enable the native Model Context Protocol Server integration in Home Assistant.
Enable Home Assistant Cloud remote access.
In ChatGPT, enable Developer Mode.
Create a new custom MCP connector.
Use:
URL: https://<nabu-casa-url>/api/mcp
Authentication: OAuth
Attempt to create the connector.

ChatGPT returns:

OAuth authorization server metadata must advertise PKCE support with code_challenge_methods_supported containing S256.

Expected behavior

Home Assistant's OAuth Authorization Server Metadata should advertise its supported PKCE code challenge methods, including S256 if supported, so OAuth 2.1 / MCP clients such as ChatGPT can complete authorization.

For example:

"code_challenge_methods_supported": ["S256"]

Actual behavior

The OAuth metadata does not advertise code_challenge_methods_supported, so ChatGPT refuses to start the OAuth authorization flow.

core-2026.9.1

Home Assistant OS

query:
Fix swallowed exceptions in prosegur action handlers

The `prosegur` integration catches exceptions in action handlers but only logs them instead of re-raising. This means the user gets no feedback in the UI when an action fails, and automations continue executing as if the action succeeded.

**Affected methods in `camera.py`,  `camera.py`:**
- `async_camera_image` (camera.py)
- `async_request_image` (camera.py)

**How to fix:**

Replace the `except` blocks that only log with ones that raise `HomeAssistantError`:

```python
# Before (bad)
except SomeError as err:
    _LOGGER.error("Failed: %s", err)

# After (good)
except SomeError as err:
    raise HomeAssistantError(
        translation_domain=DOMAIN,
        translation_key="failed_to_turn_on",
    ) from err
```

Add the corresponding translation keys to `strings.json`. After fixing, remove the `# pylint: disable-next=home-assistant-action-swallowed-exception` comments.

Cloud remote UI URL not recognised by get_url(require_current_request=True): OAuth discovery for MCP degraded on *.ui.nabu.casa

### The problem

With Home Assistant Cloud remote access **on and working**, Home Assistant does not recognise its own `*.ui.nabu.casa` URL as its external URL. As a result the OAuth discovery documents served over the cloud URL are degraded, and the MCP server cannot be connected from Claude.ai custom connectors (the client falls back to `/authorize` and gets `404: Not Found`).

Unlike the reports in #153820 and #183050, this happens **on the Nabu Casa URL itself**, with no custom domain and no reverse proxy.

**Observed** (requests to `https://<instance>.ui.nabu.casa`, remote access "On", no custom domain, *Trust X-Forwarded-For* off):

- `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` → `404 {"message":"No URL available"}`
- `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` → `200`, relative endpoints (`/auth/authorize`, …), no `issuer`
- `POST /api/mcp` without auth → `401` **without** a `WWW-Authenticate` header

In *Settings → System → Network → Home Assistant URL*, with **Use Home Assistant Cloud** enabled, the Internet URL field is empty (shows only the `http://example.duckdns.org` placeholder) instead of the remote UI URL.

**Workaround that fixes it:** disable *Use Home Assistant Cloud* and enter `https://<instance>.ui.nabu.casa` manually as the Internet URL. Immediately afterwards:

- `oauth-protected-resource` → `200` with `resource` / `authorization_servers` set to the cloud URL
- `oauth-authorization-server` → absolute endpoints and `issuer`
- `POST /api/mcp` → `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://<instance>.ui.nabu.casa/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"`

The Claude.ai connector then connects (own OAuth client, client ID `https://claude.ai`).

Since an explicitly configured `external_url` with the same host matches the request, request host/port matching works; the failure is in obtaining the cloud URL. `_get_cloud_url()` calls `async_remote_ui_url()`, which raises `CloudNotAvailable` when not logged in, when `remote_enabled` is false, or when `prefs.remote_domain` is empty. System information shows `logged_in: true` and `remote_enabled: true` with the remote connection up, which leaves an **empty `remote_domain` preference while remote access is connected** as the likely cause. After a full host/network reboot, Home Assistant's own bootstrap logged the Harmony config entry as still not finished setting up more than a minute after startup began, and the integration's connect attempt performed blocking I/O in the event loop (flagged by Home Assistant's own blocking-call detector) instead of failing/retrying asynchronously.

InfluxDB integration fails entire batch when a string field contains newline characters

### The problem

The Home Assistant InfluxDB integration **fails to write an entire batch** of events when one of the entities contains a string field with an embedded newline character (\n).

I encountered this with an entity provided by the Home Assistant iOS Companion App:

`sensor.iphone_de_ignacio_geocoded_location_2`

Its state is a perfectly valid multi-line Home Assistant state, for example:

```
Avenida de Logroño, 50
28002 Madrid Madrid
España
```

or:
```
Ronda de la Gacela, 14
22003 Madrid Madrid
España
```

When this entity is included in an InfluxDB write batch, the request fails with HTTP 400 and an Influx line protocol parsing error:

`metric parse error: expected field`

The generated line protocol appears to contain the newline from the Home Assistant state inside the string field. The receiving endpoint therefore interprets the newline as the end of the line/point instead of as part of the string value.

This is not specific to this particular iOS sensor. Any Home Assistant entity whose state or exported string attribute contains an embedded newline could potentially trigger the same problem.

More importantly, the failure affects the entire batch, not only the offending entity. A single valid Home Assistant entity containing a multiline string can therefore cause unrelated state changes in the same InfluxDB batch to be lost.

As a workaround, excluding the affected entity from the InfluxDB integration stops the HTTP 400 errors:

```
influxdb:
  exclude:
    entities:
      - sensor.iphone_de_ignacio_geocoded_location_2
```

However, excluding entities should not be necessary simply because their states contain newline characters. Multiline strings are valid Home Assistant state values and may legitimately be produced by many integrations.

I believe the InfluxDB integration should ensure that arbitrary Home Assistant string values are safely serialized before they are sent using the InfluxDB line protocol, or otherwise prevent one malformed point from causing the loss of the complete batch.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.9.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

app-influxdb

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://github.com/hassio-addons/app-influxdb

### Diagnostics information

The issue is reproducible with the Home Assistant InfluxDB integration using the InfluxDB v1 write API.

The InfluxDB connection itself is operational and thousands of other Home Assistant state changes are written successfully.

The failure correlates specifically with batches containing:

`sensor.iphone_de_ignacio_geocoded_location_2`

This entity contains a multiline state such as:

```
Avenida de Logroño, 50
28002 Madrid Madrid
España
```

The receiving endpoint in this setup is Telegraf's `inputs.influxdb_listener`, which accepts the InfluxDB v1 write protocol and forwards the metrics to InfluxDB 2.x.

The data path is:

Home Assistant
→ InfluxDB integration (v1 API)
→ HTTP /write
→ Telegraf `inputs.influxdb_listener`
→ InfluxDB 2.x

Other Home Assistant metrics pass through exactly the same path successfully.

The receiving endpoint returns HTTP 400 only when a generated line contains the multiline string. The error identifies the exact offending measurement and terminates at the first newline in the `state` field.

Excluding only this entity from the Home Assistant InfluxDB integration prevents these parse errors while the rest of the configuration remains unchanged.

This strongly suggests that the issue occurs during serialization of a valid Home Assistant multiline string into InfluxDB line protocol rather than being a connectivity, authentication, database availability, or general Telegraf/InfluxDB problem.

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
The InfluxDB connection itself is configured through the Home Assistant UI.

The only relevant YAML is the temporary workaround used to prevent the problematic entity from being sent:


influxdb:
  exclude:
    entities:
      - sensor.iphone_de_ignacio_geocoded_location_2


Without this exclusion, whenever the entity has a multiline state, for example:


Avenida de Logroño, 50
28002 Madrid Madrid
España


a batch containing that entity may fail with HTTP 400.

With the entity excluded, the parse errors disappear.

The exclusion is only a workaround and is not desirable as a permanent solution because multiline string states are valid in Home Assistant and other integrations/entities could produce similar values.
```

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Yes. Home Assistant reports an HTTP 400 while writing a batch to InfluxDB.

The relevant part of the error is:


Could not write '[...]' to influx due to '400: {"error":"metric parse error: expected field at 13:703: \"sensor.iphone_de_ignacio_geocoded_location_2,domain=sensor,entity_id=iphone_de_ignacio_geocoded_location_2 Administrative\\\\ Area_str=\\\"Madrid\\\",Areas\\\\ Of\\\\ Interest_str=\\\"N/A\\\",Country_str=\\\"España\\\",ISO\\\\ Country\\\\ Code_str=\\\"ES\\\",Inland\\\\ Water_str=\\\"N/A\\\",Locality_str=\\\"Madrid\\\",Location_str=\\\"[41.78969069056739, -3.34284844451246]\\\",Name=50.0,Name_str=\\\"Avenida de Logroño, 50, 50\\\",Ocean_str=\\\"N/A\\\",Postal\\\\ Code=20002.0,Sub\\\\ Administrative\\\\ Area_str=\\\"N/A\\\",Sub\\\\ Locality_str=\\\"Hortaleza\\\",Sub\\\\ Thoroughfare=50.0,Thoroughfare_str=\\\"Avenida de los Andes\\\",Time\\\\ Zone_str=\\\"Europe/Madrid\\\",Zones_str=\\\"[]\\\",friendly_name_str=\\\"iPhone de Papá iPhone de Ignacio Geocoded Location\\\",icon_str=\\\"mdi:map\\\",state=\\\"Avenida de los Andes, 50\\\\\""}'


The original Home Assistant state corresponding to the end of that line is:


Avenida de Logroño, 50
28002 Madrid Madrid
España


I have reproduced the same error with different values of the same entity, for example:


Ronda de la Gacela, 14
22003 Madrid Madrid
España


which produced:


400: {"error":"metric parse error: expected field at 14:731: ... state=\"Ronda de la Gacela, 14\\\""}


and:

28003 Madrid Madrid
España


which produced:


400: {"error":"metric parse error: expected field at 3:706: ... state=\"Calle del Tenedor, 4\\\""}


The important observation is that the parser error consistently occurs exactly where the first newline appears in the entity's `state` string.

Other points in the same batch are valid but the complete batch is rejected. Consequently, unrelated Home Assistant state changes contained in that batch are also not written to InfluxDB.
```

### Additional information

This appears to be a generic data-safety issue rather than an issue specific to the iOS Companion App entity used to reproduce it.

Home Assistant permits entity states and attributes to contain arbitrary strings, including multiline strings. Therefore, other integrations can legitimately produce the same type of value and trigger the same failure.

Looking at the current Home Assistant InfluxDB integration implementation, non-numeric attribute values are converted to strings and added as string fields. The resulting batch is then passed to the InfluxDB client for writing.

The particularly significant consequence is the error handling for an HTTP 400 response. A client-side invalid-input error causes the write operation for that batch to fail. The offending point is not isolated from the other valid points in the batch.

Therefore, a single entity with a multiline string can cause data loss for unrelated entities that happen to be included in the same batch.

This is observable in practice because the Home Assistant log contains a large list of otherwise valid measurements before the final HTTP 400 parse error identifies the multiline entity.

There are at least two aspects that may be worth considering for a fix:

1. Ensure that string states and attributes are serialized in a form that cannot generate invalid InfluxDB line protocol when they contain newline (`\n`), carriage return (`\r`), or CRLF (`\r\n`) characters.

2. Ideally, make batch handling resilient enough that one value that cannot be serialized/written does not cause unrelated valid events in the same batch to be lost.

The first point would address the root cause in this case. The second would provide additional protection against similar serialization/data compatibility issues in the future.

For now I can work around the issue by excluding:

`sensor.iphone_de_ignacio_geocoded_location_2`

but I would like to remove that exclusion once the integration safely supports multiline string values.

I can provide additional logs, test patches, or reproduce the issue with controlled multiline test entities if that would help diagnose or verify a fix.

enphase_envoy: transient uint32-max (2^32 Wh) consumption readings permanently corrupt long-term energy statistics

## The problem

The Envoy consumption CT occasionally returns a transient garbage reading of
~`4294967296` Wh (exactly uint32 max) for daily consumption. The
`sensor.envoy_<serial>_energy_consumption_today` entity (kWh,
`total_increasing`) then reports a state of ~`4,294,629 kWh` for one update
cycle before returning to normal (~hundreds of kWh).

Because the statistic is `total_increasing`, the recorder treats the spike
as real consumption and bakes ~4.29 million kWh into the statistic's
cumulative `sum` **permanently**. When the counter drops back, HA treats it
as a normal counter reset, so the spike is never reversed. Each occurrence
adds another ~4.29e6 kWh step. The Energy dashboard and any consumer of the
consumption statistic are unusable afterwards without manual DB surgery.

## Evidence (from my recorder DB, HA 2026.7.2)

Victron Remote Monitoring: "Today remaining" forecast uses UTC day boundary instead of Home Assistant timezone

### The problem

The "Energy consumption estimate – Today remaining" sensor provided by the
Victron Remote Monitoring integration appears to use UTC midnight as the
boundary between days instead of the timezone configured in Home Assistant.

My Home Assistant timezone is `Europe/Berlin`.

During daylight saving time (CEST, UTC+2), the sensor changes to the next day's
forecast at approximately 02:00 local time instead of 00:00 local time.

This can clearly be seen in the sensor history:

- Shortly before 02:00 local time, the "Today remaining" value approaches 0.
- At approximately 02:00 local time, the value suddenly jumps to the forecast
  for the new day.
- 02:00 CEST corresponds exactly to 00:00 UTC.

I would expect a sensor called "Today remaining" to use the Home Assistant
configured timezone, so that the day changes at 00:00 local time.

### Expected behavior

With Home Assistant configured to:

`Europe/Berlin`

the daily forecast should change at:

`00:00 Europe/Berlin`

instead of:

`00:00 UTC`

This would currently mean:

- 00:00 local time during CEST (UTC+2), not 02:00
- 00:00 local time during CET (UTC+1), not 01:00

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.9.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Unknown

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Victron Remote Monitoring

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/victron_remote_monitoring/

### Diagnostics information

Can be provided if required.

```yaml
No related errors are logged. The integration itself operates normally;

of the daily forecast aggregation.
```

A possible solution may be to make the forecast aggregations use Home
Assistant's configured timezone when calculating local day boundaries.

The same underlying calculation may potentially also affect other day-based
forecast sensors, although I have specifically observed the issue with
"Energy consumption estimate – Today remaining".

with how the forecast aggregation determines the current day.

zha:

Insecure rejoins (the trust center policy config described above) are as the name describes: very insecure. They basically let anybody walk up to your home, say "I'm insecurely rejoining the network, let me in" and then have the coordinator happily send over the network key. It's as if you permanent disable security for your Zigbee network.

This very much sounds like a firmware problem with the device. @1775939187 is this a known issue? Would you be able to take a look at this?

I understand, but your coordinator needs to be in pair mode still for this to work?

> I understand, but your coordinator needs to be in pair mode still for this to work?

No, that's the whole problem with insecure rejoins. A device can _securely_ rejoin at any point using the network key (i.e. you take the battery out of a sensor and put the battery back in). An insecure rejoin is a device saying "let me in, I also don't know the network key" even when you haven't opened the network for joins. It's a policy that is not enabled by default because it effectively disables security for your whole network.

This is a firmware problem with the device. The device has your network key and should be _securely_ rejoining the network.
