[Bug]: Kimi-K3 MoE padding floor scales with TP - crashes `deep_gemm_mega_moe` at TP>=16 and pins per-GPU weight memory at ~120GB ### Your current environment ### Summary `KimiMoE.__init__` pads `moe_intermediate_size` up to `min_moe_intermediate_per_partition * tp_size`. Because the pad target scales *with* `tp_size`, `padded // tp_size` is identically `min_moe_intermediate_per_partition` — the per-partition size saturates and stops decreasing as GPUs are added. This has two consequences for `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`, both of which only appear at TP >= 16: 1. An unguarded attribute write crashes model init when `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` is used. 2. Per-GPU MoE weight memory is pinned at ~120 GB regardless of TP, so adding nodes does not reduce it. Neither is hardware-specific. The published recipe is TP=8 on 8x GB300, which is exactly the case that skips the padding branch — which is likely why this hasn't surfaced. ### The code — `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py:493-502` ```python self.padded_moe_intermediate_size = moe_intermediate_size min_moe_intermediate_per_partition = getattr( config, "min_moe_intermediate_per_partition", 256 ) if self.tp_size > 1: moe_intermediate_per_partition = moe_intermediate_size // self.tp_size if moe_intermediate_per_partition < min_moe_intermediate_per_partition: self.padded_moe_intermediate_size = ( min_moe_intermediate_per_partition * self.tp_size ) ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug The padded value is what is actually handed to the experts (`model.py:600` for MegaMoE, `model.py:612` for `FusedMoEFactory`), so the memory is genuinely allocated; the pad region is only zeroed afterwards. ### Symptom 1 — AttributeError with `deep_gemm_mega_moe` `model.py:634-647` runs whenever padding engaged: ```python if self.padded_moe_intermediate_size != moe_intermediate_size: w13_weight = getattr(self.experts, "w13_weight", None) if w13_weight is None: w13_weight = getattr(self.experts, "w13_weight_packed", None) ... self.experts.moe_config.intermediate_size_per_partition_unpadded = ( # <-- unguarded moe_intermediate_size // self.tp_size ) ``` With `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, `self.experts` is a `KimiK3MegaMoEExperts`, which extends `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts(nn.Module)` — `moe_config` does not exist anywhere in that class. Every rank dies during `load_model`: ``` File "vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py", line 593, in __init__ self.experts.moe_config.intermediate_size_per_partition_unpadded = ( File "torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1967, in __getattr__ raise AttributeError( AttributeError: 'KimiK3MegaMoEExperts' object has no attribute 'moe_config' ``` (Line 593 is from the `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k3` image; the same statement is at line 645 on `main` as of d31de3c421.) Incidentally, this traceback is itself proof that the padding branch engaged: the statement only executes inside `if self.padded_moe_intermediate_size != moe_intermediate_size`. So in this run `moe_intermediate_size // self.tp_size < 256`, i.e. `self.tp_size > 12`, confirming that `tp_size` is the full 32 here and is not reduced to 1 by expert parallelism. **This reproduces with `--load-format dummy`** — the checkpoint is never read, so no 1.6 TB download is needed to verify it. On 4x8 H100 it fails in about 70 seconds, on all 32 ranks: ``` --load-format dummy --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --enable-expert-parallel \ --tensor-parallel-size 32 --nnodes 4 --node-rank <0..3> --enforce-eager \ --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 1 ``` **This is not a Hopper-only report.** The MegaMoE *kernels* are SM100, but this crash happens in `KimiMoE.__init__` during module construction, before any kernel launches. `use_mega_moe` is set purely by `vllm_config.kernel_config.moe_backend == "deep_gemm_mega_moe"` (`model.py:765`) with no SM or platform check on that path — reaching this traceback on H100 at all demonstrates there is no such gate. The trigger is `3072 // tp_size < 256`, i.e. `tp_size >= 13`, so a 16x B200 DEP deployment at TP=16 (`3072/16 = 192`) should hit the identical crash. I don't have Blackwell hardware to confirm that, so it's worth a check. The weight lookups immediately above use `getattr` with fallbacks precisely because the two expert implementations name things differently, so the direct `moe_config` access looks like an oversight. Note that `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts` stores only `self.intermediate_size` and has no padded/unpadded distinction — DeepSeek-V4 always passes an unpadded size, so Kimi-K3 is the first caller to hand MegaMoE a padded one. Of the allocated memory 77.40 GiB is allocated by PyTorch ``` Note this is a *lower* bound, not a measurement of the total: allocation was still in progress when the GPU filled, so it establishes >77.4 GB/GPU rather than confirming the predicted 120.5 GB. The prediction is falsifiable by anyone running TP=32 on >=128 GB GPUs. On Blackwell this is not a fit problem (120.5 GB fits in 180 GB), but it still means scaling past TP=16 buys no additional weight-memory headroom for KV cache or batch size. This also matches an independent report of ~130 GB/rank persisting across both TP=16 and TP=32 on 16x H200, described there as weights being "replicated rather than sharded" (https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3/discussions/136). DeepGEMM's expert path checks `intermediate_size % 128 != 0` (`deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py:318`), which suggests the real constraint is 128-alignment rather than a magnitude of 256. At TP=32 the natural per-partition size is `3072/32 = 96`, which is not 128-aligned, so *some* padding is needed — but a floor of 128 would give 60.3 GB/GPU instead of 120.5 GB. 2. ### 🐛 Describe the bug Enabling LoRA on a non-gated BF16 MoE model (e.g. NemotronH-style `RELU2_NO_MUL` / squared-ReLU experts) causes EngineCore startup to fail during `profile_run` with: ``` RuntimeError: Check failed: args->intermediate_size * intermediate_size_factor == Mn (1280 vs. 640) : intermediate_size has incorrect shape ``` at FlashInfer `trtllm_fused_moe_kernel_launcher.cu` `check_weights_shape`, reached via: `vllm/.../experts/trtllm_lora_moe.py` → `flashinfer.fused_moe.trtllm_bf16_routed_moe` Logs also show: ``` Using TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts Unquantized MoE LoRA backend (TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts). ``` Base (non-LoRA) serving for the same model works. Gated SILU MoE + LoRA is the intended path for this kernel. ### Expected behavior Non-gated MoE + LoRA should fall back to the Triton MoE-LoRA backend (pre-FlashInfer-LoRA behavior) and reach `Application startup complete`. ### Environment - vLLM ≥ 0.26.0 (after #48632) - Blackwell (SM100+) so `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts._supports_current_device()` is true - BF16 MoE with LoRA enabled - Non-gated activation (e.g. NemotronH) ### Root cause analysis `#48632` added `_trtllm_bf16_lora_supported()` in `oracle/unquantized.py`. The LoRA branch in `select_unquantized_moe_backend()` returns **before** the modular-kernel oracle (`is_supported_config`), so activation / `act_and_mul` checks on `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts` never run. The gate currently checks only: - device - routing method - parallel config - `intermediate_size_per_partition % 128 == 0` It does **not** check: - `moe_config.is_act_and_mul` / `_supports_no_act_and_mul()` (False — gated only) - `_supports_activation()` (SILU only) FlashInfer then uses `intermediate_size_factor = 2` (gated) against non-gated expert weights (`Mn == intermediate_size`), which triggers the assert. ### Suggested fix In `_trtllm_bf16_lora_supported()`, mirror `FusedMoEExperts.is_supported_config` activation checks and fall back to Triton for non-gated / non-SILU activations. ### Related - Introduced by: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48632 - Follow-up optimize (does not fix this): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48759 ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

+def _page_residency(mmap_obj: mmap.mmap, length: int) -> list[bool]:
+    """Return Linux page-residency bits for a writable mmap."""
+    try:
+        libc = ctypes.CDLL(None, use_errno=True)
+        mincore = libc.mincore
+    except AttributeError:
+        pytest.skip("mincore is unavailable")
+
+    page_count = (length + PAGE_SIZE - 1) // PAGE_SIZE
+    mincore.argtypes = [
+        ctypes.c_void_p,
+        ctypes.c_size_t,
+        ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_ubyte),
+    ]
+    mincore.restype = ctypes.c_int
+    vector = (ctypes.c_ubyte * page_count)()
+    address = ctypes.addressof(ctypes.c_ubyte.from_buffer(mmap_obj))
+    result = mincore(ctypes.c_void_p(address), length, vector)
+    if result != 0:
+        raise OSError(ctypes.get_errno())
+    return [bool(value & 1) for value in vector]

# Fix: Accuracy Drops ~20% with --enable-prefix-caching + MTP Speculation

**Issue:** [vllm-project/vllm #43559](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43559)
**Severity:** Critical — silent accuracy degradation
**Labels:** `bug`, `prefix-caching`, `mtp`, `speculation`
**Status:** OPEN (0 comments)

---

## 1. Root Cause Analysis

### 1.1 Symptom

When vLLM's `--enable-prefix-caching` is used together with MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) speculation, accuracy drops by approximately 20%. This is a silent degradation — the model produces outputs, but they are less accurate than without the combination.

### 1.2 Architecture Context

vLLM's prefix caching and MTP speculation interact in the following way:

1. **Prefix Caching**: Caches KV cache entries for common prompt prefixes across requests. When a new request shares a prefix with a cached request, the KV cache is reused instead of recomputed.

2. **MTP Speculation**: Uses a draft model to predict multiple tokens ahead, then verifies them with the target model. This reduces the number of target model forward passes.

The interaction occurs in the KV cache management: MTP speculation generates speculative tokens that may or may not be accepted, and prefix caching may cache KV states that include speculative tokens.

### 1.3 Root Cause

The most likely root cause is one of the following:

**Hypothesis A: Speculative tokens pollute prefix cache**
When MTP generates speculative tokens, the KV cache entries for those tokens may be cached as part of the prefix. If the speculative tokens are later rejected, the cached KV state becomes inconsistent with the actual token sequence.

**Hypothesis B: Prefix cache misses speculative token verification**
When a cached prefix is reused, the MTP speculation engine may not properly account for the fact that the cached KV state was computed with different speculative tokens.

**Hypothesis C: KV cache alignment issue**
MTP speculation may shift token positions in the KV cache, causing misalignment with the prefix cache's position encoding.

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Fix Approach

### 2.1 Disable MTP Speculation for Cached Prefixes (Immediate Fix)

```python
# vllm/spec_decode/mtp_speculator.py

class MTPSpeculator:
    def speculate(
        self,
        sampled_token_ids: torch.Tensor,
        sampling_metadata: SamplingMetadata,
        seq_group_metadata_list: List[SequenceGroupMetadata],
    ) -> Optional[SequenceGroupMetadata]:
        # NEW: Check if any sequence uses prefix-cached KV
        uses_prefix_cache = any(
            seq_meta.seq_data[0].is_prefix_cached
            for seq_meta in seq_group_metadata_list
            if seq_meta.seq_data
        )

        if uses_prefix_cache:
            # Disable MTP speculation for prefix-cached sequences
            # to prevent KV cache inconsistency
            logger.debug(
                "Disabling MTP speculation for prefix-cached sequences "
                "to prevent accuracy degradation"
            )
            return None

        # Existing speculation logic
        return self._speculate_impl(
            sampled_token_ids, sampling_metadata, seq_group_metadata_list
        )
```

### 2.2 Mark Speculative Tokens as Non-Cachable (Proper Fix)

```python
# vllm/core/block_manager.py

class BlockManager:
    def append_slots(
        self,
        seq_group_metadata_list: List[SequenceGroupMetadata],
        num_lookahead_slots: int,
    ) -> List[BlockTable]:
        for seq_group_metadata in seq_group_metadata_list:
            for seq_id, seq_data in seq_group_metadata.seq_data.items():
                # NEW: Mark speculative tokens as non-cachable
                if seq_data.is_speculative:
                    # Don't cache KV entries for speculative tokens
                    seq_data.mark_non_cachable()
                    continue

                # Existing logic
                self._append_slots_impl(seq_group_metadata, num_lookahead_slots)
```

### 2.3 Add KV Cache Consistency Check

```python
# vllm/core/kv_cache_manager.py

class KVCacheManager:
    def compute_kv_cache(
        self,
        seq_group_metadata_list: List[SequenceGroupMetadata],
    ) -> KVCacheInputs:
        for seq_group_metadata in seq_group_metadata_list:
            for seq_id, seq_data in seq_group_metadata.seq_data.items():
                # Check if cached KV matches actual token sequence
                if seq_data.is_prefix_cached:
                    cached_tokens = self._get_cached_tokens(seq_id)
                    actual_tokens = seq_data.get_token_ids()

                    if cached_tokens != actual_tokens[:len(cached_tokens)]:
                        # Cache is stale — invalidate and recompute
                        logger.warning(
                            f"KV cache stale for seq {seq_id}: "
                            f"cached {len(cached_tokens)} tokens don't match "
                            f"actual sequence. Invalidating cache."
                        )
                        self._invalidate_cache(seq_id)
                        seq_data.clear_prefix_cached()

        # Continue with computation
        return self._compute_kv_cache_impl(seq_group_metadata_list)
```

### 2.4 Add Configuration Option

```python
# vllm/config.py

@dataclass
class SpeculativeConfig:
    # ... existing fields

    # NEW: Control MTP interaction with prefix caching
    mtp_prefix_cache_mode: Literal["disable", "warn", "allow"] = "disable"
    """
    How to handle MTP speculation with prefix caching:
    - 'disable': Disable MTP for prefix-cached sequences (default, safest)
    - 'warn': Allow but log warning when both are active
    - 'allow': Allow without restriction (may cause accuracy issues)
    """
```

---

## 3. Testing Strategy

### 3.1 Accuracy Regression Test

```python
# tests/spec_decode/test_mtp_prefix_cache_interaction.py

def test_mtp_prefix_cache_accuracy():
    """Verify MTP + prefix caching doesn't degrade accuracy."""
    prompts = [
        "The capital of France is",
        "Python is a programming language that",
        "The quick brown fox jumps over",
    ]

    # Baseline: no prefix caching, no MTP
    baseline_outputs = run_vllm(
        prompts,
        enable_prefix_caching=False,
        speculative_config=None,
    )

    # Test: prefix caching + MTP
    test_outputs = run_vllm(
        prompts,
        enable_prefix_caching=True,
        speculative_config=MTPSpeculativeConfig(draft_model="meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B"),
    )

    # Compare accuracy (exact match rate)
    exact_matches = sum(
        1 for b, t in zip(baseline_outputs, test_outputs)
        if b.text == t.text
    )
    accuracy = exact_matches / len(prompts)

    # Accuracy should be within 5% of baseline
    assert accuracy >= 0.95, f"Accuracy dropped to {accuracy:.2%}"
```

### 3.2 KV Cache Consistency Test

```python
def test_kv_cache_consistency_with_mtp():
    """Verify KV cache entries are consistent with actual token sequences."""
    engine = LLM(
        model="meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B",
        enable_prefix_caching=True,
        speculative_config=MTPSpeculativeConfig(draft_model="meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B"),
    )

    # Run same prompt twice (second should use prefix cache)
    prompt = "The meaning of life is"
    output1 = engine.generate(prompt)
    output2 = engine.generate(prompt)

    # Outputs should be identical (deterministic with same seed)
    assert output1[0].text == output2[0].text

    # Verify KV cache was used for second request
    cache_stats = engine.get_cache_stats()
    assert cache_stats.prefix_cache_hits >= 1
```

### 3.3 Benchmark Test

```python
def test_mtp_prefix_cache_no_accuracy_regression():
    """Run MMLU benchmark with MTP + prefix caching."""
    # Load MMLU subset
    prompts = load_mmlu_subset(num_samples=100)

    # Run with MTP + prefix caching
    outputs = run_vllm(
        prompts,
        enable_prefix_caching=True,
        speculative_config=MTPSpeculativeConfig(draft_model="meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B"),
    )

    # Calculate accuracy
    accuracy = calculate_mmlu_accuracy(outputs)

    # Should be within 5% of baseline (no MTP, no prefix caching)
    baseline_accuracy = 0.70  # Expected baseline for Llama-3.1-8B
    assert accuracy >= baseline_accuracy * 0.95, f"Accuracy {accuracy:.2%} < {baseline_accuracy * 0.95:.2%}"
```

---

## 4. Impact Assessment

### 4.1 User Impact
- **Severity:** Critical — silent accuracy degradation affects all users
- **Scope:** Users running MTP speculation with prefix caching enabled
- **Benefit:** Restores accuracy to baseline levels

### 4.2 Code Risk
- **Risk:** Medium — changes to core KV cache and speculation logic
- **Backward Compatibility:** Full — new config option defaults to safe behavior
- **Performance:** Slight decrease for prefix-cached sequences (no MTP), but accuracy restored

### 4.3 Security
- No security implications

### 4.4 Files Modified
- `vllm/spec_decode/mtp_speculator.py` — add prefix cache check
- `vllm/core/block_manager.py` — mark speculative tokens as non-cachable
- `vllm/core/kv_cache_manager.py` — add consistency check
- `vllm/config.py` — add mtp_prefix_cache_mode config
- `tests/spec_decode/test_mtp_prefix_cache_interaction.py` (new)

---

## 5. Alternative Approaches Considered

1. **Disable prefix caching when MTP is active** — Rejected: too aggressive, loses caching benefit
2. **Disable MTP when prefix caching is active** — **Selected** (default) — conservative, preserves accuracy
3. **Fix KV cache to handle speculative tokens** — Future work — more complex but enables both features

3-way comparison, greedy (temp 0, fixed seed), batch-1 serial so batching can't introduce nondeterminism: `mamba_cache_mode=none` (ground truth — recurrent state isn't cached, bug inert) vs `align` stock vs `align` patched. Workload: a ~41k-token shared prefix (forces multi-chunk prefill) warm-reused across generative + retrieval queries; outputs compared byte-for-byte.

| Model | `none` vs `align`-stock | `none` vs `align`-patched | garbage / recall |
|---|---|---|---|
| 27B | 6/24 records differ — all benign | 3/24 — all benign | 0 garbage, 100% recall |
| 35B-A3B (MoE) | **0/24 differ** | **0/24 differ** | 0 garbage, 100% recall |

Every cross-config difference was a benign greedy-path token choice (e.g. `marker zephyr:` vs `marker: zephyr:`), semantically identical — no garbage loops, no tool-call leakage, no recall loss, in any config. The patched build tracks the `none`-mode ground truth *slightly closer* than stock on the 27B (3 vs 6 benign diffs), consistent with more-correct cached state, but negligible.

My warm-reuse does exercise the EAGLE-drop-on-Mamba path the PR targets (`drop_eagle_block` fires on every non-verified cache hit), and it still doesn't corrupt — so on these **base** checkpoints the trigger isn't just "align + MTP + prefix-cache." Since these come up together — under a concurrency-8, ~52k-token soak (600+ requests) at `num_speculative_tokens=2` with the patch, on the 27B and the MoE: **no crash, no illegal-memory, no garbage/mixed-language, `Xid 0`**. So I couldn't reproduce the #40756 crash or #35288 concurrency corruption at n=2 here either (consistent with n=4 being the aggravator).

One operational data point worth flagging: **MTP was net-slower on concurrent tool-calling**. Per-position acceptance collapses under concurrency (~99% single-stream → ~65% at concurrency-8 on the 27B, ~87% on the MoE), so end-to-end task latency *rose* with MTP on (27B 9.1s → 9.5s median), and the wasted draft compute pushed the GPU into power-cap throttling. The speculative win only showed up for single-stream long generation, not bursty concurrent tool-calling. We're keeping MTP off for that performance reason, separate from the correctness bugs.

We verified all five open fixes for this issue empirically on GB200 with a real affected model (nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16, TP4, MTP + prefix caching), using deterministic e2e corruption tests that fail on current `main` (both corruption mechanisms reproduce there — details in #48198):

- #47861, #45614, #46281 each **cure the multi-turn lane** (eagle cache-peek overrun) — verified passing with prefix caching genuinely engaged (wave-2 hit ratio ~0.48).
- **None fixes the cold-race lane** (chunk-fragmentation state poisoning): #45614 still corrupts (3 distinct greedy outputs from 16 identical prompts); #47861 / #46281 / the #45477+#47861 combination stop the corruption only because hybrid prefix-cache hits drop to exactly 0 across >150k queries — caching effectively disabled for the pattern, not cured.
- #45477 (the only write-side fix, and the right invariant) no longer applies cleanly to current main; our hand-port produced zero hits on both lanes, so it needs an author rebase before it can be assessed fairly.

Based on this, we opened #48361: a unified fix combining the working ingredients with attribution (supports_eagle_cache_peek + no-peek gates and hit-length min-clamp from #47861/#45614/#46281; end-position chunk alignment + defer semantics from #45477), extending the same invariant to the Mooncake connector lookup, and adding the missing write-side alignment so a mid-block Mamba state can never be hashed as a block-boundary snapshot. Validated red→green on GB200 for both lanes on Nemotron-Super and Qwen3.6-27B-FP8, with cache engagement asserted (liveness probe 4,224 hits — caching stays alive; only sub-2-block prompts under speculation become uncacheable, by design). Trade-offs and coordination notes (incl. #47782) are documented in the PR.

Credit where due: the read-side mechanism analysis in this thread and the fix PRs made the unified patch possible — Co-authored-by trailers included.

**Proposal: fix the state-corruption on the write side (defer block-state finalization until tokens are verified) — with TTFT data showing why the read-side drop, while correct, is expensive for warm agent workloads.**

Context: we maintain a consumer multi-GPU serving stack (noonghunna/club-3090) with several Qwen3-Next-hybrid MTP deployments. We've vendored #48375's delta onto v0.25.1 and validated it on 2× RTX 3090 across both hybrid families (dense 27B and the 35B-A3B MoE this issue reproduced on): boots clean, MTP acceptance intact (accept-len 3.2–3.9), tool-call probes clean post-agent-workload with `prefix_cache_hits_total` asserted. Full matrix: https://github.com/noonghunna/club-3090/issues/710. So: +1 for landing #48375 as the minimal correctness fix.

**The cost we measured, which motivates a follow-up.** #48375 fixes the corruption at *hit* time by dropping the final matched block — which means every warm request on a held prefix re-prefills up to one full mamba page. On hybrids that page is large (1600 tokens on the 27B at 256K ctx, 2096 on the 35B-A3B), so the cost is material and *prefix-depth-insensitive*. A 2×2 on the 27B (TP=2, MTP n=3, 13K held prefix, warm = median of 5 byte-identical replays):

| warm TTFT (13K held prefix) | prefix-ON | prefix-OFF |
|---|---:|---:|
| MTP n=3 | 1,314 ms | 13,285 ms |
| spec-off | 523 ms | 12,878 ms |

Decomposition: MTP's warm penalty is 791 ms, of which pure head-prefill overhead is only ~60 ms (scaled from the 407 ms full-prefill delta) — **~92% of the penalty is the dropped-block re-prefill**. Independently corroborated on another rig (2×3090 NVLink, 26.7K prefix): 1,335 ms vs 709 ms — same number, same mechanism, because the block-drop cost doesn't scale with prefix depth.

**The write-side alternative.** The invariant that actually needs enforcing is: *no cached block state may reflect unverified tokens*. Today the recurrent-state snapshot for a block is taken as tokens are scheduled — including in-flight draft tokens that verification later rejects — which is the root cause here. If instead a block's state is only **finalized into the prefix cache once every token in that block is verified** (provisional until then; finalized or re-taken on the next step after verification lands), then:

- no block can ever hold rejected-draft state → `drop_eagle_block` becomes unnecessary for Mamba,
- cache hits recover full depth → ~92% of MTP's warm-TTFT penalty disappears,
- the ~5% hit-token reduction from the drop also goes away.

From a read of v0.25.1, the natural wiring point looks like the align-mode boundary tracking in the mamba/GDN attention backends (`block_idx_last_scheduled_token` / `block_idx_last_computed_token` metadata) — deferring publication for the final block of a spec-decode step until the verified length covers its boundary. The cost is one deferred-write path (and possibly one extra state buffer per sequence); the decode-path state handling is untouched.

Suggested ordering: #48375 lands first as the safe minimal fix; write-side finalization as the follow-up that recovers the TTFT. Happy to validate any implementation on consumer Ampere (2×3090, both hybrid families) — we have a ready-made probe protocol for this exact interaction.

**One test-design note for whoever writes the regression tests:** on these hybrids, a held prefix shorter than 2× the mamba page gets structurally *zero* cache hits under MTP (hits = (full_blocks − 1) × page), so a short-prompt test passes vacuously. Assert on `prefix_cache_hits_total` growth, not on the flag — we initially false-negatived exactly this way (details in the club-3090#710 thread, credit to @kevinb361 for catching it).

## Confirming this affects a real production serving config — DGX Spark (GB10)

We're running exactly the affected configuration in production and wanted to add a data point.

### Our config (matches the bug report exactly)

- **Model:** Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8-dynamic (hybrid MoE architecture)
- **Hardware:** NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10), SM 12.1, 128 GB unified LPDDR5x
- **MTP:** K=2, enabled via compose
- **Prefix caching:** ON (default)
- **Attention backend:** Triton (FlashInfer + MTP crashes on GQA-16 models, vllm#37754)
- **Engine:** vLLM 0.25.x nightlies (spark-arena community builds for aarch64/GB10)
- **CUDA graphs:** ON (86 captured at startup)

### Performance context (why both features matter)

| Feature | Impact when disabled |
|---|---|
| MTP K=2 | 43 t/s -> 62.6 t/s (+29% with MTP) — disabling costs nearly a third of throughput |
| Prefix caching | Measurable TTFT regression on repeated system prompts (Claude Code sessions share ~25-31K token system prompts) |

We can't afford to permanently disable either feature. Both are load-bearing in our serving config.

### What we haven't done yet

We have NOT independently benchmarked the accuracy delta on our specific workload. The ~20% degradation in the original report was measured with different benchmarks. We plan to run a controlled A/B (MTP-only vs MTP+prefix-cache) on our standard evaluation suite and will report back with numbers.

### Observations from operating this config

We've been running MTP K=2 + prefix caching on this model for ~10 days in production (agentic coding workloads — tool-use-heavy, multi-turn). Some observations that may or may not be related:

- MTP K=3 was independently rejected on this hardware due to streamed tool-call corruption (tokens arriving in wrong order under K=3, clean under K=2). This might be a separate issue, but the failure mode (speculation-induced output corruption) is in the same family.
- Tool-use accuracy on this model is good but we've never had a non-MTP baseline to compare against since MTP was enabled the same day we migrated to this model.

### Request

**Production report: this combination also hard-crashes (CUDA device-side assert → Xid 43) and can leave the engine silently stalled — plus a confirmed mitigation datapoint.**

Setup: vLLM 0.23.0, Qwen3.6-27B (AWQ / compressed-tensors W4A16, hybrid GDN), A100-80G-PCIe, `--enable-prefix-caching` + `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, chunked prefill with `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`. Workload: sustained ~1-2 req/s of small interleaved requests (~4-6k prompt tokens) sharing 3 rotating long system-prompt prefixes, so APC hit rate runs 50-89%.

Over 8 days we hit **8 engine crashes**, all under concurrent load, none at idle:

```
CUDA device-side assert: indexSelectSmallIndex: srcIndex < srcSelectDimSize
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:07): 43, pid=..., name=python3
```

Frequency clearly tracked request concurrency (6 of the 8 landed in a single 3-hour high-traffic window). A controlled 50-minute replay at 2 req/s (3,047 requests) did **not** reproduce it, consistent with a low-probability race - which matches the concurrency-dependent prefill-fragmentation mechanism described in #45477.

One more failure mode worth recording: after a rapid crash/auto-restart sequence under sustained load, one restart served exactly 197 requests and then **stalled silently** - `num_requests_running=0`, hundreds waiting with `reason=capacity`, `kv_cache_usage~0.0`, GPU pinned at 100%, no exception logged, and no recovery until a manual restart. A gdb all-threads dump at that moment shows the `VLLM::EngineCor` thread parked in `PyThread_acquire_lock_timed` (futex wait). Happy to share the full gdb dump, dmesg, and engine logs if useful.

**Mitigation confirmed:** removing the MTP speculative config while keeping `--enable-prefix-caching` - zero crashes since (45-min soak at 2 req/s plus multi-hour production traffic), and for this short-output classification workload (30-130 output tokens) p50 latency under concurrency actually *improved* after dropping MTP (2.68s vs 3.66s).

+1 on prioritizing #48375 / #45477 - as things stand this combination fails in production in three distinct modes: the accuracy drop in this issue, hard device-side asserts, and the silent stall above.

**But MTP + APC on hybrid models is still not production-safe on 0.26:**

1. Within roughly 60 probe requests the engine died with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` and exited. Same failure class as @YashasRattehalli's 8-crashes-in-8-days production report on 0.23. Reproduced under light single-client load, no concurrency.

[Bug]: PRIORITY scheduling can silently skip a running request for a full step when the preemption victim was already deferred earlier in the same schedule() call

### Your current environment

This is a pure Python control-flow bug in `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`'s `Scheduler.schedule()`, in the `SchedulingPolicy.PRIORITY` preemption path. It does not depend on any hardware/kernel/CUDA specifics, so `collect_env.py` isn't meaningful here. Verified against `vllm-project/vllm` main at commit `e6d1310b2ac52e56e266450693af9de12a871a51` (2026-07-19), using the real `Scheduler`, `KVCacheManager`, `BlockPool`, and `Request` classes, no mocking of scheduler logic. The reproduction script below runs standalone (no pytest needed) in an environment with no GPU; the only stubbing involved is for platform-detection plumbing unrelated to the bug (noted inline in the script).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Summary:** under `SchedulingPolicy.PRIORITY`, when the scheduler needs to preempt a request to free KV blocks for the request currently being scheduled, and the chosen preemption victim happens to be a *different* running request that was already visited-and-skipped earlier in the *same* `schedule()` call (e.g. deferred by DP prefill-throttling, or otherwise given 0 new tokens this step), the scheduler's `req_index` bookkeeping is not adjusted for the removed list entry. This causes the very next request in `self.running` to be silently skipped for that entire scheduling step, even though it is `RUNNING`, was not preempted, has a pending token to compute, and there is available token budget and (after the preemption) a free KV block.

**Where**

`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`, inside `Scheduler.schedule()`, the RUNNING-requests preemption loop (currently lines 570–603):

```python
                    # The request cannot be scheduled.
                    # Preempt the lowest-priority request.
                    if self.policy == SchedulingPolicy.PRIORITY:
                        preempted_req = max(
                            self.running,
                            key=lambda r: (r.priority, r.arrival_time),
                        )
                        self.running.remove(preempted_req)
                        if preempted_req in scheduled_running_reqs:
                            preempted_req_id = preempted_req.request_id
                            scheduled_running_reqs.remove(preempted_req)
                            token_budget += num_scheduled_tokens.pop(preempted_req_id)
                            req_to_new_blocks.pop(preempted_req_id)
                            scheduled_spec_decode_tokens.pop(preempted_req_id, None)
                            preempted_encoder_inputs = scheduled_encoder_inputs.pop(
                                preempted_req_id, None
                            )
                            if preempted_encoder_inputs:
                                # Restore encoder compute budget if the preempted
                                # request had encoder inputs scheduled in this step.
                                num_embeds_to_restore = sum(
                                    preempted_req.get_num_encoder_embeds(i)
                                    for i in preempted_encoder_inputs
                                )
                                encoder_compute_budget += num_embeds_to_restore
                            req_index -= 1
                    else:
                        preempted_req = self.running.pop()

                    self._preempt_request(preempted_req, scheduled_timestamp)
                    preempted_reqs.append(preempted_req)
                    if preempted_req == request:
                        # No more request to preempt. Cannot schedule this request.
                        break
```

`preempted_req` is chosen via `max(self.running, key=lambda r: (r.priority, r.arrival_time))` — the globally worst-priority *running* request, regardless of its position in `self.running` (which is plain arrival/insertion order; it is never sorted by priority). `req_index` is only decremented when the victim was already in `scheduled_running_reqs` (i.e. it was fully scheduled earlier this same round). There is no corresponding handling for the case where the victim is at an index `< req_index` but was **not** scheduled this round — i.e. it was already visited earlier in this same `schedule()` call and skipped via one of the `continue` paths (deferred prefill under DP throttling, pipeline-parallel eligibility gating, encoder-budget exhaustion, etc. — any path that leaves a request in `self.running` without adding it to `scheduled_running_reqs`).

When that happens, `self.running.remove(preempted_req)` shifts every later element one slot left, but `req_index` is left unchanged. On the next outer-loop iteration, `self.running[req_index]` now points one position past where it should, so the request that should be there is never visited this step.

For contrast, `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` also has a *different*, already-known issue in the same neighborhood: PR #36390 (open) fixes the case where the preemption cascade fails entirely and `preempted_req == request` (self-preemption), which used to `break` the whole loop. That fix is orthogonal to this bug: in the scenario below the cascade *succeeds* (the retry after preempting the victim gets its blocks), so `new_blocks is not None` and the code path #36390 touches is never reached. This is a distinct bug in the same function.

This is a real, deterministic reproduction against the actual scheduler code (no mocking of `Scheduler`, `KVCacheManager`, `BlockPool`, or `Request`; only unrelated platform/import plumbing is stubbed, commented inline). Save as `repro.py` and run with `python repro.py`:

[Bug]: OffloadingConnector can silently return wrong output at exact chunk boundaries with mamba_cache_mode=all

### Your current environment

Reproduced with:

- vLLM: `0.25.1` nightly, commit `752a3a504`
- Model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2` (hybrid full-attention + Mamba)
- `enable_prefix_caching=True`
- `mamba_cache_mode="all"` (the model's default when prefix caching is enabled)
- `OffloadingConnector`, CPU KV offload enabled
- eager execution, greedy decoding

The relevant condition is still present in v0.26.0 and current `main` (`43c4bdcae9e589fde99984d1d5d03cbdeecf716b` as checked on 2026-08-05), although I have not rerun the GPU reproduction on those revisions yet.

### Describe the bug

`OffloadingConnector` can silently produce different output after a CPU-cache refetch when the prompt length is exactly a multiple of the offloaded Mamba chunk size and `mamba_cache_mode="all"`.

`resolve_mamba_align_size()` currently enables hit-window alignment only for `mamba_cache_mode == "align"`:

```python
if isinstance(kv_spec, MambaSpec) and kv_spec.mamba_cache_mode == "align":
    ...
```

However, `"all"` mode also stores recurrent Mamba states at token/block positions. A prefix lookup is capped at `num_tokens - 1` because the final token must be recomputed for logits. At an exact chunk boundary, without alignment the offload lookup can therefore return `N - 1` tokens while restoring the state stored at boundary `N`. That state already contains token `N`, so recomputing token `N` from it applies the token twice and changes the output without raising an exception.

### Reproduction

1. Create an `LLM` with the configuration above.
2. Use a deterministic token prompt whose length is exactly two offload chunks. In this model/configuration the chunk size was 1408 tokens, so the prompt length was 2816.
3. Generate once with greedy decoding to populate the CPU offload cache.
4. Clear the GPU prefix cache while retaining the connector cache (`reset_connector=False`; on the tested revision the default reset retained it).
5. Generate the identical prompt again.

Observed:

```text
cold:    prompt=2816 cached=0    first tokens=[18631, 43085, 17091, 47695, 1556]
refetch: prompt=2816 cached=2815 first tokens=[18631, 43085, 17091, 47695, 1270]
```

The engine completes normally, but the fifth generated token differs.

With the one-line change below, the refetch is rounded back to a valid recurrent-state boundary (`cached=1408` in this setup) and the generated output is bitwise identical to the cold run:

```diff
- if isinstance(kv_spec, MambaSpec) and kv_spec.mamba_cache_mode == "align":
+ if isinstance(kv_spec, MambaSpec) and kv_spec.mamba_cache_mode in ("align", "all"):
```

### Expected behavior

A CPU-offloaded prefix hit must never resume from a recurrent state that already includes the token being recomputed. Cold execution and CPU-refetch execution should produce identical greedy output.

### Suggested regression test

The existing `test_mamba_align_cpu_offload` already tests exact-boundary and mid-block prompts, but explicitly sets `mamba_cache_mode="align"`. Parameterizing the boundary case with `"all"` should cover this failure.

### Related but separate issue

#46453 tracks per-group prefix-hit divergence for hybrid Mamba models. This report is specifically about offload hit-window alignment in `mamba_cache_mode="all"` at an exact chunk boundary.

[Bug]: fp8/bfloat16 KV cache does a full NVML init+shutdown per attention layer per step

### Your current environment

- vLLM v0.26.0
- PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0
- Python 3.12

### 🐛 Describe the bug

When the KV cache dtype is `fp8` (or `bfloat16`), every KV-cache write calls
`CudaPlatform.has_device_capability()`, which is wrapped in `with_nvml_context` but **not
cached**. Each call therefore performs a complete `pynvml.nvmlInit()` / `nvmlShutdown()`
cycle, measured at **~15.4 ms per call** on my machine.

This runs once per attention layer per forward pass, so the cost scales with layer count and
decode steps. In a py-spy profile of the engine-core process, `nvmlInitWithFlags` +
`nvmlShutdown` accounted for roughly a third of engine-loop samples. GPU utilisation is
visibly non-sustained as a result.

With `--kv-cache-dtype auto` the code path is never reached, so this only affects users who
explicitly enable an fp8 or bfloat16 KV cache.

The issue is much more apparent when Triton attention is used.

## Root cause

`vllm/platforms/cuda.py` defines:

```python
def with_nvml_context(fn):
    @wraps(fn)
    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        pynvml.nvmlInit()
        try:
            return fn(*args, **kwargs)
        finally:
            pynvml.nvmlShutdown()
    return wrapper
```

The two sibling methods are decorated inconsistently:

```python
    @classmethod
    @cache                       # <-- cached
    @with_nvml_context
    def get_device_capability(cls, device_id: int = 0) -> DeviceCapability | None:
        ...

    @classmethod
                                 # <-- no @cache
    @with_nvml_context
    def has_device_capability(cls, capability, device_id: int = 0) -> bool:
        try:
            return super().has_device_capability(capability, device_id)
        except RuntimeError:
            return False
```

`has_device_capability`'s body only delegates to `get_device_capability`, which is **already
cached and already carries its own NVML context**. So the NVML wrapper on
`has_device_capability` does no useful work — it just pays a full init/shutdown on every
call, and without `@cache` that is every single call for the life of the process.

## Why fp8/bfloat16 specifically

`vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_reshape_and_cache_flash.py`:

```python
def _is_supported_kv_cache_dtype(kv_cache_dtype: str) -> bool:
    if not (kv_cache_dtype in _NATIVE_KV_CACHE_DTYPES
            or is_quantized_kv_cache(kv_cache_dtype)):
        return False
    if kv_cache_dtype.startswith("fp8"):
        return current_platform.has_device_capability(89) or current_platform.is_xpu()
    if kv_cache_dtype == "bfloat16":
        return current_platform.has_device_capability(80) or current_platform.is_xpu()
    return True        # <-- "auto" returns here, never touching NVML
```

[Bug]: get_open_port() hangs forever when VLLM_PORT falls inside the data parallel reserved port range

### Your current environment

Reproduced against current main (96fa3f4) and against the released `vllm/vllm-openai:0.26.0` image, where the loop is byte-identical. The affected code is pure stdlib socket handling.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Setting `VLLM_PORT` to a value inside the data parallel reserved window makes `vllm serve --data-parallel-size N` hang at startup forever, with no log output and no error.

`get_open_port()` in `vllm/utils/network_utils.py:159-165`:

```python
if "VLLM_DP_MASTER_PORT" in os.environ:
    dp_master_port = envs.VLLM_DP_MASTER_PORT
    reserved_port_range = range(dp_master_port, dp_master_port + 10)
    while True:
        candidate_port = _get_open_port()
        if candidate_port not in reserved_port_range:
            return candidate_port
```

`_get_open_port()` is called with no arguments, so when `VLLM_PORT` is set it is deterministic: it binds that exact port, releases it, and returns the same number every call. If that number falls inside `reserved_port_range` the loop rejects it and asks for it again, forever.

Repro:

```
VLLM_PORT=29500 VLLM_DP_MASTER_PORT=29500 vllm serve <model> --data-parallel-size 2
```

Isolating the function itself, with a counter added to bound the loop:

```
VLLM_PORT=29500, VLLM_DP_MASTER_PORT=29500  -> spun 200000 times, always port 29500
VLLM_PORT=29400, VLLM_DP_MASTER_PORT=29500  -> returns 29400
VLLM_PORT unset,  VLLM_DP_MASTER_PORT=29500  -> returns an ephemeral port
```

The ephemeral path is fine because the OS hands out a different port each call. Only the `VLLM_PORT` path is deterministic, and only then does the loop fail to make progress.

Confirmed live in the 0.26.0 container: three colliding configurations each wedged past 120 seconds with no output, and the decisive control is the same port with the DP guard off, which returns in 3.1 seconds. Same container, same port, only the reserved-window loop in between.

This is the same failure #24602 reported. That issue was closed as fixed by #36191, but #36191's change to this file starts below this function: it fixed `get_open_ports_list` and added `start_port` / `max_attempts` to `_get_open_port`, and this call site was never updated to use them. The machinery for the fix is already in the file, one function away.

I have a PR up that routes this loop through the same `start_port` / `max_attempts` pattern `get_open_ports_list` uses, so it advances past the reserved window instead of spinning, and raises the existing `RuntimeError` if no port is available.

I went through the current state of this issue to find what's actually
> still unfixed on `main`:
>
> - The DP coordinator race was fixed by #37452 (merged).
> - The engine/API-server ZMQ handshake addresses now use late binding
>   (port 0 + `LAST_ENDPOINT`, children report bound addresses back), which
>   is why #35977 and #39496 kept hitting merge conflicts.
> - The `shm_broadcast.py` XPUB race has a focused open fix in #44495
>   (@RTCartist) — not duplicating that.
> - What still races on `main` is `_data_parallel_master_port_list`:
>   `get_open_ports_list()` probes and closes sockets at config creation,
>   and the port is only bound minutes later by torch's TCPStore in the
>   global-rank-0 worker (`init_distributed_environment`,
>   `parallel_state.py`). That's the exact field visible in the handshake
>   log in the issue description.
>
> I'm planning a scoped PR for that last slice: generalize the existing
> `_pick_stateless_dp_port` coord-store pattern (master binds port 0,
> holds the socket, publishes via TCPStore; `create_tcp_store(
> master_listen_fd=...)` hands the held socket to the consumer), create the
> coordination store for all coordinated-DP launches instead of only
> elastic-EP, and ship `_coord_store_port` through the existing handshake
> field whitelist. Fallback behavior without a coord store is unchanged.
> Shout if someone is already on this or if maintainers prefer a different
> shape.

[Bug]: Inkling: trailing <|end_message|> leaks into content on plain-text turns when tools are enabled (every post-tool-result synthesis turn)

### Your current environment

vLLM nightly `0.26.1rc1.dev428+g46e6a83ce`, serving `thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4` (TP2) with:

```
--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser inkling --reasoning-parser inkling
```

Reproduced both with and without the pending Inkling parser PRs #50528 and #49876 applied. Parser-level bug — no GPU needed to reproduce (script below).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

When a request **offers tools** and the model replies with **plain text** (no thinking block, no tool call), the response `content` ends with a literal `<|end_message|>`:

```
"content": "Greg Stenzel is a longtime client based in Bozeman.<|end_message|>"
```

This is the shape of **every synthesis turn after a `role: tool` result** in an agent loop (model answers from the tool output, no new tool call), so agent frameworks hit it on essentially every tool round. Both streaming and non-streaming are affected. Related to #49865 / #49876, but distinct: #49876's plain-text mode only engages when the request has **no tools** (`prompt_has_tools` is false), so tools-enabled plain-text turns still leak.

**Root cause** (two cooperating spots in the delegating reasoning+tool pipeline):

1. `StreamingParserEngine._on_terminal` (skip_tool_parsing branch): the reasoning pass deliberately passes block-end terminals (`<|end_message|>`, `<|content_model_end_sampling|>`) through as content *so a downstream tool pass can consume them* — the tool parser needs them to close `<|content_invoke_tool_json|>` blocks. But on a turn with no tool block, the streaming tool phase never engages (`DelegatingParser.parse_delta` only routes to the tool parser after reasoning-end is confirmed / a tool block starts), so the preserved marker goes straight to the client.

2. `DelegatingParser._extract_tool_calls` (non-streaming, auto tool choice): when the tool pass finds no tool calls, the no-tools-called branch returns the **pre-tool-pass** content — discarding `tool_call_info.content`, in which the engine-based tool parser had already consumed the stray marker:

```python
else:
    # No tool calls.
    ...
    return None, content   # <- pre-tool-pass content, still carries <|end_message|>
```

### Repro (no GPU)

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
from vllm.parser.parser_manager import ParserManager

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small", trust_remote_code=True)
tools = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_info", "parameters":
          {"type": "object", "properties": {"q": {"type": "string"}}}}}]
req = ChatCompletionRequest(model="m", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], tools=tools)
cls = ParserManager.get_parser("inkling", "inkling", enable_auto_tools=True)

raw = "<|content_text|>The lookup returned three results.<|end_message|>"

# Non-streaming
p = cls(tok)
_, content = p.extract_reasoning(raw, req)
_, content = p._extract_tool_calls(content, req, enable_auto_tools=True)
print("non-streaming:", repr(content))

# Streaming (prompt ends with the model-role marker, reasoning closed in prompt)
p = cls(tok)
prompt_ids = tok.encode("<|end_message|><|message_model|>", add_special_tokens=False)
ids = tok.encode(raw, add_special_tokens=False)
out = ""
for i, t in enumerate(ids):
    dm = p.parse_delta(tok.decode([t]), [t], req, prompt_token_ids=prompt_ids,
                       finished=i == len(ids) - 1)
    if dm and dm.content:
        out += dm.content
print("streaming:   ", repr(out))
```

Both print content ending in `<|end_message|>`. Expected: `'The lookup returned three results.'`

### Fix that worked for me

1. In the `skip_tool_parsing` branch of `_on_terminal`, track whether a tool block was actually handed downstream (set a flag when the transition carries `TOOL_CALL_START`), and only pass block-end terminal text through as content when that flag is set — otherwise consume it. A block-end marker is only meaningful to the tool pass as the closer of an open tool block; when no tool block opened, passing it through can only leak.

2. In `DelegatingParser._extract_tool_calls`, when the tool parser is engine-based and returned no tool calls, keep `tool_call_info.content` (the engine consumed stray structural markers) instead of the pre-tool-pass content.

With both changes, a 6-shape matrix (plain synthesis turn / tool-at-start / content-then-tool / reasoning-then-text / reasoning-then-tool / two tools, each streaming + non-streaming) parses clean: no leaked markers, tool calls still extracted, reasoning still separated. Happy to open a PR if the approach looks right to maintainers.

[Bug]: Inkling tool call leaks as content in multi-turn streaming (turn-initial tool call, tool_calls empty)

### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>vLLM version</summary>

- vLLM `0.26.1rc1.dev30+g5773c4e60` (nightly, 2026-07-28)
- Model: `thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4` (also reproduces conceptually on any Inkling)
- Flags: `--tokenizer-mode inkling --reasoning-parser inkling --tool-call-parser inkling --enable-auto-tool-choice`
- The bug is in the streaming parser path, so it should be hardware-independent.

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Summary:** In **streaming** mode, when an assistant turn in a **multi-turn** conversation begins *directly* with a tool call (no leading text), the Inkling tool-call block leaks into `delta.content` as raw markers and `tool_calls` stays empty:

```
<|content_invoke_tool_json|>{"name":"search_notes","args":{"query":"..."}}<|end_message|>
```

**Deterministic trigger matrix** (same model, same request otherwise):

| scenario | result |
| --- | --- |
| single-turn, streaming | ✅ tool_calls parsed |
| multi-turn, **non**-streaming | ✅ tool_calls parsed |
| **multi-turn + streaming** | ❌ tool block leaks as content, `tool_calls == []` |

It is **independent of `reasoning_effort`** — reproduces at both `none` and `max`, including when the model emits no reasoning at all. (Possibly related to #49865, but that is non-reasoning-mode `<|end_message|>` leakage; this one specifically drops whole tool calls only in the multi-turn streaming path.)

This matters a lot for agent frameworks (e.g. Open WebUI): they stream and are inherently multi-turn (tool → result → next call), so the model frequently opens a turn with a tool call and the call is silently lost.

#### Minimal reproduction

```python
import json, urllib.request

URL = "http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions"
TOOLS = [{"type": "function", "function": {
    "name": "search_notes", "description": "Search the user's notes.",
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}}}}}]

# multi-turn: prior assistant tool call + tool result, then a follow-up
messages = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "Search my notes for DSpark."},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": None, "tool_calls": [
        {"id": "c1", "type": "function",
         "function": {"name": "search_notes", "arguments": "{\"query\": \"DSpark\"}"}}]},
    {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "c1", "content": "Found 2 docs."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Now search my notes again for MTP."},
]

def run(stream):
    body = {"model": "thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4", "messages": messages,
            "tools": TOOLS, "tool_choice": "auto",
            "temperature": 1.0, "top_p": 1.0, "max_tokens": 500, "stream": stream}
    req = urllib.request.Request(URL, data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    if not stream:
        d = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))
        m = d["choices"][0]["message"]
        print("non-stream: tool_calls=", [t["function"]["name"] for t in (m.get("tool_calls") or [])],
              "content=", repr(m.get("content")))
        return
    content, names = "", []
    for raw in urllib.request.urlopen(req):
        ln = raw.decode("utf-8", "ignore").strip()
        if not ln.startswith("data:"):
            continue
        data = ln[5:].strip()
        if data == "[DONE]":
            break
        delta = json.loads(data)["choices"][0].get("delta", {})
        if delta.get("content"):
            content += delta["content"]
        for tc in (delta.get("tool_calls") or []):
            if (tc.get("function") or {}).get("name"):
                names.append(tc["function"]["name"])
    print("stream:     tool_calls=", names, "content=", repr(content))

run(stream=False)   # -> tool_calls=['search_notes'] content=None      (correct)
run(stream=True)    # -> tool_calls=[]  content='<|content_invoke_tool_json|>{...}<|end_message|>'  (BUG)
```

#### Expected

Streaming multi-turn should parse the tool call identically to non-streaming: `tool_calls=[search_notes]`, no marker text in `content`.

#### Actual

Streaming returns `tool_calls == []` and the raw `<|content_invoke_tool_json|>{...}<|end_message|>` block as `content`.

#### Root-cause notes

The chat-completion server streams via `DelegatingParser.parse_delta` (`vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py`); the tool-call block leaks through as `DeltaMessage.content`. In the failing case the model's turn starts directly with `<|content_invoke_tool_json|>` (the generation prompt already ends with a primed `<|message_model|>`), and the streaming reasoning→tool handoff drops the content-kind marker that should start the tool block. `InklingParser.inkling_config` already carries a comment about this class of problem ("the reasoning pass can hand the tool pass reconstructed text whose token-id slice no longer contains the content-kind marker that starts the tool block") and sets `token_id_terminals={}` to mitigate it, but the mitigation does not cover the turn-initial tool call in multi-turn streaming. The non-streaming single-pass path (`_single_pass_parse`) receives the full text and parses it correctly, which is why only streaming is affected.

Happy to help test a fix.

One correction to the trigger matrix, and it widens the blast radius: the discriminator isn't turn count, it's whether the turn opens with a <|content_thinking|> block.

Any streaming turn without a thinking block leaks the whole markup as content and emits zero tool calls. The single-turn run likely had the model emit reasoning first (renderer defaults reasoning effort high), which is why it read as multi-turn-specific.

Root cause: the stream never leaves the reasoning phase. In StreamingParserEngine._on_terminal, the skip_tool_parsing branch is asymmetric — state == MESSAGE_HEADER emits TEXT_CHUNK only, while the path carrying REASONING_END emits both. Inkling's table has REASONING_END on (REASONING, TOOL_START) but not on (MESSAGE_HEADER, TOOL_START). So a turn opening with reasoning hands off correctly; one opening with a tool or text block doesn't — _reasoning_ended never flips, the transition in DelegatingParser.parse_delta never fires, and the tool engine is never fed anything.

Hitting a tool terminal in MESSAGE_HEADER means reasoning ended with zero length, and the delegating layer needs to be told.

Working on a fix. The change is small, but that branch is shared by every engine-based parser, so I want to establish which of them can reach MESSAGE_HEADER first. Repro is CPU-only, drops in as a regression test.

This is a well-designed system, yet it encounters a rather tricky bug. 
The issue arises when a single request contains two large images: while each individual image is smaller than the configured `encoder_cache` limit, their combined size exceeds it. When the first image reaches the LLM forward pass, the remaining data at the end is less than 768 tokens, necessitating concatenation with the second image to satisfy cache requirements; however, the second image cannot undergo ViT processing due to insufficient `encoder_cache` space. Meanwhile, the first image cannot release its cache because its processing is incomplete, creating a perfect deadlock loop.

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
hints:
We hit the same deadlock on a **non-Mamba** model, so #47771 (`_mamba_block_aligned_split` alignment) would not cover it. The residual that leaves the first item unfinished comes from the EAGLE shift instead.

**Env**: v0.21.0, Gemma-4-26B-A4B (sliding-window attention, no Mamba), draft-model speculative decoding (resolved to `method='mtp'`, so `use_eagle()` is true), `max_soft_tokens=1120` (1,100 embeddings per image), default `max_num_batched_tokens=2048`.

**Symptom**: a request with 2+ distinct images never returns. No exception, no log, GPU idle, `/health` 200. `/metrics` still reports 0 running / 0 waiting because no stats are published while nothing is scheduled, which makes it look like the request never reached the engine. py-spy shows EngineCore spinning at the `time.sleep(0.001)` in `_process_engine_step`.

**Deadlock** (placeholders at offset 10 and 1112, length 1102 each):

1. `can_allocate` fails for item 1 (1100 + 1100 > 2048), so `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` rolls back to `start_pos - (num_computed_tokens + shift_computed_tokens)` = `1112 - 1` = **1111**, one token short of completing item 0, because `shift_computed_tokens = 1` for eagle/mtp.
2. Item 0 is therefore still referenced by the same request and never becomes freeable.
3. Next step, `num_computed_tokens + shift == start_pos`, so the `else` branch sets `num_new_tokens = 0` and the waiting loop breaks. The request can never progress.

**Conditions**. We broke each one independently on hardware:

| condition | broken by | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 × per-item embeddings > `max(max_num_batched_tokens, max tokens per item)` | `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096` | works, up to the 8-image limit |
| chunk ends before the previous item completes (EAGLE shift here, Mamba alignment in the report above) | removing `--speculative-config` | works at 2048 |
| the two placeholders are adjacent | one text token between the images | works at 2048 |

The last row is why some VLMs never hit this: templates that wrap each image (`Picture N: <|vision_start|>…<|vision_end|>`) always leave tokens in between, while Gemma-4 emits `<|image|>` back-to-back. One such model stayed healthy even with the budget exceeded (two 16,384-token images against a 16,384 budget).

Blast radius: while one request is stuck, every later image request to the same model stalls as well, because the stuck one pins the encoder cache. Text-only requests keep working, and it recovers when the stuck client disconnects.

**Repro**: serve any Gemma-4 checkpoint with a draft model and send a chat request whose content is `[text, image_url(A), image_url(B)]` with two different images. It hangs. The same image twice returns, and `[text, image_url(A), text, image_url(B)]` returns.

`encoder_cache_size = max_num_batched_tokens`, `shift_computed_tokens=1 if self.use_eagle else 0` and the zero-collapse are identical from v0.18.0 through main, so upgrading does not help.

The invariant that breaks is in `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs`: the rollback can stop before the end of the last fully schedulable item, so that item stays referenced and can never be freed.

[Bug]: VLLM silently ignores falsey yaml configuration options

### Your current environment

[vllm-env.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30833301/vllm-env.log)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

  --config <file>.yaml silently drops boolean false values, defeating any flag whose real default isn't False

  vLLM version: v0.25.1 (vllm/utils/argparse_utils.py)

  Summary

  When loading engine args from a YAML file via --config, any key with value false is silently omitted from the resulting arg list — instead of being translated into an explicit "off" signal. This is silently wrong for any boolean-valued CLI flag whose actual default is
  not already False (e.g. tri-state fields defaulting to None and resolved later by other logic). The user has no way to know their false was ignored: no warning, no error, config just quietly reverts to whatever the flag's real default resolves to.

  Root cause

  FlexibleArgumentParser's config-file-to-argv conversion (vllm/utils/argparse_utils.py, in the loop that builds processed_args):

```
  for key, value in config.items():
      if isinstance(value, bool):
          if value:
              processed_args.append("--" + key)
          # else: nothing is appended — False is silently dropped
      ...
```

  This assumes every boolean flag's true off-state is "flag absent." That's correct for store_true-style flags defaulting to False, but wrong for flags backed by a tri-state bool | None = None field that gets filled in later by unrelated defaulting logic.

  Confirmed affected flags

  1. --enable-flashinfer-autotune → KernelConfig.enable_flashinfer_autotune: bool = None. Left unset, it's later defaulted by the active --optimization-level preset (vllm/config/vllm.py, OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL_TO_CONFIG) — O0 defaults it to False, but the overall default
  optimization level is O2, which defaults it to True. Result: enable-flashinfer-autotune: false in a --config yaml is completely ignored at O2 (the default), and flashinfer's autotune warmup (kernel_warmup.py → flashinfer_autotune → _dummy_run) still runs. In our case
  this caused a reproducible OOM during warmup across many separate debugging sessions before we traced it back to this.
  2. --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager → SchedulerConfig.disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager: bool | None = None, similarly resolved later by several auto-disable heuristics in VllmConfig (platform support, chunked local attention + eagle, KV connector HMA support, etc.).
  disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager: false in a --config yaml is dropped the same way. In our testing this one happened not to change the resolved value (the heuristics independently resolved to the same default), but it's the identical defect.

  Minimal repro

  # config.yaml
  model: <any model>
  enable-flashinfer-autotune: false

  vllm serve --config config.yaml

  Effective config (from startup log) shows enable_flashinfer_autotune=True, not False.

  Impact

  Silent — no error, no warning. Anyone using --config yaml (rather than raw CLI flags) to explicitly disable a flag whose real default isn't False will have that setting silently ignored, with no indication anything went wrong. We burned a significant amount of debugging

[Bug]: EngineCore dies on first guided-decoding request when dspark speculative decoding is enabled (grammar bitmask width mismatch)

## Summary

With `--speculative-config.method=dspark` enabled on `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, the **first request that uses guided decoding** (`response_format={"type": "json_object"}`, JSON schema, or enforced `tool_choice`) crashes the EngineCore:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (4040) must match the size of tensor b (4041) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

The whole engine dies: every in-flight and subsequent request returns 500 until the engine finishes a multi-minute restart (model reload + warmup + draft-module setup). A single malformed-width bitmask should never be fatal to the engine.

The identical configuration **without** the speculative config serves guided decoding correctly, so the over-wide bitmask is produced only on the speculative-decode scheduler path.

## Environment

- vLLM `0.26.0` (official Docker image `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.26.0`)
- torch `2.11.0+cu130`, CUDA 13.0, FlashInfer `0.6.14`, Triton `3.6.0`
- 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, 96 GB), single node, TP=4
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (vocab_size = 129,280), which ships its DSpark draft module in-checkpoint

## Analysis

`StructuredOutputsWorker.__init__` sizes its GPU bitmask buffer as `(max_num_logits, cdiv(vocab_size, 32))`. For this model `vocab_size = 129,280` → `cdiv = 4040` int32 words.

The scheduler-side numpy `grammar_bitmask` that arrives at `apply_grammar_bitmask` has dim-1 = **4041** words — sized for at least `vocab_size + 1` (`cdiv(129281, 32) = 4041`; a table of vocab + a few added/special tokens, e.g. the tokenizer's `len()` of 129,283, gives the same 4041). The copy in `buffer_utils.async_copy_to_gpu` slices only rows (dim 0); dim 1 must match exactly → `RuntimeError`, worker death, engine death.

Since the non-speculative path produces a correctly sized (or correctly consumed) bitmask for the same model + same `guidance` backend, the +1-word-wide bitmask is produced only on the speculative-decode scheduler path. Likely suspects: the spec-decode path building the grammar bitmask against the llguidance tokenizer table size (base vocab + added tokens) or an EOS/sentinel-augmented vocab, while the worker buffer uses the model config's `vocab_size`.

Two orthogonal problems worth fixing:

1. **Width mismatch (root cause):** the spec-decode structured-output path should derive the bitmask width from the same vocab size the worker uses (model config vocab), or the worker should align/truncate dim 1 to `min(incoming, buffer)` — truncation is lossless when the surplus words only cover token IDs ≥ vocab_size, which real tokens can never take.
2. **Blast radius:** `apply_grammar_bitmask` should validate the incoming bitmask shape and fail the *request*, not the engine. Killing the EngineCore (multi-minute outage, all in-flight requests lost) on a malformed guided request is far too severe.

## Impact

- Any deployment with dspark speculative decoding enabled loses the entire engine on the first structured-output request — from any user, on any endpoint that maps to guided decoding (`response_format`, `json_schema`, forced `tool_choice`).
- Outage is several minutes per occurrence (model reload + warmup + draft graph setup); repeated guided requests cause a crash loop.

`sm120_einsum_fallback.py` (dropped into site-packages) — dequantizes both operands by broadcasting their block scales, runs `torch.einsum`, and handles the weight arriving flattened as `(h*d, r)`:

```python
import torch

def fp8_einsum_torch(eq, apair, bpair, out, recipe=None, **kw):
    a, a_s = apair            # e.g. a (T, h, r) fp8e4m3, a_s (T, h, r/128) f32
    b, b_s = bpair            # e.g. b (h*d, r) fp8e4m3, b_s (h*d/128, r/128) e8m0
    af = a.float()
    asf = a_s.float()
    while asf.dim() < af.dim():
        asf = asf.unsqueeze(-1)
    for d in range(af.dim()):                     # broadcast block scales up
        if asf.shape[d] != af.shape[d] and asf.shape[d] > 1:
            asf = asf.repeat_interleave(-(-af.shape[d] // asf.shape[d]), dim=d)
        if asf.shape[d] > af.shape[d]:
            asf = asf.narrow(d, 0, af.shape[d])
    af = af * asf
    bf = b.float()
    bsf = b_s.float()                              # e8m0 -> f32 is exact
    for d in range(bf.dim()):
        if bsf.shape[d] != bf.shape[d] and bsf.shape[d] > 1:
            bsf = bsf.repeat_interleave(-(-bf.shape[d] // bsf.shape[d]), dim=d)
        if bsf.shape[d] > bf.shape[d]:
            bsf = bsf.narrow(d, 0, bf.shape[d])
    bf = bf * bsf
    n_b_subs = len(eq.split(',')[1].split('->')[0])
    if bf.dim() == 2 and n_b_subs == 3:           # weight arrives (h*d, r); eq wants hdr
        bf = bf.view(out.shape[1], -1, bf.shape[-1])
    out.copy_(torch.einsum(eq, af, bf).to(out.dtype))
    return out
```

query:
[Bug]: Packed IPC weight transfer permanently leaks the producer-side staging buffer

### Your current environment

Reproduced on torch 2.11.0+cu130 / H100 80GB; the mechanism is torch-level and not specific to a vLLM version — current `main` carries the affected code in `vllm/distributed/weight_transfer/packed_tensor.py`.

### Describe the bug

`packed_ipc_producer` calls `reduce_tensor` once per staging buffer and ships the same rebuild args with every chunk; `packed_ipc_consumer` rebuilds a tensor from those args and releases it again on every chunk (it clones the unpacked tensors and drops the view). torch's cross-process IPC refcount pairs **one export with one rebuild-release cycle**: the export sets the shared counter to 1, each consumer-side release decrements it, and `torch.cuda.ipc_collect()` on the producer only reclaims a dropped buffer when the counter is exactly 0.

A multi-chunk transfer therefore drives the counter negative (1 - n_chunks), and the staging buffer becomes permanently unreclaimable once the producer drops it. Every packed weight transfer strands `packed_buffer_size_bytes` on the producer side. RL training loops that sync weights every step leak one buffer per step per producer rank until the colocated inference engine OOMs on wake.

Reading the refcount slot directly (it lives in the shared-memory file named by `ref_counter_handle` inside the rebuild args) during a two-process run shows the trajectory: export -> 1, then 0 / -1 / -2 after the first / second / third consume, and the buffer stays in `memory_allocated` through repeated `ipc_collect` calls.

The release-per-chunk consumer pattern dates back to the introduction of chunked packed transfers (#37476), so this affects every release since.

### Minimal reproduction (single GPU, ~10s, pure torch)

```python
"""Minimal repro: sender-side CUDA IPC storage is permanently stranded when
one reduce_tensor export is consumed (rebuild + release) more than once,
which is exactly what packed weight transfer does (one export, one consume
per chunk). Run: python ipc_leak_repro.py  (single GPU, ~10s)
"""
import multiprocessing as mp

import torch

BUF = 256 * 1024 * 1024


def consumer(q, done, stop):
    torch.cuda.init()
    while (item := q.get()) is not None:
        rebuild, args = item
        t = rebuild(*args)   # open the IPC mapping (like packed_ipc_consumer)
        del t                # release immediately (like clone-and-drop per chunk)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        done.put(1)
    stop.get()


def run(n_consumes):
    from torch.multiprocessing.reductions import reduce_tensor

    ctx = mp.get_context("spawn")
    q, done, stop = ctx.Queue(), ctx.Queue(), ctx.Queue()
    p = ctx.Process(target=consumer, args=(q, done, stop), daemon=True)
    p.start()
    torch.cuda.init()
    base = torch.cuda.memory_allocated()

    buf = torch.empty(BUF, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
    handle = reduce_tensor(buf)          # export once: cross-process refcount = 1
    for _ in range(n_consumes):          # each consume decrements once on release
        q.put(handle)
        done.get()
    del handle, buf                      # sender drops the buffer

    for _ in range(5):                   # "next rollout" = more ipc_collect calls
```

```python
reduce_tensor's args carry (ref_counter_handle, ref_counter_offset): the
handle names a shared-memory file, the offset indexes an int64 slot. Dump
the slot value after export and after each consumer rebuild-release.
"""
import multiprocessing as mp
import os
import struct

import torch


def find_counter(args):
    flat = []

    def walk(x):
        if isinstance(x, (tuple, list)):
            for y in x:
                walk(y)
        else:
            flat.append(x)

    walk(args)
    for i, x in enumerate(flat):
        if isinstance(x, (bytes, str)) and "torch_" in str(x):
            name = x.decode() if isinstance(x, bytes) else x
            # events also live in shm files; the ref counter handle is the one
            # followed by an int offset whose file is int64-slot sized
            nxt = flat[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(flat) else None
            if isinstance(nxt, int):
                path = "/dev/shm/" + name.lstrip("/")
                if os.path.exists(path):
                    yield name, nxt, path


def read_slot(path, offset):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        data = f.read()
    n = len(data) // 8
    vals = struct.unpack(f"<{n}q", data[: n * 8])
    window = {i: v for i, v in enumerate(vals) if v != 0 or i == offset}
    return vals[offset] if offset < n else None, len(data), window


def consumer(q, done, stop):
    torch.cuda.init()
    while True:
        item = q.get()
        if item is None:
            break
        f, a = item
        t = f(*a)
        del t
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        done.put(1)
    stop.get()

    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    freed = base - torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
```

query:
[RFC]: [TieredOffloading][Performance] Tiered Lookup Resolution

### Motivation.

This RFC focuses on FS offloading, but the issue generally applies to all of TieredOffloading.

Tiered lookups happen in 2 phases: 
  Phase1 : Check if the prefix's KV value is available in the tier (os.path.exists() for FS offloading) 
  Phase2: Promote the KV block to CPU (os.read for FS offloading)

KV lookups in tiered offloading are considered a HIT only when the KV's materialize in the CPU tier. As an extreme case example, for some request that has none of its KV blocks are in the CPU, but has all of its KV secondary tiers, this 2 Phase lookup approach results in unnecessary tier -> CPU loads. 

In this scenario, a lookup is inevitably executed on all the prefix keys as the keys enter Phase1 and return a "RETRY" lookup result.
reference : Sliding Window Lookups here https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/a0056e103e214d5b0b73ca9e24003e09f8cbec63/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py#L652
```
                case LookupResult.RETRY:
                    # Block location uncertain — does not count as hit.
                    # Don't break: keep scanning to let manager kick off
                    # async lookups.
                    defer_lookup = True
                    consecutive_hits = 0
```
The scheduler continues scanning more prefix-hashes, triggering a lookup for all the previous (SWA) / next (FA) keys in the prefix.
When the offloading scheduler retries, and if Phase1 is completed, the promotions are triggered immediately here  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0df620d429261fb4e3c1200c6b8414209587a86c/vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/manager.py#L361

```
            result = tier.lookup(key, req_context)
            if result is LookupResult.HIT:
                promoted = self._initiate_promotion(tier, key, req_context)
                self._accumulate_lookup_sync_delay(req_state, lookup_start)
                if (
                    req_state is not None
                    and promoted
                    and req_state.secondary_lookup_start_time is None
                ):
                    req_state.secondary_lookup_start_time = lookup_start
                return LookupResult.MISS if not promoted else LookupResult.RETRY
```

The result in a HIT only when the blocks are in the CPU, which at this point is the entire request. 

This policy is okay of Full-Attention groups. But for Sliding Window attention and Mamba (align mode "all"), we perform tier -> CPU loads for keys that are eventually thrown out. i.e. not used in CPU -> GPU loads.

### Proposed Change.

Policy change - Lightweight resolution of lookups for Tiering / Deferred tier promotions:

The existing approach in the offloading/scheduler.py is correct. We should trigger lookups for keys to determine availability in the secondary tiers. But the promotions to the Primary tier should be deferred. 

The common case is that the tiers are reliable. i.e. when os.path.exists is a hit, then os.read also succeeds. We may relax the condition "The lookup is resolved only when the data is in the CPU tier" to "The lookup is resolved when the tier reliably says the file exists" . This information is sufficient to resolve prefix matches. 
With the prefix-match resolved, we load only what is necessary from the tier. 

In the event tier -> CPU fails, we abandon KV loads and perform prefills on the GPU.
