[Bug]: GatedDeltaNet metadata builder classifies a stateless first chunk as a decode (same root cause as #51483)

## Summary

The shared `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder` classifies a request's first one-token chunk as a decode. Because the decode path reads its linear-attention state slot without zeroing it, and mamba-style state pages are not zeroed on reallocation, such a request would read whatever recurrent and conv state the previous owner of its recycled block left behind. #51483 fixes this for the `KimiK3KDAMetadataBuilder` subclass (Kimi-K3's full-rank-gate KDA path), but the base builder and every other model on it are unaffected by that change, so this is filed separately.

Models on the unmodified base builder, and so in scope: Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, OLMo-hybrid, InternS2-Mobius, Bailing-MoE-v3, and standalone Kimi-Linear (`KimiLinearForCausalLM`, whose `KimiGatedDeltaNetAttention` does not override the backend the way Kimi-K3 does). Their MTP and drafter variants reuse the same base builder.

This is a distinct defect from #49918 / PR #47123; see "Relationship to #49918" below.

## Mechanism

The full write-up for the Kimi case is in #51483; the shared-layer version:

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py:213` calls `split_decodes_and_prefills(m, decode_threshold=1)` with the default `treat_short_extends_as_decodes=True`, so every row with `query_len <= 1` counts as a decode, including a row that has never been forwarded (`num_computed_tokens == 0`).
- `has_initial_state` is computed only when `num_prefills > 0` (`gdn_attn.py:391-392`). An all-one-token batch is all decodes, so `num_prefills == 0` and `has_initial_state` is `None`.
- The decode path then reads the recurrent state slot with no `has_initial_state` gate and no zero-fill. In the OLMo layer that is `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule(initial_state=ssm_state, ssm_state_indices=non_spec_state_indices_tensor, ...)` on the `num_decodes > 0` branch (`olmo_gdn_linear_attn.py`); in the Qwen layer it is `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` / `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode` with `initial_state=ssm_state` on the `num_decodes > 0` branches (`qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py`), and the conv update on the same branch (`causal_conv1d_update`) reads its slot the same way. The prefill path, by contrast, gates on `has_initial_state` and so zeroes a stateless slot.
- Mamba-style state pages are not zeroed on reallocation: the mamba spec is not in the worker-side zero-on-allocation set (`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:86`).

Putting those together: a freshly admitted request whose block was previously owned by another request would read that request's leftover recurrent and conv state instead of a zero state. That is a correctness bug on its own, and it is also a path by which a corrupted (NaN) state block can be inherited by a new request. I have verified the misclassification and the unconditional decode read directly (see below); I have not run an end-to-end generation showing a recycled block still holding a prior request's state, so treat the inheritance step as a consequence of the code path rather than an observed failure.

The trigger is a scheduler step whose batch is entirely one-token rows and includes at least one first chunk. On default flags these models resolve to `mamba_cache_mode="align"` (like Kimi-K3), where a plain one-token prompt admitted alongside decodes is the reachable trigger; the budget-clamped first chunk (`scheduler.py:922`) is additionally gated by `_mamba_block_aligned_split` and reaches one token only when align is off or `long_prefill_token_threshold` / `max_num_batched_tokens` is below the mamba block size. A batch with any longer row is unaffected.

## What I verified

- Ran the real `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build` on `seq_lens=[100, 50, 1]`, `query_lens=[1, 1, 1]`, `is_prefilling=[False, False, True]`: it returns 3 decodes, 0 prefills, `has_initial_state=None`, the same wrong classification the Kimi subclass gave before #51483.
- Confirmed by reading that the OLMo and Qwen GDN decode branches read `ssm_state` unconditionally on the `num_prefills == 0` route, while their prefill paths gate on `has_initial_state`.

## Relationship to #49918 / PR #47123

#49918 (and its fix PR #47123, which touches only `_is_uniform_decode` in `gpu_model_runner.py`) is a different root cause with a similar symptom: a `K+1`-token prompt under speculative decoding is misdispatched to the captured FULL spec-verify cudagraph by the runner's shape-only `_is_uniform_decode`, and the recurrent-state *write* is skipped. There the builder correctly reports `num_prefills > 0`. The defect here is the opposite at the builder level: the builder reports `num_prefills == 0` for a non-spec first chunk, and the decode path performs a stale *read*. #47123 does not touch `split_decodes_and_prefills` or the non-spec classification, so it does not fix this.

## Suggested fix

The same shape as #51483: classify by state rather than query length in the base builder (a first chunk with no computed tokens is a prefill; a resumed one-token chunk stays a decode), masked with the runner's `is_prefilling` flag so the cudagraph capture dummy batch is not promoted, and re-key the base cudagraph staging guard to the condition the dispatcher uses. The staging guard differs from Kimi's, so it needs its own measurement across the affected models. I am happy to open that PR once #51483 settles, or to defer to a maintainer who owns this backend.

## Environment

vLLM current main; observed on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell and RTX 5050 (sm_120), torch 2.13.0+cu130.

## Tool assistance

Claude Code was used for the investigation and for drafting this report. I reviewed every claim, ran the builder as described, and read the cited paths.

### 🐛 Describe the bug `apply_softcap` in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_attention_helpers.py` computes `x * tanh(S / x)` as `x * (exp(S/x) - exp(-S/x)) / (exp(S/x) + exp(-S/x))`. Both exponentials overflow to `inf` when `|S / x| > ~88`, so the ratio is `inf / inf = NaN` and the whole attention row is poisoned. This path runs for models that use attention logit softcapping, for example Gemma-2 with `attn_logit_softcapping = 50`. A pre-softcap score above 4400 overflows. These models have very large attention logits, which is why they use softcapping. The same helper is used by the unified, DiffKV, and INT4 attention kernels. Reproduced on main at commit `c191787a68` with a GTX 1650 Ti and Triton 3.7.1. Reproduction: ```python import torch from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton from vllm.v1.attention.ops.triton_attention_helpers import apply_softcap @triton.jit def _probe(s_ptr, out_ptr, n, cap, BLOCK: tl.constexpr): offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) mask = offs < n s = tl.load(s_ptr + offs, mask=mask, other=0.0) tl.store(out_ptr + offs, apply_softcap(s, cap), mask=mask) cap = 50.0 s = torch.tensor( [1000.0, 3000.0, 5000.0, 10000.0, -10000.0, 4400.0], device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32, ) out = torch.empty_like(s) _probe[(1,)](s, out, s.numel(), cap, BLOCK=16) print("kernel:", out.tolist()) print("tanh :", (cap * torch.tanh(s / cap)).tolist()) ``` Observed: ```text kernel: [50.0, 50.0, nan, nan, nan, inf] tanh : [50.0, 50.0, 50.0, 50.0, -50.0, 50.0] ``` Expected: the softcap returns a finite value, `x * tanh(S / x)`, for every finite score. ```text

### 🐛 Describe the bug

When `max_model_len` is auto-fitted down because the KV cache cannot hold the full context, the V2 GPU model runner keeps using the *original* length in its `ModelState`, while attention metadata builders created afterwards size their buffers from the *reduced* `model_config.max_model_len`. For DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA this makes `_build_c128a_metadata` fail its assertion during CUDA-graph capture, and the engine dies at startup.

It is not deterministic: it only triggers when free memory at startup is slightly too small for the full context. The same configuration started fine on a second attempt (KV cache 12.3 GiB → no reduction).

**Log**

```text
max_model_len: reduced from 1048576 to 980224 to fit in available GPU memory (9.81 GiB KV cache)
...
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", in compile_or_warm_up_model
    cuda_graph_memory_bytes = self.model_runner.capture_model()
  ...
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/default.py", in prepare_attn
    attn_metadata = build_attn_metadata(
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py", in build_attn_metadata
    metadata = attn_metadata_builder.build_for_cudagraph_capture(
  File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v4/sparse_mla.py", in _build_c128a_metadata
    assert active_topk_width >= cm.max_seq_len // self.compress_ratio
AssertionError
```

**Root cause**

1. `ModelState.__init__` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/interface.py`) caches `self.max_model_len = self.model_config.max_model_len` when the model is loaded (`load_model` → `init_model_state`). No method updates it later.
2. After KV sizing, `Worker.update_max_model_len` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`) writes the reduced value into `model_config.max_model_len` and calls `model_runner.update_max_model_len`.
3. `GPUModelRunner.update_max_model_len` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`) only updates `self.max_model_len` and `self.req_states.max_model_len` — **`self.model_state` keeps the original length**.
4. The attention metadata builders are created afterwards. `DeepseekV4SparseMLAMetadataBuilder.__init__` sizes the C128A buffers from the **reduced** `model_config.max_model_len`: `c128a_max_compressed = align_up(cdiv(980224, 128), 128) = 7680`.
5. During CUDA-graph capture, `prepare_attn` in `model_states/default.py` uses `max_seq_len = self.max_model_len` (`for_capture` branch) → the **stale** 1048576 → `max_seq_len // 128 = 8192`.
6. `_build_c128a_metadata` clamps `active_topk_width` to `c128a_max_compressed` (7680) and then asserts it is `>= 8192` → `AssertionError`.

**Upstream check**

On `vllm-project/vllm` `main` (2026-09-15): `ModelState.__init__` sets `self.max_model_len` from `model_config` and never updates it; `prepare_attn` uses it for capture; `GPUModelRunner.update_max_model_len` does not touch `model_state`; `sparse_mla.py` computes `c128a_max_compressed` from `model_config.max_model_len` and has the same assertion. We have not reproduced it on a `main` build ourselves.

**Reproduction**

Any DeepSeek-V4 sparse-MLA configuration with `max_model_len` on auto (or `-1`) where the available KV cache is smaller than the full model context, e.g. lower `--gpu-memory-utilization` until the startup log shows `max_model_len: reduced from …`.

**Workaround**

Set an explicit `--max-model-len` that fits the KV cache (we use 900000). Then no auto-fit happens and both values agree.

**Suggested fix**

Propagate the update to the model state, e.g. in `GPUModelRunner.update_max_model_len`: `self.model_state.max_model_len = max_model_len` (plus any other cached copies) — or let `ModelState` read `self.model_config.max_model_len` instead of caching it.

**Related**

#46794 describes the same pattern in the V1 `GPUModelRunner` (`InputBatch` built with the original `max_model_len` before the auto-fit, stale block table → `RuntimeError` during decode). This one is the V2 runner's `ModelState`; a general fix could make every component that snapshots `max_model_len` pick up the auto-fitted value.

[Performance][ROCm] shared_expert_gate ([1, K] weight) misses every skinny-GEMM path and costs 13.7% of the decode step

## Summary

On ROCm, `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` dispatches on `m = weight.shape[0]`. Its two skinny-GEMM branches cover `m > 8` (wvSplitK) and `m % 4 == 0` (LLMM1), so for `m <= 8` only `m ∈ {4, 8}` are covered — **`m ∈ {1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7}` falls through** to `torch.nn.functional.linear` → rocBLAS. (The `n` conditions also differ: wvSplitK takes `0 < n <= 5`, LLMM1 only `n == 1`.)

`m == 1` is not a rare shape. In transformers today, `self.shared_expert_gate = torch.nn.Linear(config.hidden_size, 1, bias=False)` — i.e. a `[1, hidden]` weight — appears in **`qwen2_moe`, `qwen3_next`, and `qwen3_5_moe`**, invoked once per layer per token to produce the scalar that gates the shared expert's contribution. (`qwen3_moe` and `qwen3_vl_moe` have no shared expert, so they are unaffected; `glm4_moe` has a shared expert but no gate.) Because `bias=False` there, `bias is None` always holds for this call.

For a `1×2048 @ 2048×1` product, rocBLAS selects `Cijk_Ailk_Bljk_BBS_BH_MT128x32x16_..._GSU1_...` — a **128×32 macro-tile with no split-K**. That is one workgroup on a 40-CU GPU serially walking `k=2048`: **~140 µs to move 4 KiB of weights**, against **~7.9 µs** for every width the skinny ladder does cover.

Measured on a Qwen3.5-MoE 35B-A3B (40 layers, hidden 2048, 256 experts, 8 active), batch-1 decode, gfx1151:

| | |
|---|---|
| cost per call | 137 µs |
| calls per decode step | 40 (one per layer) |
| **total** | **5.48 ms of a 40.06 ms step = 13.7%** |
| decode after fixing it | 40.06 → 34.79 ms/step, **24.53 → 28.32 tok/s (+15.5%)** |

## Environment

- gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S / Strix Halo), ROCm 7.14, torch 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0
- vLLM 0.27.1 (the same dispatch conditions are present on `main` today)
- `VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM` at its default (`True`)

## Where

`vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py`, in `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl`:

```python
    if use_skinny:
        x_view = x.reshape(-1, x.size(-1)).contiguous()
        if m > 8 and 0 < n <= 5:                                     # m == 1 fails
            ...
        elif m % 4 == 0 and n == 1 and k <= 8192 and bias is None:   # 1 % 4 != 0, fails
            ...

    if rocm_aiter_ops.is_tgemm_enabled():
        ...
    return torch.nn.functional.linear(x, weight, bias)   # <-- m == 1 lands here
```

Note `is_tgemm_enabled()` requires `on_gfx950()`, and `use_aiter_triton_gemm()` matches only a hardcoded shape whitelist, so on gfx11xx there is no other path to catch this.

## Reproducer

Standalone, no checkpoint needed. Part A needs only torch; Part B additionally needs vLLM: https://gist.github.com/wenis/ea2a42350797771304a2d8ea8c7848f7

Output on the environment above, **stock vLLM**, `--k 2048 --iters 200`:

```
device : AMD Radeon 8060S Graphics
torch  : 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0
shape  : x[1, 2048] @ w[m, 2048].T  (batch-1 decode), bfloat16

=== Part A: torch.nn.functional.linear (vLLM's fallback path) ===
   m    us/call     GiB/s   note
   1     141.17      0.03   <- shared_expert_gate; 4 KiB of weights
   2      37.45      0.20
   3      40.33      0.28
   4      37.82      0.40
   8      39.65      0.77
  12      38.00      1.20
  16      39.09      1.56
  32      40.12      3.04
  64      37.81      6.46

m=1 as a reduction (x * w).sum(-1) :     5.47 us
m=1 via F.linear                   :   141.17 us   (25.8x slower)

=== Part B: vLLM's rocm_unquantized_gemm dispatch ===
   m    us/call   expected path
   1     139.93   *** NO SKINNY PATH -> rocBLAS fallback ***
   2      37.16   *** NO SKINNY PATH -> rocBLAS fallback ***
   3      38.82   *** NO SKINNY PATH -> rocBLAS fallback ***
   4       7.90   LLMM1 (m % 4 == 0, n == 1)
   8       7.88   LLMM1 (m % 4 == 0, n == 1)
  12       7.99   wvSplitK (m > 8, n <= 5)
  16       7.95   wvSplitK (m > 8, n <= 5)
  32       8.01   wvSplitK (m > 8, n <= 5)
  64       7.96   wvSplitK (m > 8, n <= 5)
```

Two separate things show up here, and I think only the first is vLLM's to fix:

1. **The dispatch gap.** `m = 1` costs **139.93 µs** against **~7.9 µs** for every covered width — **17.7x** — while moving *less* data than any of them.
2. **rocBLAS is additionally pathological at `m == 1` specifically.** In Part A, which never touches vLLM's ladder, `m = 1` costs **141 µs** while `m ∈ {2, 3, 4, 8, ..., 64}` all sit at **37–40 µs**. So `m = 2` and `m = 3` miss the skinny ladder too, but cost ~3.7x less than `m = 1` does. The degenerate single-row output is its own kernel-selection problem, independent of vLLM.

## Attribution

The 137 µs in the table above was measured on the full model and then traced, not inferred from reading the guard:

1. vLLM's own torch profiler (`--profiler-config.profiler=torch`), 51 decode steps under representative serving flags with CUDA graphs **on**. Kernel `Cijk_..._MT128x32x16_..._GSU1` appeared at **137.5 µs × 39.2 calls/step**. An `--enforce-eager` run agreed at 137.06 µs × 40 calls, so it is not a graph-capture artifact.
2. Call-chain attribution on the eager trace resolved it to `aten::mm < aten::matmul < aten::linear < vllm::rocm_unquantized_gemm < vllm::moe_forward_shared`.
3. Dispatch counts for the step were exactly **271 = 231 `wvSplitK` + 40 fallback**, with `LLMM1` never taken — i.e. exactly one linear per layer misses the ladder.
4. `shared_expert_gate.weight [1, 2048]` is the **only** 2-D weight in the model with `shape[0] == 1`, so the 40 fallbacks are fully accounted for.

## Proposed fix

A `[1, K]` weight is a dot product. Adding it as a third branch in the existing ladder:

```python
        elif m == 1:
            out = (x_view * weight.reshape(-1)).sum(-1, keepdim=True)
            if bias is not None:
                out = out + bias
            return out.reshape(*x.shape[:-1], weight.shape[0])
```

With that mounted over the container's copy, Part B's `m = 1` row goes **139.93 µs → 6.82 µs (20.5x)**, and every other row is unchanged within noise (7.88–8.08 µs). End-to-end on the model above: **+15.5% decode**, with the `Cijk` kernel gone from the profile entirely and `wvSplitK` untouched (17.58 vs 17.54 ms/step), i.e. nothing else moved.

The `bias is not None` arm is defensive only — transformers builds this layer with `bias=False`.

Relaxing the `LLMM1` branch to accept `m < 4` looks unattractive: it passes a hardcoded split factor of 4, and the `m % 4 == 0` guard appears to be a vectorization requirement. The patch deliberately fixes only `m == 1`; `m ∈ {2, 3, 5, 6, 7}` remain uncovered, and I have no model that exercises them, so I would rather not widen it speculatively. Happy to restructure however maintainers prefer.

## Numerics — please read before taking the patch as-is

**The output is not bitwise identical to `F.linear`, and the difference is not only summation order.**

`x_view * weight.reshape(-1)` is a bf16 × bf16 product, so **each of the K element products is rounded to bf16 before it is summed**. `F.linear` accumulates the products in fp32 without rounding the intermediates. `torch.sum` then accumulates those bf16 values in fp32, so the reduction step itself is fine — it is the elementwise product that loses precision the GEMM keeps.

Measured on random bf16 vectors at K=2048, max absolute difference was **3.1e-02 to 2.5e-01** across runs, on dot products of order ~45 — a small number of bf16 ulps, but a real and systematic difference rather than pure reordering.

If that matters, the safer formulation is to widen before multiplying:

```python
            out = (x_view.float() * weight.reshape(-1).float()).sum(-1, keepdim=True).to(x.dtype)
```

which should keep the fp32 intermediates the GEMM has. **I have not benchmarked that variant** — it adds two small casts to a 4 KiB operand, so I would expect it to stay far ahead of 140 µs, but I would not want that assumption in the patch without a maintainer confirming which trade-off is wanted. Padding `m` to 16 and slicing the result is a third option that would stay exact and keep it a GEMM.

For what it is worth on end-to-end behaviour with the bf16-product version applied: greedy decode matched the unpatched baseline for 794 of 1028 characters (~200 identical tokens) before diverging at a near-tie between two equally plausible continuations, and across 400 tool-calling benchmark problems there were **zero malformed tool calls**. That is evidence the patched model is healthy in absolute terms; it is **not** a controlled A/B, since I do not have an unpatched run of the same benchmark. A maintainer wanting a strict before/after should ask for one.

vLLM already selects different kernels by shape, so bitwise stability across shapes does not appear to be a property it currently guarantees — flagging it explicitly in case that changes which fix is preferred.

## Relationship to existing work on this call site

**#43187** proposes a Triton fusion for the *same* call site — collapsing the gate's skinny GEMM, sigmoid and broadcast-multiply into a single kernel, measured on MI355x. I believe the two are complementary rather than competing, because they attack different layers:

- #43187 removes **kernel-launch count and intermediate tensors** in `models/qwen2_moe.py`.
- This issue is that `layers/utils.py`'s dispatch ladder **never offers that GEMM a skinny path at all**, so it lands on a rocBLAS kernel measured at 17.7× the cost of the ones the ladder does select for neighbouring widths.

If #43187 lands, its fused kernel replaces this call site for the models it covers, and this fix still applies to every *other* `m == 1` linear reaching `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl`. If it doesn't, this fix helps the call site on its own. Fixing the dispatch also makes the un-fused path a fairer baseline to measure a fusion against.

**#39280** (merged) added AITER Fused Shared Experts, which bypasses the call site at MoE-block level — but it is opt-in (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS`, default `False`) and requires AITER. **#37800**, which would have enabled it by default on ROCm, was closed. So on a default ROCm configuration, and on any configuration running with AITER off (as gfx1151 is here), the unfused path is what executes.

## Related

- #15830 introduced this dispatch (and, per its history, the `n <= 5` bound for spec decode).
- Point 2 under the reproducer may deserve a separate rocBLAS/hipBLASLt report: selecting a 128×32 tile with `GSU1` for a degenerate 1-row output is a poor heuristic regardless of what vLLM hands it.

DeepseekV32IndexerBackend requires --block-size 64 — not documented or auto-detected

**Title:** `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` requires `--block-size 64` — not documented or auto-detected

**vLLM version:** v0.24.0

**Backend:** `TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` / `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` (PR [#38476](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38476))

---

`DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` (used by GLM-DSA models via `TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` backend) only supports block size `[64]`:

```python
SUPPORTED_BLOCK_SIZES = [64]
```

However, the KV cache manager defaults to block size `16`. When these don't overlap, `select_common_block_size()` in `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py` raises:

```
ValueError: No common block size for 16 between kv_manager=[16] and backend=[64]
```

This error is opaque and doesn't point users to the solution (`--block-size 64`).

**Proposed fix:** Either:
1. Auto-set block size to 64 when `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` is selected (similar to how other backends constrain block sizes), OR
2. Add a clear error message: `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend requires --block-size 64, but got --block-size 16`, OR
3. Document the `--block-size 64` requirement in the TRITON_MLA_SPARSE / DSA model deployment guide.

**Affected models:** Any GLM-DSA variant (GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V3.2, etc.) when using `VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_MLA_SPARSE`.
hints:
Confirming this is still present in **v0.26.0**, with an additional data point: the failure is **pipeline-parallelism-dependent** for GLM-DSA models.

Setup: GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, NVFP4 compressed-tensors checkpoint — FP4 routed experts, BF16 attention/trunk), 2 nodes × 8× B200, Ray executor.

- `--tensor-parallel-size 8` single node: boots fine with **default** block size.
- `--pipeline-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel` across 2 nodes: crashes at KV-cache init on the PP rank-1 workers with

```
ValueError: No common block size for 32.
```

(the KV manager picked 32 here rather than 16, but it's the same `select_common_block_size()` failure — `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` only advertises `[64]`).

`--block-size 64` fixes it, same as reported above. +1 for auto-setting the block size when this backend is selected — the PP-dependence makes the current error even harder to attribute, since the same model/config boots cleanly without PP.

[Bug]: One bad multimodal item (feature/placeholder mismatch) kills the entire V1 engine tree instead of failing that request

### Describe the bug

A single multimodal item whose processed feature count disagrees with its prompt placeholder count raises `ValueError` inside `_merge_multimodal_embeddings`, and V1 treats it as a **fatal engine exception**: the offending `EngineCore` dies, every `AsyncLLM.add_request` on every API server then raises `EngineDeadError`, and the process manager tears down the whole deployment (all DP ranks plus all API servers). One bad request — or one poisoned processor-cache entry — is a total outage requiring a full restart.

We hit this in a DP8 internal-LB deployment (Gemma 4 audio): a request whose prompt spliced 638 placeholder slots was served 138 multimodal embeddings, and the entire 8-engine + 8-API-server group died mid-benchmark. The same raise is present on current `main` (`vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py:718`).

The failing request is fully identified at the failure site (`req_id` plus the item's `mm_hash`, both captured by `dump_input`), so this is a request-scoped, recoverable condition — not engine-state corruption.

### To Reproduce

Serve any multimodal model with DP > 1 and internal LB, then submit a request where the mm placeholder count in the prompt differs from the number of embeddings produced for the item. We triggered it via a stale processor-cache entry (a cached item processed from a 10 s clip was served to a request whose prompt spliced placeholders for a different clip — see the cross-linked uuid issue for how the entry got stale); any processing bug that splits splice count from feature count reaches the same raise.

Observed chain (v0.26.1rc1.dev1246):

```
(Worker pid=…) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1055] ValueError: Attempted to assign 138 = 138 multimodal tokens to 638 placeholders
    vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py:711 _merge_multimodal_embeddings
(ApiServer_7 pid=…) ERROR [serving.py:908] vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue.
    vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py:305 add_request
ERROR [utils.py:592] RuntimeError: Process ApiServer_4 (PID: 507668) died with exit code None
    vllm/v1/utils.py:579 wait_for_completion_or_failure
```

### Expected behavior

- Abort/reject the offending request (stream error or 4xx) with the merge-mismatch message; keep the engine alive.
- Evict the offending item's `mm_hash` from the processor/encoder caches — otherwise a poisoned entry re-kills the engine on the next request that touches it.
- Engine suicide is the right response to corrupt engine state; an mm count mismatch with full request context available is a bad-input condition.

### Environment

- vLLM: v0.26.1rc1.dev1246+g1a085dadf (paths re-verified on `main` @ f4eccdade)
- Hardware: 8x B200 (SM100), `--data-parallel-size 8`, internal LB, 8 API servers, chunked prefill (the crash hit on a resumed chunked prefill, `num_computed_tokens=128`), speculative decoding enabled (not involved in the failure path)
- Model: Gemma 4 audio (the `_merge_multimodal_embeddings` raise itself is model-agnostic)

query:
[Performance]: Streaming derender bypasses renderer thread pool and blocks the event loop

### Your current environment

- vllm version: v0.28.0
- Architecture: AArch64
- Deployment: vLLM Render as a sidecar
- Request type: streaming Chat Completions
- Concurrent requests: 20
- Output length: up to 2048 tokens
- `--renderer-num-workers`: tested with both `4` and `8`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Streaming Derender appears to perform CPU-bound detokenization directly on the FastAPI event loop instead of using the renderer thread pool.

Under concurrent streaming workloads, this serializes Derender processing, increases per-chunk latency, delays tokenization requests, and propagates backpressure to the inference engine.

This looks related to, but not fully covered by, [#49396](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49396), which offloaded existing Derender CPU work to the renderer thread pool.

## Observed implementation

The non-streaming Derender paths use asynchronous wrappers backed by the renderer executor.

However, the streaming paths call synchronous detokenization directly from async code:

- `OnlineDerenderer.derender_chat_stream()`
- `OnlineDerenderer.derender_completion_stream()`
- `_detokenize_delta()`

As a result, increasing `--renderer-num-workers` does not improve streaming Derender throughput.

## Benchmark results

| Metric | 4 workers | 8 workers |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Aggregate throughput | 889.1 tok/s | 899.5 tok/s |
| Per-stream throughput p50 | 46.3 tok/s | 46.0 tok/s |
| Derender RPC latency p50 | 21.35 ms | 21.52 ms |
| Chunk cadence p50 | 21.49 ms | 21.66 ms |
| Tokenize latency p50 | 153.8 ms | 155.4 ms |

Compared with the Render-disabled baseline:

| Metric | Render disabled | Streaming Render |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Aggregate throughput | 1011.6 tok/s | 889.1 tok/s |
| Per-stream throughput p50 | 53.1 tok/s | 46.3 tok/s |
| TTFT p50 | 166 ms | 167 ms |
| TTOT p50 | 18.70 ms | 21.26 ms |

The workload completed successfully without request errors.

## Additional timing evidence

For the streaming Derender consumer:

| Measurement | p50 |
| --- | ---: |
| Derender RPC time | 21.35 ms |
| RPC plus local processing | 21.40 ms |
| Chunk consumption cadence | 21.49 ms |
| Queue wait time | 0.15 ms |

The timing approximately satisfies:

```text
chunk cadence
~= queue wait + Derender processing
~= Derender RPC latency
```

This indicates that the streaming consumption loop is paced almost entirely by the synchronous Derender request.

The same RPC takes approximately 3.2 ms under light load but approximately 21.4 ms at concurrency 20, indicating event-loop saturation and queuing.

## Additional context: token-only Generate does not provide batch streaming

The token-only `/inference/v1/generate` endpoint currently handles one prompt or sequence per request. Therefore, a multi-prompt Completion request must be fanned out into multiple independent Generate streams.

Each generated stream maintains its own Derender `stream_state` and invokes the streaming Derender endpoint for every chunk:

```text
multi-prompt request
  -> N Generate streams
  -> N independent Derender states
  -> one Derender request per generated chunk
```

This is not the direct cause of the event-loop blocking issue, which is also reproducible with concurrent single-prompt requests. However, the lack of a batch Generate interface amplifies the problem because the number of concurrent per-chunk Derender calls grows with the number of generated sequences.

It may be useful to clarify whether batch token-only Generate is planned. Regardless of that direction, streaming Derender should avoid performing CPU-bound work directly on the shared event loop.

## Expected behavior

Streaming Derender CPU work should use the renderer's shared executor, consistent with the approach introduced by [#49396](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49396).

Increasing `--renderer-num-workers` should provide additional concurrency for streaming Derender and prevent Derender work from blocking Tokenize requests on the same event loop.

## Suggested direction

Consider offloading the CPU-bound part of streaming Derender to the existing renderer executor, while preserving the current async streaming API and client-carried `stream_state`.

Conceptually:

```python
result = await make_async(
    streaming_derender_cpu_work,
    executor=renderer._executor,
)(generate_chunk, stream_state)
```

The exact executor boundary may need to include parser replay and incremental detokenization so that all CPU-bound work is removed from the event loop.

Batch token-only Generate could reduce the number of independent RPC streams, but it should be treated as a separate enhancement rather than a prerequisite for fixing the event-loop blocking issue.

## Related work

- [#49396: Offload Derender CPU work to the renderer thread pool](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49396)
- [#47161: Streaming Derender RFC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47161)

Could you confirm whether streaming Derender is expected to use the renderer executor, or whether another concurrency mechanism is planned for this path?

Idefics3/SmolVLM: num_patches=0 for non-tiled images mis-sizes pixel_values while the prompt still reserves image_seq_len placeholder tokens

### Description

For Idefics3/SmolVLM, when an image doesn't get tiled (`do_image_splitting=False`, or splitting enabled but the image is already small enough that no split is needed), `Idefics3ProcessingInfo` computes `num_patches=0` for that image and uses it to size the image's `pixel_values`/`pixel_attention_mask` slice in the multimodal field config, while the prompt still correctly reserves `image_seq_len` placeholder tokens for it. The zero-size slice doesn't match the real, non-empty pixel data HF's own preprocessing produces for that image, which should surface as a `_merge_multimodal_embeddings` token-count mismatch (0 actual vs `image_seq_len` expected) at inference time.

### Where the numbers diverge

`get_number_of_image_patches` in HF's `Idefics3ImageProcessor` (checked directly against `transformers==5.5.3`, the minimum vLLM currently requires per `requirements/common.txt`):

```python
# transformers/models/idefics3/image_processing_idefics3.py, v5.5.3
def get_number_of_image_patches(self, height, width, images_kwargs):
    ...
    num_patches = num_rows = num_cols = 0
    if do_image_splitting:
        ...
        if resized_height > max_height or resized_width > max_width:
            num_rows = math.ceil(resized_height / max_height)
            num_cols = math.ceil(resized_width / max_width)
            num_patches = num_rows * num_cols + 1
    return num_patches, num_rows, num_cols
```

`num_patches` stays `0` whenever `do_image_splitting=False`, or whenever splitting is enabled but the image doesn't actually exceed `max_image_size`. This is consistent with the real preprocessing path, `split_images()` in the same class, which returns `num_splits_h = num_splits_w = 0` in exactly the same "no split needed" case, but still returns `frames = [image]`, one real frame, the global image itself.

`vllm/model_executor/models/idefics3.py` uses this `num_patches` value in two places that end up disagreeing with each other:

1. `Idefics3MultiModalProcessor._call_hf_processor` (line ~331-340):
   ```python
   num_patches = [
       self.info.get_num_patches(image_width=size.width, image_height=size.height,
                                  processor=hf_processor, mm_kwargs=mm_kwargs)
       for size in image_sizes
   ]
   processed_outputs["num_patches"] = torch.tensor(num_patches)
   ```
   This directly reuses HF's `num_patches` (0 in the no-split case) as `size_per_item` for `MultiModalFieldConfig.flat_from_sizes("image", num_patches)` in `_get_mm_fields_config` (line ~356-359), which slices the flattened `pixel_values`/`pixel_attention_mask` tensor per image using exactly these sizes. A `0` here means vLLM will slice a zero-row chunk for that image, even though HF's actual preprocessing produced one real frame of pixel data for it.

2. `Idefics3ProcessingInfo.get_image_repl` (line ~204-247) builds the prompt text for the same image independently, and has its own explicit special case for this:
   ```python
   _, grid_h, grid_w = self._get_image_feature_grid_size(...)
   if grid_w == 0 and grid_h == 0:
       return global_img_placeholder + fake_image_token   # image_seq_len <image> tokens
   ```
   So the prompt correctly ends up with `image_seq_len` placeholder tokens for this image, that part is right, it's specifically the `pixel_values` sizing in (1) that doesn't have an equivalent special case.

### Why this should be user-visible

`MultiModalFieldConfig.flat_from_sizes` slices a flattened tensor using `size_per_item` as consecutive chunk sizes (`vllm/multimodal/inputs.py`, `flat_from_sizes`). A `0` entry for an image whose actual pixel data isn't empty means either that image's real pixel rows get silently reattributed to a neighboring image's slice in the same batch (in a multi-image request mixing split and non-split images), or, in the single-image case, the vision tower ends up running on a 0-row input and producing 0 embeddings for that image. Either way, `is_multimodal.sum()` (from the correctly-sized prompt, `image_seq_len` positions) won't match `len(mm_embeds_flat)` (0, or misattributed from another image) when `_merge_multimodal_embeddings` runs (`vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py`, ~line 545-550), which is exactly the shape-mismatch `RuntimeError` that function's `except` branch is written to catch and report.

### Reproduction

Any Idefics3/SmolVLM checkpoint with `do_image_splitting=False` set (either via `--mm-processor-kwargs '{"do_image_splitting": false}'`, or a `preprocessor_config.json` that sets that default), or any image small enough that splitting doesn't trigger even with the default `do_image_splitting=True`, should hit this on the very first request containing that image. `smolvlm.py` inherits this class unmodified, so it's affected the same way.

### Notes

`tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_smolvlm.py` doesn't appear to cover the no-split path (this is inferred from the file layout in the repo, I didn't run the suite), which is consistent with this not having been caught yet, dummy/test images there are sized to force splitting.

Happy to help narrow down the exact runtime error text if useful, wanted to get the root-cause diff (the `num_patches=0`-but-real-pixel-data-exists mismatch, specifically in the `_get_mm_fields_config` sizing, not the prompt string which is already correct) written up precisely first.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description In vLLM 0.29.0's V1 model runner, a completed request can leave its `prompt_embeds` tensor referenced by `InputBatch.req_prompt_embeds`. After all requests have been removed and the persistent batch is empty, the dictionary still contains one tensor for every slot that previously handled a prompt-embedding request. Reusing those slots with ordinary token-ID requests does not release or overwrite the old tensors. They remain alive until another prompt-embedding request overwrites the same slot, the dictionary is cleared, or the worker exits. The retention is bounded by persistent-batch capacity, but a worker can keep the peak prompt-embedding footprint of a previous burst even after ordinary text requests replace that workload. The reproducer retains 256 MiB across eight reused slots and releases it only when the stale dictionary is cleared. At a `max_num_seqs` of 256, the same `(4096, 4096)` BF16 shape can retain up to 8 GiB of host memory. This can increase host-memory pressure, swapping, allocation failures, or container eviction risk. Stale entries can also cause unnecessary prompt-embedding staging work for replacement requests. ## Reproduction Use the script [repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32476544/repro_slot_retention.py), with vLLM 0.29.0 installed, run: ```bash python repro.py 2>&1 | tee reproducer.log ``` The script reproduces a prompt-embedding burst followed by ordinary text traffic: 1. fills eight slots with `(4096, 4096)` BF16 prompt-embedding tensors, totaling 256 MiB; 2. completes all eight requests and forces garbage collection; 3. reuses every slot with an unrelated token-ID request; 4. verifies that every old tensor is still attached to the reused slot; and 5. clears only `req_prompt_embeds` as a control while the text requests remain active. The script records both weak-reference liveness and process RSS. It calls `malloc_trim()` only after clearing the dictionary so that the RSS control is visible; the weak references establish tensor lifetime independently of the allocator. ## Actual result ```text After the embedding requests finish: active request IDs: [] req_prompt_embeds keys: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7] live old tensors: 8 live old tensor bytes: 268435456 process RSS bytes: 1166053376 After text requests reuse the same slots: active request IDs: [text-request-0, ..., text-request-7] req_prompt_embeds keys: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7] live old tensors: 8 live old tensor bytes: 268435456 stale entries still reference the old tensors: true process RSS bytes: 1166053376 After clearing only req_prompt_embeds: active request IDs: [text-request-0, ..., text-request-7] req_prompt_embeds keys: [] live old tensors: 0 live old tensor bytes: 0 process RSS bytes: 896708608 RSS drop bytes: 269344768 ``` The weak-reference control shows that the stale dictionary entries are the remaining owners of the tensors. The text requests remain active when the old tensors are released, so the tensors are not needed by the replacement requests. The complete output is in [reproducer_slot_retention.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32476576/reproducer_slot_retention.log). ## Expected result Once a request is removed, its slot must no longer own the request's prompt-embedding tensor. With an empty batch, `req_prompt_embeds` should be empty. Reusing the slots with token-ID requests should not keep any tensor from the completed requests alive. ## Root cause [`InputBatch.add_request()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py#L350-L386) stores the tensor by slot index: ```python if request.prompt_embeds is not None: self.req_prompt_embeds[req_index] = request.prompt_embeds ``` [`InputBatch.remove_request()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py#L528-L582) clears the other request-scoped state but never removes this entry. The empty-batch branch of [`condense()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py#L706-L727) also leaves the dictionary unchanged. The missing cleanup can be performed as soon as the request index is known: ```python self.req_prompt_embeds.pop(req_index, None) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

[Bug]: Qwen4Exp PinnedHost PLE prefetch reads n-gram ids from graph-pool memory that later segments reuse

### Your current environment

DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), TP=1, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13, vLLM main (`1ea7c63f4` nightly wheel), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next,
MTP n=3, `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`Qwen4ExpPLEPinnedHostEmbedding.start_prefetch`
([ngram_embedding.py#L493-L506](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9f07d023d/vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py#L493-L506))
launches the lookup on a side stream and returns; `_finalize_prefetch` joins later. The `gathered_ids` it reads come
from a captured graph segment, so they live in the graph pool. Once `start_prefetch` returns, later segments can reuse
that memory, and at replay the main stream may overwrite the ids while the side stream is still reading them
(`record_stream` does not cover graph-pool memory). The effect is silent: greedy outputs stop being reproducible.

Measured with a backend that runs exactly this flow and differs only in row storage (a pageable file mapping, #58439).
Protocol: 8 greedy prompts, cold vs warm, within one server start.

| lookup | cold == warm | max \|Δlogprob\| |
|---|---|---|
| side stream, ids from the graph pool (this flow) | 2/8 | 1.41 |
| same + #57785 | 1/8 | 1.41 |
| side stream, ids copied to a persistent buffer first | **8/8** | 0 |
| current stream | **8/8** | 0 |

Caveat: PinnedHost itself could not run here, because its pinned table does not fit in 128 GB of unified memory.
Pinned reads are faster, so the window should be narrower; not reproduced on PinnedHost itself.

Possible fix: copy `gathered_ids` into a persistent (non-pool) buffer on the current stream before the side-stream
launch (row 3), or look up on the current stream (row 4, which loses the overlap).

*AI assistance: prepared with Claude; measurements run and checked by the submitter.*
hints:
Same box as you (GB10, sm_121, 128 GB unified), so I hit your caveat too — the PinnedHost table doesn't fit here either. Can't add a PinnedHost run. Two things from reading `main` instead.

**The flow is as you describe, and there's an asymmetry in it that argues for your row 3.** In `start_prefetch`:

```python
gathered_ids  = self._gather_dp_ids(ngram_ids, slot_size)     # allocated in the captured region
active_output = self._prefetch_buffer[: gathered_ids.shape[0]]  # persistent
prefetch_stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
gathered_ids.record_stream(prefetch_stream)
with torch.cuda.stream(prefetch_stream):
    self._lookup(gathered_ids, output=active_output)
```

The **output** side of the side-stream transfer already uses a persistent buffer — `self._prefetch_buffer` is allocated once at setup (`torch.empty(max_total_tokens * etp_dp, num_ngram_heads, embedding_dim, ...)`), outside any capture, alongside `self._prefetch_stream`. The **input** side is the only thing still coming straight out of the pool.

So "copy `gathered_ids` into a persistent buffer first" isn't a new mechanism here, it's the pattern this class already uses for the other half of the same transfer. A second pre-allocated `int` buffer sized the same way (`max_total_tokens * etp_data_parallel_size`), filled on the current stream before the `wait_stream`, would mirror it exactly — and unlike row 4 it keeps the overlap you're paying the side stream for.

**On the `record_stream` half I'd rather not vouch for you.** I went looking for something in-tree that states `record_stream` can't protect graph-pool blocks, and didn't find it — the closest is `_activation_offloading/offload_ops.py` telling callers not to use `record_stream` at all, for unrelated fragmentation reasons. Your measurements are the evidence here; I just can't corroborate the mechanism from the source, and someone will likely ask for that.

Worth noting your table already discriminates without needing the mechanism: rows 3 and 4 both go 8/8 and Δ 0, rows 1 and 2 don't. That's the input-ids lifetime and nothing else, whatever the allocator's reason turns out to be.

query:
[Bug]: decorate_logs corrupts JSON log output

##### Problem

The `python-json-logger` example in `examples/features/logging_configuration.md` configures vLLM application logs as JSON. Worker processes subsequently call `vllm.utils.system_utils.decorate_logs()`, which rewrites `stdout` and `stderr` to prepend a process prefix to every line.

For example, a formatter emits:

```json
{"message": "Engine started"}
```

but the actual output is:

```text
(Worker_DP0 pid=12345) {"message": "Engine started"}
```

The result is not valid JSON or NDJSON, so structured-log consumers cannot parse it.

Thanks to Kevin Howell (@kahowell) for finding and reporting this issue.

##### Expected behavior

- A configured JSON formatter emits one valid JSON object per `LogRecord`.
- vLLM process identity remains available to log consumers.
- Default human-readable console logging retains its familiar process prefix.

##### Proposed direction

Move the vLLM logical process name into a `LogRecord` attribute, such as `vllm_process_name`, through a chained record factory. The default text formatter can render that attribute with the standard `process` PID attribute. `decorate_logs()` should set record metadata instead of rewriting standard streams.

This preserves rank-aware names such as `Worker_DP0_TP1` in structured output without prepending non-JSON text.

##### Scope and follow-up

The immediate fix should guarantee valid JSON for records emitted through configured Python loggers. It cannot convert direct writes from third-party or native libraries into JSON.

`VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH` is also supplied to Uvicorn as its logging configuration. Documenting or providing a complete JSON configuration for `uvicorn`, `uvicorn.error`, and `uvicorn.access` is a follow-up, rather than part of this bug fix.

##### Related

- #57200 tracks the broader console logging configuration model.

---

[Feature]:  Record model_id in bench latency/throughput --output-json

### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

`vllm bench serve` records the model in its `--output-json` payload:

```python
# vllm/benchmarks/serve.py:2283
result_json["model_id"] = model_id
```

`vllm bench latency` and `vllm bench throughput` do not. Their payloads are:

```python
# vllm/benchmarks/latency.py:171
results = {
    "avg_latency": ...,
    "latencies": ...,
    "percentiles": ...,
}

# vllm/benchmarks/throughput.py:1143
results = {
    "elapsed_time": ...,
    "num_requests": ...,
    "total_num_tokens": ...,
    "requests_per_second": ...,
    "tokens_per_second": ...,
}
```

So a latency or throughput result file does not say which model produced the
numbers. Any consumer that archives, compares, or ingests these files has to
recover the model out-of-band — from the output filename, or from the shell
command that produced it. Both are lossy: filenames are chosen by the caller,
and the command is not stored next to the result.

This bites in CI/benchmark-tracking setups, where result files are collected
from many runs and loaded into a database. With no `model_id`, rows end up
attributed by filename, which silently produces wrong model labels rather than
an error.

The `.pytorch.json` sibling written under `SAVE_TO_PYTORCH_BENCHMARK_FORMAT=1`
does carry the model (inside `extra_info.args`), but that file is opt-in and
exists for the PyTorch OSS benchmark database, so relying on it is a workaround
rather than a fix for the primary `--output-json` output.

Proposal: add `model_id` to both payloads, using the same key `bench serve`
already uses.

### Alternatives

- **`--metadata KEY=VALUE`** (proposed in #41541) lets the caller pass arbitrary
  fields, including the model. That is a useful feature but a different one: it
  is opt-in and requires every caller to remember to pass the model it already
  told vLLM about on the command line. The model is not user metadata; vLLM
  knows it.
- **Parse it from the filename / invoking command** — what consumers do today,
  and the reason model names get mislabelled.
- **Depend on the `.pytorch.json` sibling** — requires setting
  `SAVE_TO_PYTORCH_BENCHMARK_FORMAT=1` and reading a file whose stated purpose
  is a different database schema.

### Additional context

The change is additive and does not alter existing fields. The in-tree consumer
of these files, `.buildkite/performance-benchmarks/scripts/convert-results-json-to-markdown.py`,
selects columns from explicit allowlists (`latency_column_mapping:19`,
`throughput_results_column_mapping:32`) and already maps `"model_id": "Model"`
for serving rows, so an added key is ignored there rather than breaking the
tables. Each file's `save_to_pytorch_benchmark_format` reads named keys only.

Happy to send the PR.

[Bug] NIXL lease reaper strands expired KV blocks behind a heartbeated head entry

### Your current environment

`v0.27.1`. Found by source inspection; the repro below is standalone stdlib and
needs no vLLM install. I have not yet quantified the runtime impact on a live
deployment — filing this because the control flow looks unambiguous and the
reclaim path it affects is shared by both NIXL connector modes.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The NIXL lease reaper in `NixlConnectorWorker` relies on `_reqs_to_send` being ordered by expiry, but `_handle_heartbeat` breaks that invariant. A request that keeps receiving heartbeats can sit at the head of the dict and block every entry behind it from ever being reaped, even long after those entries' leases expire.

**The invariant.** The reaper exits at the first non-expired entry:

```python
# vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py (~L2147)
while self._reqs_to_send:
    req_id, expires = next(iter(self._reqs_to_send.items()))
    # Sorted dict, oldest requests are put first so we can exit early.
    if now < expires:
        break
    ...
    del self._reqs_to_send[req_id]
```

That is correct only while expiry order matches insertion order.

**What breaks it.** Heartbeats update the value in place:

```python
# same file (~L2198)
if req_id in self._reqs_to_send:
    old = self._reqs_to_send[req_id]
    self._reqs_to_send[req_id] = max(old, new_expiry)
```

Updating an existing key in a Python `dict` does not change its insertion position, so a renewed request keeps its original (early) slot while its expiry moves arbitrarily far into the future. Requests are inserted once (`pull_worker.py` asserts `req_id not in self._reqs_to_send` before inserting), so the position is never revisited.

**Consequence.** This is the common case under load: the oldest pending-send request is the one most likely to still be queued on D, and therefore the one being heartbeated, while newer requests behind it are not.

### Minimal reproduction

```python
LEASE_DURATION = 30.0     # kv_lease_duration default
LEASE_EXTENSION = 20.0    # kv_lease_duration * 2 // 3

def reap(reqs_to_send, now):                      # verbatim control flow
    done = []
    while reqs_to_send:
        req_id, expires = next(iter(reqs_to_send.items()))
        if now < expires:
            break
        del reqs_to_send[req_id]
        done.append(req_id)
    return done

def handle_heartbeat(reqs_to_send, req_id, now):  # verbatim
    if req_id in reqs_to_send:
        reqs_to_send[req_id] = max(reqs_to_send[req_id], now + LEASE_EXTENSION)

reqs = {"A": 0.0 + LEASE_DURATION,   # 30.0, enters first, stays queued on D
        "B": 2.0 + LEASE_DURATION,   # 32.0, never renewed
        "C": 4.0 + LEASE_DURATION}   # 34.0, never renewed
for t in (20.0, 40.0, 60.0, 80.0):
    handle_heartbeat(reqs, "A", t)   # A -> 100.0, still at the head

for now in (35.0, 50.0, 90.0):
    print(now, reap(dict(reqs), now))
```

Output:

```
35.0 []
50.0 []
90.0 []
```

`B` and `C` expired at `t=32.0` and `t=34.0`. At `t=90.0` neither has been released. They stay stranded for as long as `A` keeps receiving heartbeats, which by design can be indefinite ("each heartbeat extends the lease ... keeping blocks alive indefinitely while D is healthy" — `docs/design/nixl_kv_cache_lease.md`).

### Impact

Blocks that should have been reclaimed within `kv_lease_duration` (default 30s) of their reader disconnecting are held indefinitely on P, reducing available KV cache. This is the exact failure mode lease renewal was introduced to avoid (#41383): the design doc motivates the short initial lease by noting that under the old fixed 480s timeout "P would hold onto potentially several GBs of 'dead' blocks for up to 8 minutes". The head-of-line case restores that behaviour without a bound.

It also makes `vllm:nixl_num_kv_expired_reqs` under-report, since stranded entries are never passed to `record_kv_expired_req()`.

### Note on one fix that does *not* work

Re-inserting on heartbeat (delete + insert to move the entry to the tail) does not restore the invariant, because `max(old, now + extension)` can still be smaller than a later-inserted entry's initial expiry:

```
Y inserted t=0   -> expiry 30
X inserted t=25  -> expiry 55
Y renewed at t=26 -> max(30, 46) = 46, moved to tail
order: X(55), Y(46)   # at now=50, X blocks the already-expired Y
```

### Candidate fixes

1. **Scan all entries** instead of exiting early. Simplest and obviously correct; `O(n)` per step in the number of pending sends rather than amortized `O(1)`.
2. **Expiry-ordered heap with lazy deletion.** Push `(expiry, req_id)` on insert and on each renewal; pop while `top.expiry <= now` and skip entries whose expiry no longer matches the dict. `O(log n)`, more code.
3. **Keep the dict, maintain a separate ordered index** keyed by expiry.

Happy to send a PR for whichever shape maintainers prefer.

One thing to check alongside the fix: the reaper calls `self._reqs_to_process.remove(req_id)` (`base_worker.py` ~L2160) while other paths use `.discard()` (`pull_worker.py` ~L90). Any fix that reaps entries the current code never reaches will exercise that line for request IDs it previously never saw, so `remove()` vs `discard()` there may need a second look.

### Related but distinct

- #53095 (`NixlPushConnector heartbeat fails to renew KV leases`) is the opposite
  direction: leases expiring while the consumer still wants the blocks. This
  report is about a renewed entry preventing *other* entries from expiring. Both
  touch `_handle_heartbeat` / `_reqs_to_send` in `base_worker.py`, which is shared
  by the push and pull paths, so a fix here may be worth checking against that
  report.
- #46283 concerns decode-side *recv* blocks leaking on abort, and notes in passing
  that the `_reqs_to_send` reaper covers only the send side. That observation is
  consistent with this report but the defect is a different one.
- #53128 (closed) is the `TieringOffloadingSpec` p2p `_UNBOUND_STORE_TIMEOUT_S`
  path, a separate mechanism.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

[Bug][Frontend]: Anthropic /v1/messages always hoists inline system messages because merge detection checks the CLI --chat-template (None) instead of the model's template

### Your current environment

`main` @ 73a78e6f1f. `vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --reasoning-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47` (no `--chat-template`), with Claude Code 2.1.281 connected via `/v1/messages`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

This is item 1 of #58647, split out as its own issue.

`AnthropicServingMessages.__init__` decides whether to hoist inline `role: "system"` messages by calling:

```python
self._merge_inline_system = self._detect_merge_inline_system(chat_template)
```

`chat_template` here is the **`--chat-template` CLI value**, which is `None` for almost every deployment, and `_detect_merge_inline_system` short-circuits:

```python
if not chat_template:
    return True
```

As a result, the probe that renders `[system, user, system, user]` never runs against the template that is actually used, which comes from the tokenizer. **Every deployment that relies on the model's own template goes down the merge path**, including models whose templates handle inline system messages correctly (GLM-5.3 is one). The "preserve in place" branch added in #46025 only runs when a user passes `--chat-template` explicitly.

The merge path (`_convert_system_message`) appends every inline system message to the leading system block. Claude Code sends a new inline system message almost every turn (`<total_tokens>N tokens left</total_tokens>`). So the leading block changes on each request, and everything after it, i.e. the whole conversation, misses the prefix cache. It also changes semantics: a mid-conversation instruction becomes part of the global system prompt.

#### Reproducer (offline, tokenizer only)

The script builds Claude Code-shaped consecutive turns, runs each one through `to_chat_completion_request`, renders it with GLM-5.3-Flash's template, and counts how many prompt tokens turn N+1 shares with turn N. That count is the best possible prefix-cache hit.

```
turn 1->2: shared 671/709 (94.6%)
```

query:
[Bug] Qwen4Exp QSA indexer: per-chunk logits buffer grows with max_seq_len, caching allocator keeps every size, device OOM/hang on unified-memory GB10 (SM121) during long prefill

## Your current environment

- vLLM `0.28.1rc1.dev628+g2a02f6efe` (nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:96b234afa2867031ad0a226b149a06483861e613e3a3083da53398d347b5ffbd`, arm64), CUDA 13, V2 model runner.
- 2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, **unified memory**, 119 GB each), TP=2 across the two nodes (Ray-less multi-node, `--nnodes 2`).
- Model: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (Qwen4Exp architecture: 12 QSA sparse-attention layers with indexer, 36 GDN layers, PLE), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 262144`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`, chunked prefill, prefix caching, MTP k=3, `cudagraph_mode FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, `gpu_memory_utilization 0.8`.
- `indexer_compress_ratio=4`, `indexer_budget=2048` (model config). KV block size on this hybrid: 3200 tokens.
- Note: we run a few local overlays on top of this nightly (fp8 KV for QSA from #55557, a refusal-direction hook), but `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ops/qsa_indexer.py` (the code path below) is unmodified upstream. The previous nightly we ran (`8a728663`, `0.28.1rc1.dev388`) does not show the problem with the same model, hardware and flags.

## 🐛 Describe the bug

A single 254K-token cold prefill kills the engine on GB10: the step hangs at exactly **166,400 computed tokens**, the driver logs `NVRM: nvCheckOkFailedNoLog: Check failed: Out of memory [NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY] ... _memdescAllocInternal(pMemDesc) @ mem_desc.c:1359` on both nodes, and after 300 s the EngineCore dies with `TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out.` (dumped `SchedulerOutput`: `num_computed_tokens=[..., 166400]`, `num_scheduled_tokens={...: 3200}`).

Node-exporter shows each rank consuming ~9–14 GB **outside the KV pool** during the last ~60 s of the prefill (worker 13 → 4 GB available, head 9 → 0 GB), whereas on `8a728663` the same prefill leaves memory flat.

### Root cause

`qsa_select_paged_prefill` in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ops/qsa_indexer.py` now sizes the indexer logits buffer by the batch's `max_seq_len`:

```python
logits_width = triton.cdiv(triton.cdiv(max_seq_len, compress_ratio), 64) * 64
logits_width = min(max(64, logits_width), page_table.shape[1] * k_cache.shape[1])
max_logits_bytes = envs.VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB * 1024 * 1024   # 512 MB default
rows_per_chunk = max(1, max_logits_bytes // (logits_width * 4))
...
logits = torch.empty((num_queries, logits_width), dtype=torch.float32, ...)
```

Previously (`8a728663`) the width was the fixed page-table width (`columns = page_table.shape[1] * k_cache.shape[1]`), so every chunk allocated the same 512 MB buffer and the caching allocator reused it.

With chunked prefill (3200-token chunks here) and `compress_ratio=4`, chunk *i* of a long prompt now allocates `3200 × (800·i) × 4 B = 10.24 MB × i`, a **strictly increasing** size per chunk, until 3200 rows no longer fit under the 512 MB cap: `i = 52` → `52 × 3200 = 166,400 tokens`, exactly where the engine died. The PyTorch caching allocator never finds a cached block large enough for the next request, so it `cudaMalloc`s a new one each chunk and keeps the previous ones: `Σ 10.24 MB × i (i ≤ 52) ≈ 14 GB per rank`. On a discrete GPU `cudaMalloc` would eventually fail and the allocator would flush its cache and retry; on unified-memory GB10 `cudaMalloc` keeps succeeding until the driver has nothing left, and the failure surfaces as a GPU hang (`NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY` in dmesg) instead of a Python OOM.

### Evidence

- Attempt 1 (defaults): hang at 166,400 tokens, `NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY` ×7 on the worker node at the hang time, EngineCore dead 300 s later.
- Attempt 2 (`gdn_prefill_backend=triton`, to rule out the new FlashInfer GDN prefill path on SM12x): node memory still dropping during the prefill (head 9 → 6 GB in 49 s), probe aborted by a watchdog. GDN kernel is not the cause.
- Attempt 3 (`VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB=64`): the per-chunk request saturates at ~21K tokens (chunk 7) and is reused from there. Memory flat for the whole 254K prefill and for 8 concurrent 254K prompts; no errors. The cold prefill is even ~10% faster than on `8a728663` (92 s vs ~102 s single 254K prompt).

### Workaround

`VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB=64` (cost: up to 8 kernel launches per chunk and layer at 166K context instead of 1).

### Suggested fix

Round `logits_width` up to coarse buckets (e.g. multiples of 16K compressed columns), or allocate the buffer once at the page-table width as before, or take it from the workspace manager, so the caching allocator can reuse one block across chunks. Any allocation whose size grows monotonically per chunk will reproduce this on unified-memory devices.

## Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

During multi-rank prefiller startup with `MooncakeConnector`, worker registration can fail if the global rank 0 process is temporarily unable to answer the bootstrap HTTP request for more than approximately five seconds while registering a large host-memory segment.

The relevant code currently creates an [`httpx.AsyncClient()` without an explicit timeout](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py#L1085-L1114). In the tested environment, HTTPX 0.28.1 reports a default timeout of 5.0 seconds. The loop retries only `httpx.ConnectError`; every other exception reaches the generic handler and is re-raised.

The original log did not capture the exception class or traceback. The approximately 5.37-second timing, HTTPX's 5-second default, blank `str(e)`, and the server's later `200 OK` responses are consistent with an `httpx.TimeoutException`, most likely `httpx.ReadTimeout`. The exact subtype remains an inference, not a directly logged fact.

#### Relevant sanitized configuration

```text
MOONCAKE_GLOBAL_SEGMENT_SIZE=21474836480
HCCL_INTRA_PCIE_ENABLE=0
HCCL_INTRA_ROCE_ENABLE=1

--distributed-executor-backend mp
--data-parallel-size 1
```

The bootstrap HTTP server itself [runs in a daemon thread of the global rank 0 prefiller process](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_utils.py#L32-L65). In the observed failure, startup followed this timeline:

#### Why one registration failure becomes a permanent startup hang

The current control flow turns the registration exception into an unbounded wait:

1. `register_worker_with_bootstrap()` re-raises any exception other than `httpx.ConnectError`.
2. `_mooncake_sender_listener()` therefore exits before reaching [`ready_event.set()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py#L1115-L1137).
3. `register_kv_caches()` submits that coroutine through `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe()`, but does not retain or inspect the returned Future.
4. The same function then calls [`ready_event.wait()` with no timeout](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py#L1734-L1738).
5. The registration error is no longer propagated to the waiting thread, and startup remains blocked indefinitely.

#### Minimal reproduction outline

1. Start a multi-rank prefiller using `MooncakeConnector`.
2. Let global rank 0 host `MooncakeBootstrapServer`.
3. Configure a sufficiently large Mooncake host segment (20 GiB in this case), or otherwise delay/unservice the rank 0 bootstrap response for longer than five seconds during initialization.
4. Allow the other worker ranks to call `register_worker_with_bootstrap()` concurrently.
5. Observe that their POST requests time out after about five seconds and are not retried.

This can also be reproduced deterministically in a unit test by delaying the `/register` response beyond HTTPX's default timeout.

The production failure was observed once in the archived deployment. A controlled recurrence rate is not yet available; the same-run P0/P2 groups are the available negative controls.

#### Expected behavior

Transient bootstrap unavailability during worker initialization should be retried with bounded backoff and a configurable timeout. Worker registration should eventually succeed once rank 0 is responsive.

#### Actual behavior

A non-`ConnectError` registration exception is treated as fatal. The affected worker listener exits before setting its ready event, while its caller waits on that event without a timeout or inspection of the failed Future. The distributed service therefore cannot finish startup or fail cleanly.

#### Suggested fix

- Give bootstrap registration an explicit, configurable timeout.
- Retry `httpx.TimeoutException` as well as `httpx.ConnectError`, with bounded backoff and a clear final error containing the exception type.
- Make `/register` idempotent for an identical `(engine_id, dp_rank, tp_rank, pp_rank, addr)` payload. This is important because a client timeout can happen after the server records the registration but before the response reaches the client; the current duplicate-registration path returns HTTP 400.
- Retain and inspect the Future returned by `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe()`, and replace the unbounded `ready_event.wait()` with a bounded wait so registration failures propagate and startup fails cleanly instead of hanging.
- Log the exception type and traceback (for example, with `logger.exception`) rather than only `str(e)`.
- Add tests where the bootstrap response is delayed for more than five seconds and the client eventually registers successfully, and where terminal registration failure cannot leave `register_kv_caches()` waiting forever.

I searched existing open and closed issues for Mooncake bootstrap registration failures and HTTPX timeouts. The existing `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` reports concern runtime transfer/restart behavior rather than this startup registration race.

[Feature]: Switch Python Harmony dependency to oss-harmony

### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Summary
vLLM’s **Rust** path already uses [`oss-harmony`](https://github.com/oss-harmony/harmony) `v0.0.11` (`rust/Cargo.toml`, #46799). Python still depends on PyPI [`openai-harmony`](https://pypi.org/project/openai-harmony/), which is stuck at **0.0.8**.
Please switch the Python dependency to **`oss-harmony >= 0.0.11`** (same import name: `openai_harmony`) so serving, parsers, and tests share one Harmony implementation and air-gapped GPT-OSS no longer has to download tiktoken vocabs at runtime.
This is **not** a duplicate of #46799 (Rust only) or of docs-only work around `TIKTOKEN_*` (#22525). There is no open PR that migrates the **Python** package.
## Why `oss-harmony` instead of `openai-harmony`
1. **Air-gapped / offline load works.** Official `openai-harmony==0.0.8` downloads the tiktoken vocab at `load_harmony_encoding(...)`. With no network that fails as `HarmonyError: error downloading or loading vocab file`. `oss-harmony==0.0.11` **embeds** the vocabs (`include_bytes!` + zstd). GPT-OSS Harmony encoding loads with **no** `TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE` / cache env vars.
2. **Unblocks [openai/harmony#101](https://github.com/openai/harmony/issues/101).** That issue (vendor vocabs for offline use) is still **open**; upstream has not shipped a PyPI release past 0.0.8. oss-harmony already shipped the fix.
3. **Same public Python API.** Drop-in `openai_harmony` module: `load_harmony_encoding`, `Message`, `Conversation`, `SystemContent`, `StreamableParser`, `ToolNamespaceConfig`, `render_*`, `parse_messages_from_completion_tokens`, stop tokens, `is_special_token`, etc. vLLM call sites do not need a rewrite just to swap the wheel.
4. **Align Python with Rust.** One Harmony version and one render/parse behavior across the engine, instead of Python 0.0.8 vs Rust 0.0.11 (#46800 already noted that split).
5. **Parser coverage for both header layouts.** 0.0.11 parses **recipient-first** (0.0.8 / training-style) **and** **channel-first** commentary tool calls, including `<|constrain|>` adjacent to `to=...`.
6. **Correct `<|constrain|>` tokenization on render.** If `content_type` is set (vLLM does this for JSON/code tool probes), 0.0.8 emits a **literal** ` json` / ` code` string. 0.0.11 emits the **`<|constrain|>` special token**, which matches how the format is defined.
7. **No extra runtime HTTP for Harmony itself.** Removes a surprising network dependency from first GPT-OSS request / encoding load (CI, air-gap, HPC, locked-down clusters).
8. **Maintained fork used in production-shaped stacks.** oss-harmony is what vLLM Rust already pinned; Python should not be the outlier.
### Known render delta (accepted)
Commentary-channel messages (function tools, not python/browser on `analysis`) render **channel-first** in 0.0.11:
```text
# openai-harmony 0.0.8
<|start|>assistant to=functions.get_weather<|channel|>commentary<|message|>...
# oss-harmony 0.0.11
<|start|>assistant<|channel|>commentary to=functions.get_weather<|message|>...
```
Python/browser **analysis** headers are **unchanged**. System/developer/user renders were **byte-identical** in a 0.0.8 vs 0.0.11 comparison. Parsing of both layouts still yields the same `recipient` / `channel` for routing.
## `gpt-oss` package
[`gpt-oss`](https://github.com/openai/gpt-oss) is **not** a default vLLM install dep. It is a **test extra** (`requirements/test/*.in`) and is only needed for:
- `--tool-server demo` wrappers (`SimpleBrowserTool`, `PythonTool`)
- `python -m gpt_oss.evals` (e.g. GPQA)
Serving GPT-OSS **models** only needs Harmony (`openai_harmony`), not the `gpt-oss` dist.
**Packaging catch:** PyPI `gpt-oss` still `Requires-Dist: openai-harmony`. Both wheels export `openai_harmony`, so installing **both** overwrites the module. vLLM should:
- Depend on `oss-harmony >= 0.0.11`
- **Exclude** `openai-harmony` when resolving test extras (`uv` `exclude-dependencies` / `uv pip compile --excludes`)
`uv pip check` may still warn that `gpt-oss` wanted `openai-harmony`. That is **metadata only**; imports work because `oss-harmony` provides `openai_harmony`.
### `gpt-oss` functional check (clone `openai/gpt-oss` 0.0.9)
Installed the clone with **only** `oss-harmony==0.0.11` (no `openai-harmony`):
- Harmony-using modules import: Responses API, `PythonTool`, `SimpleBrowserTool`, ollama inference helper
- **`pytest tests/` → 22 passed** (skipped live browser backend)
- Compared 0.0.8 vs 0.0.11 on the exact message shapes gpt-oss builds:
  - **No API removed.** Routing on `recipient` (`python`, `browser.*`, `functions.*`) still works
  - System / developer / user / **analysis** python+browser renders **identical**
  - Model-style completion tokens in **both** header orders parse to the same route
  - Only **commentary** function-call / function-output **re-render** changes (Responses API multi-turn, `chat.py --raw`)
Not run (need Docker / network / weights, not missing Harmony APIs): live `PythonTool.process`, Exa/You.com browser, GPU `chat.py`.
## How this was tested (vLLM Harmony swap)
Isolated **`openai-harmony==0.0.8`** vs **`oss-harmony==0.0.11`** (0.0.8 vocab loaded via `TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE` so official package could run at all).
**vLLM unit tests** (same files, both packages):
- `tests/parser/test_harmony.py`
- `tests/entrypoints/openai/parser/test_harmony_utils.py`
- `tests/entrypoints/openai/parser/test_harmony_render_parity.py`
- `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_harmony_utils.py`
**258 passed** on both 0.0.8 and 0.0.11. GPU e2e `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_harmony.py` was **not** run.
**Additional probes:**
- Offline `load_harmony_encoding(HarmonyEncodingName.HARMONY_GPT_OSS)` on 0.0.11 with **no** tiktoken env
- Render/parse of commentary vs analysis tool calls; gpt-oss-style messages without `content_type` (gpt-oss never sets it; vLLM does for some probes)
- `gpt-oss==0.0.8` + `oss-harmony==0.0.11` with `--excludes openai-harmony`: `gpt_oss`, demo tools, `gpt_oss.evals`, encoding load all **OK**; `uv pip check` fails on declared dep only
## Proposed Python change (sketch)
- `requirements/common.txt`: `oss-harmony >= 0.0.11` (replace `openai-harmony >= 0.0.3`)
- Test lockfiles: pin `oss-harmony==0.0.11`, do not pin `openai-harmony`
- When compiling/installing test reqs that pull `gpt-oss`, exclude `openai-harmony` so the official wheel cannot shadow `openai_harmony`
- Optional: `[tool.uv] exclude-dependencies = ["openai-harmony"]` (single `[tool.uv]` table)
Happy to follow up with a PR if this direction is OK.
## References
- oss-harmony: https://github.com/oss-harmony/harmony (`v0.0.11`)
- openai/harmony#101 (vocab download / air-gap)
- vLLM #46799 (Rust → oss-harmony)
- vLLM #22525 (`TIKTOKEN_*` workaround docs)
- vLLM #23567 (discussion of forking / inlining Harmony)
- gpt-oss: https://github.com/openai/gpt-oss (declares `openai-harmony`; runtime uses `openai_harmony`)

### Alternatives

**1. Wait for official `openai-harmony` (tried; stalled)**
I filed [openai/harmony#101](https://github.com/openai/harmony/issues/101) (2026-03-10) asking upstream to make Harmony offline-first: bundle the `.tiktoken` vocabs in the package, ship the same files in GPT-OSS model repos, and add a deterministic lookup order (explicit path → env → model dir → package resources → optional download). That is the real fix for air-gapped GPT-OSS (`HarmonyError: error downloading or loading vocab file`).
There was **no OpenAI review or implementation**. I pinged `@scott-oai` on 2026-03-23; still no response. PyPI `openai-harmony` remains at **0.0.8**. Related offline issues ([#46](https://github.com/openai/harmony/issues/46), [#95](https://github.com/openai/harmony/issues/95)) are likewise still open. Treating `openai-harmony` as a supported dependency for vLLM is not realistic on the evidence: no release that embeds vocabs, no engagement on the air-gap design, and vLLM already had to document a `TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE` workaround (#22525).
**2. Keep `openai-harmony` and tell operators to vendor vocabs**
This is the current path. It works only if someone copies `o200k_base.tiktoken` / `cl100k_base.tiktoken` into the image and sets env vars. It is easy to miss until runtime, duplicates packaging in every air-gapped deploy, and leaves Python on 0.0.8 while Rust is already on oss-harmony 0.0.11.
**3. Vendor / inline Harmony inside vLLM**
Discussed in #23567. Higher maintenance than depending on the existing drop-in fork.
**4. Switch Python to `oss-harmony` (preferred)**
@bbrowning replied on #101 that the fork would **embed the vocabs with zstd** ([oss-harmony/harmony#7](https://github.com/oss-harmony/harmony/pull/7)). That shipped in `oss-harmony` 0.0.11 — the same crate vLLM Rust already pins (#46799). Same `openai_harmony` import; no `TIKTOKEN_*` required. This alternative is what actually landed, because upstream `openai-harmony` is not being maintained for this use case.
