[Bug]: MiniMax-M3 fails to start with transformers 5.18.0: MiniMaxM3VLVideoProcessor._preprocess() missing 'do_convert_rgb'

### Your current environment

- vLLM `main` (reproduced on 0.20.2rc1.dev6026+ga6939e710 and on upstream `main` @ aee8fe202a). Any build that resolves transformers 5.18.0 is affected.
- transformers **5.18.0** (released 2026-09-30). transformers 5.17.0 works.
- Seen on NVIDIA VR200 (aarch64) and R100 (x86_64) with CUDA 13.4. The failure is in the multimodal processor, so it is not hardware-specific. The minimal repro below runs on CPU.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`vllm serve nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` (also `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3`) fails during engine startup, while vLLM profiles multimodal memory with a dummy video:

```text
ValueError: Failed to apply MiniMaxVLProcessor on data={'text': ']<]video[>[', 'videos': [array(...)]} ...
  File ".../transformers/video_processing_utils.py", line 270, in preprocess
TypeError: MiniMaxM3VLVideoProcessor._preprocess() missing 1 required positional argument: 'do_convert_rgb'
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above.
```

Minimal reproducer (CPU only):

```python
import torch
from vllm.transformers_utils.processors.minimax_m3 import MiniMaxM3VLVideoProcessor

video = torch.randint(0, 255, (4, 3, 224, 224), dtype=torch.uint8)
MiniMaxM3VLVideoProcessor()(videos=[video], return_tensors="pt")
# transformers 5.18.0: TypeError: MiniMaxM3VLVideoProcessor._preprocess() missing 1 required positional argument: 'do_convert_rgb'
# transformers 5.17.0: works
```

`tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_minimax_m3.py` also fails on transformers 5.18.0 (`test_video_tokens_increase_with_max_long_side_pixel` and `test_video_volumetric_cap_raises`).

**Cause.** transformers 5.18.0 moved RGB conversion out of `BaseVideoProcessor._preprocess()`. In 5.18, `preprocess()` pops `do_convert_rgb` and hands it to `_prepare_input_videos()`, and `_preprocess()` no longer receives it ([5.17](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.17.0/src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py#L302-L305) vs [5.18](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.18.0/src/transformers/video_processing_utils.py#L247-L278)). vLLM's `MiniMaxM3VLVideoProcessor._preprocess()` in `vllm/transformers_utils/processors/minimax_m3.py` still declares `do_convert_rgb: bool` as a required argument, even though it never uses it.

**Why CI didn't catch it.** The test requirements pin `transformers==5.17.0` (`requirements/test/{cuda,cpu,rocm}.txt`), but `requirements/common.txt` allows `transformers >= 5.10.4`. Fresh `pip install vllm` and Docker image builds therefore get 5.18.0.

**Workaround.** Install `transformers==5.17.0`.

[Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash (Glm5Next): common non-square images (4032x3024, 3840x2160, A4 at 300 dpi) are refused with "exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size 7921"

### Your current environment

vLLM `0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b` (source commit 385dce36bcee42309924a5ece951a96db3dce7f2), `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` at revision `423acf37583782c51c142d145aef733d72943d93`, two DGX Spark (GB10) nodes, `max_num_batched_tokens` 2048, vision enabled (image only). The sizing code below is unchanged on main as of 4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Valid images that the model's own processor accepts are rejected with HTTP 400:

```
The decoder prompt contains a(n) image item with 7950 embedding tokens, which exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size 7921. Please reduce the input size or increase the encoder cache size by setting --limit-mm-per-prompt at startup.
```

It is deterministic and it hits ordinary images. A typical phone photo (4032×3024), a 4K frame (3840×2160) and an A4 page at 300 dpi (3508×2480) all fail, while a square image of nearly the same size passes. Reproduced with generated images (script below), one request per image, `max_tokens` 8; the same seven results on two serving configurations:

| image | HTTP | tokens |
|---|---|---|
| 2560×1440 (QHD) | 200 | prompt 4,802 |
| 3000×3000 (square) | 200 | prompt 7,939 |
| 5000×2000 | 200 | prompt 7,858 |
| 4032×3024 (phone photo, 4:3) | **400** | image item 7,931 |
| 3840×2160 (4K, 16:9) | **400** | image item 7,973 |
| 3508×2480 (A4 at 300 dpi) | **400** | image item 7,950 |
| 2600×2400 | **400** | image item 7,998 |

(The accepted rows' prompt tokens are the image tokens plus 18 text tokens: 4,784, 7,921 and 7,840 image tokens.)

**Cause, as far as I can tell**

- The checkpoint's `processor_config.json` declares `max_image_tokens: 8000`, so the processor budget is `max_pixels = 8000 × 28 × 28 × 2 = 12,544,000`.
- The encoder cache is sized from `get_max_image_tokens()`, which uses `get_image_size_with_most_features()`. `Glm5NextProcessingInfo` (`vllm/models/glm5next/common/multimodal.py`) does not override it, so it inherits `Glm4vProcessingInfo`'s `_get_vision_info(image_width=9999999, image_height=9999999, num_frames=1, ...)`. A **square** input resolves to 2492×2492, i.e. 89×89 = **7,921** tokens.
- `smart_resize` in `vllm/transformers_utils/processors/glm5next.py` aligns each side upward to a multiple of 28 and then fits the canvas under the pixel budget, so other aspect ratios end on more tokens under the same budget. Calling it with t=2, factors 28 and `max_pixels=12_544_000` gives exactly the "image item" counts above (7,931 / 7,973 / 7,950 / 7,998), and 8,000 at most over aspect ratios.

So the real per-item maximum is 8,000 (the declared `max_image_tokens`), but the cache is sized for 7,921, and any image that lands in 7,922–8,000 tokens is refused by the `num_embeds > self.mm_encoder_cache_size` check in `vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py`.

This is the same class as #34040 (GLM-4V / GLM-OCR, encoder cache underestimation), whose fix set `num_frames=1`; the remaining gap is that the most-features size is still a single square.

**Reproduction**

Serve GLM-5.3-Flash with vision enabled, then run the script (Pillow and the standard library only; the images are generated, nothing to attach):

```
python repro_encoder_cache.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model <served model name>
```

<details><summary>repro_encoder_cache.py</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Synthetic-image reproduction: GLM-5.3 (Glm5Next) refuses images of 7,922-8,000 tokens.

Needs only Pillow and the standard library. Every image is generated here (a gradient with its own size
written on it), so nothing has to be attached. One request per image, a one-line prompt, max_tokens 8.

    python repro_encoder_cache.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model <served model name> [--out result.json]

An image whose processed size is N tokens is accepted when N <= the server's encoder cache (7,921 here) and
refused with HTTP 400 ("... image item with N embedding tokens, which exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache
size 7921 ...") otherwise, although the checkpoint's processor allows up to max_image_tokens = 8000.
"""

import argparse
import base64
import io
import json
import re
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

# (width, height, what it stands for)
SIZES = [
    (2560, 1440, "QHD"),
    (3000, 3000, "square, above the budget (processed to 2492x2492)"),
    (5000, 2000, "5:2"),
    (4032, 3024, "typical phone photo (4:3)"),
    (3840, 2160, "4K (16:9)"),
    (3508, 2480, "A4 at 300 dpi"),
    (2600, 2400, "13:12"),
]


def make_image(width, height):
    gray = Image.linear_gradient("L").resize((width, height))
    image = Image.merge(
        "RGB",
        (gray, Image.new("L", (width, height), 128), gray.transpose(Image.Transpose.ROTATE_180)),
    )
    try:
        font = ImageFont.load_default(size=max(24, width // 12))
    except TypeError:  # Pillow < 10.1 has a fixed-size default font
        font = ImageFont.load_default()
    ImageDraw.Draw(image).text((width // 20, height // 3), f"{width}x{height}", fill="white", font=font)
    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    image.save(buffer, "JPEG", quality=80)
    return "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode()


def ask(base_url, model, data_url, timeout):
    body = {
        "model": model,
        "max_tokens": 8,
        "temperature": 0,
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": [
                    {"type": "text", "text": "Reply with OK."},
                    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": data_url}},
                ],
            }
        ],
    }
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        base_url.rstrip("/") + "/v1/chat/completions",
        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout) as response:
            usage = json.load(response)["usage"]
            return 200, {"prompt_tokens": usage["prompt_tokens"]}
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        message = json.loads(error.read().decode())["error"]["message"]
        found = re.search(r"with (\d+) embedding tokens.*cache size (\d+)", message)
        return error.code, {"image_tokens": int(found[1]), "encoder_cache_size": int(found[2])} if found else {"message": message}


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--base-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:8000")
    parser.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--out")
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=600)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    rows = []
    print(f"{'image':>11}  {'HTTP':>4}  detail")
    for width, height, note in SIZES:
        status, detail = ask(args.base_url, args.model, make_image(width, height), args.timeout)
        rows.append({"width": width, "height": height, "note": note, "http": status, **detail})
        print(f"{width}x{height:<5}  {status:>4}  {detail}  # {note}")
    if args.out:
        with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            json.dump(rows, handle, indent=1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

[Bug]: MoE LoRA one-shot path rejects max_lora_rank=256 although LoRAConfig accepts it

## Environment

- vLLM: `0.28.1rc1.dev344+ge6eb9074e`
- vLLM commit: `e6eb9074e9f1fce6115dc036b40d07ebaa926979`
- The relevant config, dispatch, and assertion are unchanged on current main
  `bb363db9a5ec2edc7b39e99b00af363a89d1fb81` as of 2026-09-03. The full
  end-to-end reproduction below was run on `e6eb9074e`.
- GPU: `2 x NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB`
- Base model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16`
  - revision: `bf77c3174f68ad409e1c2aa60daeb46e32d1c606`
- Adapter: `ace-nguyen/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16-dummy-moe-lora`
  - revision: `c7a2f3395ad0d9612edaa9ff6a2975a4a8bab921`
  - actual adapter rank: `4`

## Reproduction

Run the same public model and adapter twice, changing only
`--max-lora-rank`.

### Control: rank 128

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve \
  nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-lora \
  --lora-modules \
    dummy=ace-nguyen/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16-dummy-moe-lora \
  --max-lora-rank 128 \
  --max-model-len 2048 \
  --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \
  --trust-remote-code
```

After the server becomes ready, send a short LoRA request:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "dummy",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly OK."}],
    "temperature": 0,
    "max_completion_tokens": 8
  }'
```

Observed control result: the server starts, logs `Using fused MoE LoRA
implementation`, and the LoRA request returns HTTP 200.

### Failing case: rank 256

Stop the control server and run the same command with only this change:

```diff
-  --max-lora-rank 128 \
+  --max-lora-rank 256 \
```

The engine fails during initialization/warm-up, before the API server becomes
ready:

```text
AssertionError: fused_moe_lora_one_shot supports max_lora_rank<=128; got rank=256
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'fused_moe_lora_one_shot supports max_lora_rank<=128; got rank=256'
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
```

Both tensor-parallel workers hit the same assertion.

## Observed behavior

`LoRAConfig` accepts `max_lora_rank=256`, but the selected non-fully-sharded
fused MoE-LoRA one-shot path rejects the padded maximum rank during engine
warm-up. This makes the entire server fail to start even though the loaded
adapter's actual rank is only 4.

## Expected behavior

One of the following should happen:

1. Ranks greater than 128 are routed to a compatible fallback implementation;
2. the one-shot implementation tiles the rank dimension; or
3. vLLM rejects this model/path/configuration combination before model loading
   with an intentional, actionable `ValueError`.

An accepted global LoRA configuration should not reach a raw assertion after
the model weights have been loaded.

## Why this is inconsistent

`LoRAConfig.MaxLoRARanks` includes `256`, `320`, and `512`:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e6eb9074e9f1fce6115dc036b40d07ebaa926979/vllm/config/lora.py#L27-L35

For non-fully-sharded MoE LoRA, dispatch reaches the one-shot implementation
without a `max_lora_rank > 128` fallback:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e6eb9074e9f1fce6115dc036b40d07ebaa926979/vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py#L1479-L1524

The one-shot wrapper then asserts that the rank is at most 128:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e6eb9074e9f1fce6115dc036b40d07ebaa926979/vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py#L345-L354

The source comment explains the kernel-local restriction, but this restriction
is not reflected in validation or dispatch.

## Suggested fix direction

- Route ranks greater than 128 to the existing shrink/expand path, including
  its `add_inputs=False` callers.
- Alternatively, add a model/path-aware initialization check before loading
  model weights.
- Longer term, implement rank tiling in the one-shot kernel.

A regression test should cover the boundary:

- rank 128 continues to use the one-shot path;
- rank 256 either completes through a supported fallback or fails early with
  an intentional validation error;
- cover normal and dual-stream MoE-LoRA dispatch if both use this path.

## Related, but not duplicates

- PR #42290 introduced the one-shot MoE-LoRA kernel. Review comments already
  noted that rank greater than 128 should fall back to the legacy path and that
  dual-stream dispatch needed the same guard, but the merged implementation
  still asserts:
  - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42290#discussion_r3216969192
  - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42290#discussion_r3216969204
- Issue #40038 uses the same model and dummy adapter on A100, but reports a
  mixed base/LoRA batch metadata OOB after startup. It was fixed by #40131 and
  is distinct from this rank-dependent startup assertion:
  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40038
- Issue #3934 is an older, closed general LoRA rank request and does not track
  the current fused MoE one-shot dispatch behavior:
  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/3934
- PR #44147 is a FlashInfer MoE-LoRA backend and its public tests do not cover
  rank 256:
  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44147

No exact open issue or fix PR was found as of 2026-09-03.

## Workaround

If all loaded adapters have actual rank at most 128, configure
`--max-lora-rank 128` (or lower). `--fully-sharded-loras` may bypass the
one-shot path when expert parallelism is disabled, but it has not been
validated with this reproduction and is not compatible with expert parallelism.

[Bug]: Responses API streaming regenerates output item id/call_id in response.completed (breaks strict clients)

### Your current environment

- vLLM version: **v0.29.0** (`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0`)
- Model: Qwen3.8 family (tool calling enabled)
- Endpoint: OpenAI-compatible **Responses API** — `/v1/responses` with `stream: true`
- Client: strict OpenAI Responses consumer (a third-party agent runner)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

When streaming `/v1/responses`, items delivered through `response.output_item.added` / `response.output_item.done` carry stable identifiers, but the terminal `response.completed` payload **regenerates** them (new `id`, new `call_id`). A client that correlates streamed items to the final payload therefore observes an identity change and aborts the run.

### Reproduction

POST `/v1/responses` with `stream: true`, one function tool, and a prompt that forces a tool call:

```json
{
  "model": "<served-model>",
  "stream": true,
  "input": "Call the get_weather tool for Paris. You must call the tool now.",
  "tools": [{
    "type": "function",
    "name": "get_weather",
    "description": "get weather",
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}
  }]
}
```

Observed stream (ids shown):

```
response.output_item.added idx=0 type=reasoning     id=89d3c2a7e9e2f1cd call_id=None
response.output_item.done  idx=0 type=reasoning     id=89d3c2a7e9e2f1cd
response.output_item.added idx=1 type=function_call id=86c1dbf1a8fefbcf call_id=call_951f53b107639ed7
response.output_item.done  idx=1 type=function_call id=86c1dbf1a8fefbcf call_id=call_951f53b107639ed7
response.completed         pos=0 type=reasoning     id=rs_b540917d7602e6c3 call_id=None
response.completed         pos=1 type=function_call id=fc_bebd3a7f583cf8e4 call_id=chatcmpl-tool-878dd447ef4d81ef
```

`added`/`done` are self-consistent, but `response.completed` **changes both `id` and `call_id`**: `call_951f…` → `chatcmpl-tool-878d…` and `86c1db…` → `fc_bebd…`.

### Expected behavior

`response.completed` should reuse the exact `id` and `call_id` that were streamed in `response.output_item.added` / `.done` for each item, and keep each item's `type` / `output_index` stable across the whole stream (as the OpenAI Responses API guarantees).

### Impact

Deterministic on every function-call turn. Strict clients fail with an "output item identity changed" / `responses_output_identity_conflict`-style error (guards that compare the first-seen item `type`/`call_id` for an `output_index` against later events). Reproduced on v0.29.0; also present on v0.28.0.

### Workaround

A proxy-side rewrite of the terminal payload (restoring the streamed ids) mitigates this, but the correct fix is server-side: keep item identity stable end-to-end.

[Bug]: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 breaks DeepEncoder models (DeepSeek-OCR family): mean_batch_invariant returns float32, LayerNorm2d then feeds fp32 into a bf16 conv2d

### Your current environment

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:unlimited-ocr` (arm64 digest `sha256:2935d4d261b7972060c358d86b8811bc04ee484526a0fc265ad9fad92bde2e0e`), vLLM `v0.23.1rc1.dev541+g7aaf016a1`
- GPU: NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark class), single GPU
- Model: `baidu/Unlimited-OCR` @ `07dea832e22aefee32ad281d4b80551282e1c168` (bf16), served per the official recipe

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` the engine fails during memory profiling, after the weights load:

```
RuntimeError: Input type (torch.cuda.FloatTensor) and weight type (CUDABFloat16Type) should be the same
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/conv.py", line 134, in _forward_conv
    x = F.conv2d(
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above.
```

The same command **without** `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` starts and serves normally (and three greedy reads of the same page are byte-identical with `--max-num-seqs 1`).

**Root cause.** Batch-invariant mode registers `aten::mean.dim` -> `mean_batch_invariant`, which casts its input to float32 and returns float32 regardless of the input dtype:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a160c6fe5910957a0feac50074ec6fc183c2a92/vllm/model_executor/determinism/batch_invariant.py#L899-L920

`aten::mean` returns the input dtype when `dtype` is not given, so this override changes the dtype seen by model code. DeepEncoder's `LayerNorm2d` computes `u = x.mean(1, keepdim=True)`; `x - u` then promotes the activations to float32, and the following `conv2d` (bf16 weights) raises:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a160c6fe5910957a0feac50074ec6fc183c2a92/vllm/model_executor/models/deepencoder.py#L221-L226

Any model whose code calls `Tensor.mean` on bf16/fp16 activations and feeds the result into a dtype-strict op (conv, or a matmul outside the overridden set) is exposed; DeepSeek-OCR / DeepSeek-OCR-2 / Unlimited-OCR share this `LayerNorm2d`.

**Suggested fix.** Keep the float32 accumulation for determinism, but return the input dtype unless a dtype was requested (matching `aten::mean` semantics), e.g. at the end of `mean_batch_invariant`:

```python
    return result if dtype is not None else result.to(input.dtype)
```

### Reproduce

```bash
docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc host -e VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 vllm/vllm-openai:unlimited-ocr \
  baidu/Unlimited-OCR --trust-remote-code \
  --logits_processors vllm.model_executor.models.unlimited_ocr:NGramPerReqLogitsProcessor \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --mm-processor-cache-gb 0
```

The function and the `LayerNorm2d` above are unchanged on `main` as of 7a160c6fe5.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched existing issues for `mean_batch_invariant` / batch invariant + conv2d dtype; found none.

- vLLM: `v0.30.0`
- Container: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0`
- Model: `Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound`


`Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound` fails during model initialization on stock vLLM `v0.30.0`.

The checkpoint uses AutoRound / INC quantization for the model body, but the Qwen3.8 PLE embedding is intentionally left unquantized.

vLLM passes the model-level `INCConfig` to `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config()`. The PLE implementation does not recognize `INCConfig`, so initialization fails before weights are loaded:

```text

    embedding_quant_method = Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config(

    raise NotImplementedError(

NotImplementedError: Qwen4Exp PLE embedding does not support quantization config INCConfig
```

This happens on both TP workers.

The rest of the AutoRound path appears to initialize correctly before the failure. In particular, the checkpoint is recognized as INC and the expected W4A16 MoE backend is selected:

```text
Using 'MARLIN' WNA16 MoE backend.
```

### Reproduction

A minimal reproduction should be possible with the public Intel checkpoint:

```bash
vllm serve Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
    --enable-expert-parallel
```

My production configuration additionally uses long context, prefix caching, chunked prefill and MTP, but the exception occurs during model construction before those features are relevant.

### Expected behavior

The model should load successfully.

For an AutoRound/INC checkpoint where the PLE embedding itself is not quantized, the PLE layer should use the unquantized PLE embedding implementation rather than rejecting the model-level `INCConfig`.

Conceptually, this case seems equivalent to:

```python
if isinstance(quant_config, INCConfig):
    # PLE is excluded from AutoRound quantization in this checkpoint.
    return Qwen4ExpPLEUnquantizedEmbeddingMethod()
```

The exact implementation should probably verify the per-layer/checkpoint quantization metadata rather than assuming that every INC checkpoint necessarily has an unquantized PLE.

### Why this seems to be a PLE quantization-dispatch issue

The checkpoint is a mixed layout:

- the main model uses AutoRound W4A16 / `INCConfig`;
- PLE is not quantized by the AutoRound recipe;
- nevertheless, PLE method selection receives the model-level `INCConfig`;
- `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config()` interprets that config as if it described the PLE table itself and rejects it.

There are similar mixed-quantization PLE issues for Qwen4Exp where the body quantization config does not directly describe the PLE representation, e.g. #54765 and #56272.

### Workaround tested

As a diagnostic workaround, I patched `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config()` so that `INCConfig` selects the unquantized PLE method.

With that change, the model gets past the original exception and proceeds to initialize:

```text
Resolved Engram configuration:
EngramConfig(cpu_offload=True, embedding_across_dp=False, dp_shared_memory=False)

Using 'MARLIN' WNA16 MoE backend.
```

So the INC W4A16/MARLIN path itself is not the source of this particular exception.

I would prefer an upstream fix that determines the PLE representation correctly from the checkpoint/layer metadata rather than relying on this local workaround.

### Additional context

The older dedicated image `vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next` successfully serves this exact checkpoint on the same 2x A100 system.

That image uses the older separate PLE offload worker implementation, so this appears to be a compatibility regression/coverage gap in the newer Qwen4Exp PLE/Engram implementation rather than an unsupported AutoRound checkpoint in general.

[Bug] GLM-5.3-Flash with TP=1 per rank (DP4) fails at CUDA-graph capture in fused_recurrent_kda: grid.z = batch x 64 heads exceeds 65535

### Your current environment

- vLLM nightly `0.28.1rc1.dev681+ge7edf17ce` (2026-09-11, also reproduced on `dev628+g2a02f6efe`, 2026-09-10), image `vllm/vllm-openai` nightly aarch64, torch 2.13 + cu130
- 1 tray of GB200 NVL72 (4× GB200, SM100, 184 GiB each)
- Model `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (FP8 checkpoint), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 16384`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

GLM-5.3-Flash served with TP=1 per rank — in our case `--data-parallel-size 4` with or without `--enable-expert-parallel`, i.e. the recipe's `single_node_dep` strategy, at the default CUDA-graph capture sizes (max 1024) — dies during engine start-up at the first CUDA-graph capture, on every DP worker:

```
File ".../vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py", line 686, in forward
File ".../vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/kda.py", line 571, in _forward
File ".../vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/third_party/kda/kernels.py", line 178, in fused_recurrent_kda
File ".../vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/third_party/kda/kernels.py", line 99, in fused_recurrent_kda_fwd
RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument
```

(called from `determine_available_memory → profile_cudagraph_memory → capture_model`, `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`). TP4 / TP4+EP start fine.

**Root cause.** `fused_recurrent_kda_fwd` launches `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel` with `grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)`. CUDA limits `gridDim.z` to 65535. GLM-5.3-Flash has 64 KDA value heads; at TP=1 (every DP rank) all 64 heads are on one GPU and the first (largest) capture batch is 1024 sequences, so `N * HV = 1024 * 64 = 65536`, one over the limit, and `cuLaunchKernel` fails with `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE`. The condition is `N * HV > 65535` for the largest captured batch: with TP4 each rank owns 16 heads (`1024 * 16 = 16384`), so the TP strategies do not reach it at the default capture sizes; any configuration that does (more heads per rank, a larger max capture size, other models with this kernel) would. The same `grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)` pattern is in the AMD copy and in `third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/{fused_recurrent,fused_sigmoid_gating,kda}.py`; the packed-decode kernel in the same file already guards this case (`split_batch_head_grid = B * HV > 65535`), the recurrent varlen path does not.

**Fix.** Put `N * HV` in `gridDim.x` (limit 2^31-1) and swap the `program_id` mapping in the kernel — PR to follow.

**Workarounds.** `--max-cudagraph-capture-size 1008` (any value ≤ 1023), `--max-num-seqs ≤ 1023`, or TP ≥ 2.

### Reproduction

```
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 16384
```
on 4× GB200 (or `--data-parallel-size 4` without EP). Reproduced 3/3 on two consecutive nightlies; a single-GPU TP=1 attempt ran out of memory before capture on our 184 GiB GPUs, so DP is the practical trigger.

+            compute_gate=True,
+            lower_bound=-5.0,
+            out=out,
+        )

+    full_out = torch.zeros_like(k)

[Bug]: NIXL: heartbeats do not refresh `engine_ttl`, so a decode instance evicts and re-handshakes a prefill engine it is waiting on

### Your current environment

- Code references are to `main` at `5f30fc7031`. The deployment ran a build based on `e33de821` with NIXL 1.3.2 and UCX 1.21.x.
- Disaggregated P/D. Decode is TP2 with `NixlConnector` (pull). Prefill is PCP8, so each decode TP worker loads 8 remote agents per prefill engine. 96 decode ranks. UCX transports `rc`, `cuda_copy`, `cuda_ipc`.

### Describe the bug

`_engine_last_active` is stamped only when a handshake completes (`nixl/base_worker.py:1336`) and when a read is issued (`nixl/pull_worker.py:156`). `_send_heartbeats` (`nixl/base_worker.py:3220-3249`) does not stamp it. A decode instance that queues requests for a prefill engine heartbeats that engine every `kv_lease_duration // 6` seconds but reads nothing from it until the requests are scheduled. Once `engine_ttl` (3600 s) passes, the next heartbeat calls `_ensure_handshake`, which runs `_evict_stale_engines` first (`:1307`), evicts that same engine, finds it missing and submits a new handshake. So a decode instance that holds waiting requests evicts and reloads every remote agent of the engine they wait on, once per `engine_ttl`.

### Why it matters

Each reload runs `remove_remote_agent` and then `loadRemoteMD` for every remote rank. In our deployment each full re-handshake left 476-481 64 KiB UCX buffers (about 960 VMAs) behind per decode worker, which is a separate NIXL/UCX issue. A decode rank that could not admit work kept requests waiting for tens of minutes at a time. It ran about 6 handshakes per hour against about 1 per hour on healthy ranks, and it hit `vm.max_map_count` (262,144) after about 31 hours. Example from the log: one worker evicted a prefill engine as "inactive for 3604.0s" and handshaked it again 64 s later. Heartbeat-driven evictions are the part of that churn where the engine is still in use.

Reproduced on upstream `main` (`5f30fc7031` CI image, NIXL 1.4.1, UCX 1.22.0, Qwen3-0.6B, two prefill engines and one decode on two H100 nodes over RoCE): decode with `engine_ttl: 60` and `--max-num-seqs 1`, one long request from prefill 2, and one request from prefill 1 waiting behind it for about 150 s. The decode evicted and re-handshaked prefill 1 every ~62 s while it waited (handshakes 2 -> 3 -> 4), and each reconnect left 2,560 KiB more pinned memory on the decode EngineCore. With heartbeats counted as activity, no handshake happened in the same run and `VmPin` stayed flat.

### Expected behavior

An engine this instance is heartbeating is in use, so TTL eviction should skip it. #52245 stamps the same timestamp on the push-mode D side for the same reason, and #54689 skips engines with in-flight reads.

AI assistance was used to trace the code paths and draft this report.

[Performance]: Qwen4Exp skinny decode GEMM has no SM12x plans; on GB10 (DGX Spark) BF16 projections fall back to cuBLAS SM80 WMMA kernels

_Posted by Claude (AI assistant) on behalf of @sethforprivacy, as part of our local-inference tuning work._

### Summary

On SM121 (DGX Spark / GB10), `qwen4_exp_low_latency_gemm` is disabled: `_gemm_plans()` returns plans only for SM103 and SM90, keyed by TP4 local shapes. Every decode-sized BF16 projection in Qwen4Exp therefore goes through `F.linear`. On GB10, cuBLAS (CUDA 13.0, cuBLAS 13.1.1) picks SM80 WMMA kernels for these shapes, for example `cutlass_80_wmma_tensorop_bf16_s161616gemm_bf16_16x16_128x2_tn_align8`, with one warp per CTA. In our profile those GEMMs were about half of each decode step. The CuTe-DSL skinny GEMM from the same module, tuned for TP2 shapes, runs them at 240–255 GB/s.

### Setup

- vLLM 0.30.0, V2 model runner, breakable CUDA graphs (FULL decode graphs).
- `Blackfrost-AI/CYBER-FROST-3.8-NVFP4`: a ModelOpt mixed-precision Qwen3.8-Flash-Next fine-tune. The routed experts are NVFP4; every other projection is BF16.
- TP2 across two DGX Spark over RoCE. MTP with 3 speculative tokens.

### Profile (torch profiler, 1 stream, decode)

Per decode step of about 51 ms:

- About 28 ms is BF16 dense projections on the SM80 WMMA kernels, at 125–205 GB/s.
- The small projections are pure latency. `in_proj_ba` (48 x 2560) takes 12–19 us; the shared-expert gate (1 x 2560) takes up to 6.5 us.
- About 11 ms is the NVFP4 MoE.

### Tuned TP2 plans

I enabled the existing skinny GEMM for SM12x with a plan table for the TP2 local shapes. Each config was chosen by timing every valid `SkinnyGemmConfig` inside CUDA graphs, with weight copies rotated past L2. These are isolated timings in us, cuBLAS vs skinny:

| local (N, K) | role | M=1 | M=4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| (8192, 2560) | GDN in_proj_qkvz | 247.4 -> 172.7 | 187.4 -> 173.2 |
| (6656, 2560) | QSA q/k/v/gate | 201.9 -> 140.2 | 150.7 -> 141.1 |
| (2560, 3072) | GDN / QSA out | 96.0 -> 65.4 | 70.2 -> 65.1 |
| (336, 10240) | HC down + inject | 34.4 -> 28.6 | 33.9 -> 28.7 |
| (10240, 320) | HC up | 29.9 -> 27.6 | 30.2 -> 27.6 |
| (640, 2560) | shared-expert gate/up, indexer q/k | 16.3 -> 15.0 | 18.8 -> 15.0 |
| (512, 2560) | router | 13.3 -> 12.1 | 16.3 -> 12.1 |
| (48, 2560) | GDN in_proj_ba | 3.7 -> 2.6 | 18.8 -> 2.6 |
| (1, 2560) | shared-expert gate | 6.5 -> 0.9 | 2.6 -> 1.2 |
| (124160, 2560) | LM head | 3614.6 -> 2505.4 | 2644.9 -> 2513.9 |

M=1 matters because the MTP draft passes run at M=1. Plans for M=2, 8 and 16 behave the same way. For K=320 (shared-expert down, HC up), the only valid tiling is `block_size=32, vector_width=2`, and at M=16 it loses to cuBLAS. In the model, dense-GEMM time per decode step fell from 31.4 to 27.9 ms; 530 target modules and 15 MTP modules took the skinny path.

### FP8 per-channel (for checkpoint producers)

For the same projections, ModelOpt `FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN` (`CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`) beats both: (8192, 2560) runs in 98.6 us at M=4 and is 1.4x faster than BF16 at M=2048. Re-storing those layers in FP8 cut the decode step from 51 to 43 ms. Held-out NLL was unchanged: 0.3838 vs 0.3842.

### Suggestion

Add an SM12x entry to `_gemm_plans()`, keyed by the TP2 (and TP1) local shapes. The tuning script and plan table we used are available on request.

### 🐛 Describe the bug **False positive WARNING** emitted **~50 times** (once per MoE layer) when loading non-gated MoE models: ``` (Worker_TP0_EP0 pid=171) WARNING 07-19 17:54:46 [routed_experts.py:1042] Unexpected gate/up projection names: up_proj, . Fused gate/up mapping will be skipped. WARNING 07-19 17:54:47 [routed_experts.py:1042] Unexpected gate/up projection names: up_proj, . Fused gate/up mapping will be skipped. ... (repeated ~50 times total) ``` **No functional impact** — weights load correctly, model works. Only massive log noise. --- ### Root Cause Two commits combined: | Commit | Date | Role | |--------|------|------| | `1ab952293` (#47058) | ~Jul 2024 | Added warning logic in `routed_experts.py:1037-1047` — only handles `gate_proj`+`up_proj` or `w1`+`w3` | | `c233d90aa` (#48496) | **2026-07-18** | Migrated Nemotron H to new API with `ckpt_names=("up_proj", "down_proj", "")` — **triggered the warning** | **v0.25.1 (released 2026-07-12) does NOT have this bug** — `c233d90aa` was merged **6 days after** the v0.25.1 tag. The bug exists only on `main` / post-v0.25.1 dev builds. --- ### Affected Models - `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4` (served as `nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra`) - `nvidia/Nemotron-H-8B` and other Nemotron H variants - Any non-gated MoE using `ckpt_up_proj_name=""` --- ### Technical Details **File:** `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py:1037-1047` ```python if ckpt_gate_proj_name == "gate_proj" and ckpt_up_proj_name == "up_proj": gate_up = "gate_up_proj" elif ckpt_gate_proj_name == "w1" and ckpt_up_proj_name == "w3": gate_up = "w13" else: logger.warning( # ← triggers for NemotronH: ("up_proj", "down_proj", "") "Unexpected gate/up projection names: %s, %s. Fused gate/up mapping will be skipped.", ckpt_gate_proj_name, ckpt_up_proj_name ) ``` **NemotronH passes** (`vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_h.py:689-691`): ```python ckpt_names=("up_proj", "down_proj", "") # ckpt_up_proj_name = "" ``` **Why 50×?** Each `RoutedExperts` layer calls `get_expert_mapping(include_fused=True)` in its `load_weights()` → each MoE layer emits the warning once. Nemotron 3 Ultra has ~48-50 MoE layers. **Why harmless:** - Fused mapping only applies when checkpoint has pre-fused `gate_up_proj` / `w13` weights - NemotronH checkpoints have separate `up_proj` + `down_proj` → fused mapping correctly skipped - Per-expert mapping (lines 1056-1070) loads weights correctly --- ### Reproduction ```python from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams llm = LLM( model="nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4", served_model_name="nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra", tensor_parallel_size=1, ) # Observe WARNING in logs (~50 times) outputs = llm.generate(["Hello"], SamplingParams(max_tokens=10)) ``` ```bash # Or via CLI: vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4 \ --served-model-name nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 ``` --- ### Expected behavior No WARNING for non-gated MoE models. The fused mapping is correctly skipped (checkpoint doesn't have pre-fused weights), but per-expert mapping loads weights properly. --- ### Suggested fix In `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py:1037-1047`: ```python if ckpt_gate_proj_name == "gate_proj" and ckpt_up_proj_name == "up_proj": gate_up = "gate_up_proj" elif ckpt_gate_proj_name == "w1" and ckpt_up_proj_name == "w3": gate_up = "w13" elif ckpt_up_proj_name == "": # non-gated MoE (Nemotron H / Nemotron 3 Ultra) gate_up = None # explicitly skip without warning else: logger.warning(...) ``` --- ### Environment - **vLLM:** main branch (`0.23.1rc1.dev1263+gc233d90aa`, post-`c233d90aa`) - **Model:** `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4` - **Served as:** `nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra` - **GPU:** Any --- ### Labels `bug`, `moe`, `NemotronH`, `Nemotron3Ultra`, `logging`, `false-positive` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

[Bug]: Guidance `disable_additional_properties` rewrites `const` and `enum` literal values

## Your current environment

- vLLM source: `fa94450b743766d466021a40e5b5f5f5746c92b9` (upstream `main` on September 25, 2026; `backend_guidance.py` is unchanged at later `main` commit `378504a5442b8a9240b359dae3e6f75f35c38f19`)
- macOS 26.6.2 arm64; Python 3.12.13; torch 2.13.0; CPU-only validation
- llguidance 1.7.6; jsonschema 4.26.0
- No HTTP server, model weights, or GPU are needed.

Enabled with:

```bash
vllm serve <model> --structured-outputs-config '{"backend": "guidance", "disable_additional_properties": true}'
```

## 🐛 Describe the bug

With `StructuredOutputsConfig.disable_additional_properties=True`, `serialize_guidance_grammar()` ([L227-L243](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa94450b743766d466021a40e5b5f5f5746c92b9/vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_guidance.py#L227-L243)) passes the schema through [`process_for_additional_properties()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa94450b743766d466021a40e5b5f5f5746c92b9/vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_guidance.py#L76-L85) before llguidance compiles it. That function calls [`_walk_json_for_additional_properties()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa94450b743766d466021a40e5b5f5f5746c92b9/vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_guidance.py#L37-L48), which recurses into every dict and list value and applies this rule to each dict:

```python
if "additionalProperties" not in data and (
    "properties" in data or "patternProperties" in data
):
    data["additionalProperties"] = False
```

The walker does not distinguish schema nodes from instance data. An object literal under `const` or `enum` that happens to have a `properties` or `patternProperties` member is treated as a schema object, and `additionalProperties: false` is inserted into the literal value. This is a vLLM preprocessing bug: the changed schema is already visible in the output of `process_for_additional_properties()`, before llguidance sees it.

Object literals without such a member, e.g. `{"const": {"a": 1}}`, are not modified. Common data shapes do use a `properties` member, though. For example, a GeoJSON Feature. For such a literal, the only value the original `const`/`enum` allows is rejected by the compiled Guidance matcher, and the rewritten object, which the original schema rejects, is accepted instead. With the option disabled, the same schema compiles correctly.

### Minimal reproduction

Run from this vLLM checkout with the listed dependencies. The byte tokenizer lets the check run without a model and includes EOS in the matcher result:

```python
import json

import llguidance as llg
from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator
from llguidance import TokenizerWrapper

from vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_guidance import (
    process_for_additional_properties,
    serialize_guidance_grammar,
)
from vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_types import StructuredOutputOptions


class ByteTokenizer:
    eos_token_id = 256
    bos_token_id = None
    tokens = [bytes([i]) for i in range(256)] + [b"<eos>"]
    special_token_ids = [256]

    def __call__(self, value):
        return list(value if isinstance(value, bytes) else value.encode())


tokenizer = llg.LLTokenizer(TokenizerWrapper(ByteTokenizer()), slices=[])


def accepts_complete(grammar, value):
    matcher = llg.LLMatcher(tokenizer, grammar, log_level=0)
    assert not matcher.is_error(), matcher.get_error()
    tokens = list(json.dumps(value).encode()) + [tokenizer.eos_token]
    return matcher.validate_tokens(tokens) == len(tokens)


def grammar(schema, disable_additional_properties):
    return serialize_guidance_grammar(
        StructuredOutputOptions.JSON,
        json.dumps(schema),
        disable_additional_properties=disable_additional_properties,
    )


# A GeoJSON Feature; its "properties" member is instance data.
feature = {"type": "Feature", "geometry": None, "properties": {"name": "HQ"}}
changed = {**feature, "additionalProperties": False}

for keyword in ("const", "enum"):
    schema = {keyword: feature if keyword == "const" else [feature]}
    Draft202012Validator.check_schema(schema)
    flag_off, flag_on = grammar(schema, False), grammar(schema, True)
    print(json.dumps({
        "keyword": keyword,
        "prepared_schema": process_for_additional_properties(schema),
        "original_valid_by_schema": Draft202012Validator(schema).is_valid(feature),
        "original_accepted_flag_off": accepts_complete(flag_off, feature),
        "original_accepted_flag_on": accepts_complete(flag_on, feature),
        "changed_valid_by_schema": Draft202012Validator(schema).is_valid(changed),
        "changed_accepted_flag_on": accepts_complete(flag_on, changed),
    }))

# Control: an object literal without a properties/patternProperties key is untouched.
print(json.dumps({
    "control_prepared_schema": process_for_additional_properties({"const": {"a": 1}}),
}))
```

Observed results for both `const` and `enum`:

| Keyword | Original valid by schema | Original accepted, option off | Original accepted, option on | Rewritten valid by schema | Rewritten accepted, option on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `const` | `true` | `true` | `false` | `false` | `true` |
| `enum` | `true` | `true` | `false` | `false` | `true` |

`prepared_schema` shows the inserted field. For `const`, it is `{"const": {"type": "Feature", "geometry": null, "properties": {"name": "HQ"}, "additionalProperties": false}}`; `enum` changes its element the same way. The control prints `{"const": {"a": 1}}` unchanged.

### Expected behavior

- The option may add `additionalProperties: false` to object **schema nodes**, but must preserve instance values inside `const` and `enum` exactly.
- With the option on, the compiled matcher should accept the original literal and reject the rewritten value for this schema, matching the result with the option off.

A possible fix direction: recurse only into schema-valued keywords (`properties`/`patternProperties`/`$defs` values, `items`, `prefixItems`, `anyOf`/`allOf`/`oneOf`, `not`, `if`/`then`/`else`, `additionalProperties`, `contains`, `dependentSchemas`, …) and never into `const`, `enum`, `default`, or `examples`.

### Duplicate check

Searched current and past vLLM issues/PRs for `process_for_additional_properties`, `_walk_json_for_additional_properties`, `disable_additional_properties`, `disable-additional-properties`, and related Guidance `additionalProperties` terms on September 25, 2026. I found no matching report or open fix. Hits for `disable_additional_properties` only contain it inside pasted config dumps.

Guidance's `disable_additional_properties` rewrite would edit eligible schema nodes in a new document while leaving literal values under `const` and `enum` unchanged.

The RFC also calls out `not`, `if`, and `oneOf` contexts where adding `additionalProperties: false` can change validity in either direction. The literal-value fix can land as a focused incremental PR while the broader eligibility policy is reviewed.

Hi @equiluxe, I am working on a focused PR for this to ensure `_walk_json_for_additional_properties` only traverses schema-bearing keywords and leaves literal values under `const`, `enum`, `default`, and `examples` untouched.

[Bug]: Fill-in DSpark underallocates KV lookahead and can overwrite target KV (synthetic CUDA repro)

### Summary

With a DSpark checkpoint configured with `sample_from_anchor=false`, the V2 drafter writes **N+1 query positions**, but `VllmConfig.num_lookahead_tokens` reserves only **N**. At a block boundary, the last draft query reads an unallocated block-table entry. A reused table row can contain a stale physical block ID there, causing a draft write into another request's target KV cache.

**Related open fix:** #48909 addresses this query-width mismatch (currently unmerged). This report adds a weights-free synthetic CUDA reproduction and direct before/after cache-corruption evidence on a recent nightly. It is distinct from the older cache-layout issue #41262, which was closed by #42095; that fix is already included in the tested build.

### Environment

- vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev284+gbeef814e1`, commit `beef814e1d3aa1e198b604a08aa2494fad9842be`
- PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, Python 3.11.14; one NVIDIA H200
- Target: `google/gemma-4-31B-it`, BF16
- Draft: `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-speculator.dspark`, `sample_from_anchor=false`, 7 speculative tokens
- V2 runner, FlashAttention 4, TP=1, eager, async scheduling off, prefix caching off, chunked prefill off, no LoRA
- `max_model_len=8192`, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `max_num_seqs=16`, KV budget 32 GiB

The allocation/slot preparation defect below requires no model weights, tokenizer, prompts, or training data.

### Deterministic synthetic reproduction

Run this script inside the affected CUDA vLLM environment, e.g. `uv run --no-config --no-project --python /path/to/vllm-env/bin/python python repro_dspark_lookahead.py`.

The script intentionally places synthetic block ID 99 in the unused tail of a block-table row, matching the live gather behavior (which copies valid entries without clearing the rest). It only prepares slot mappings; it never accesses another process's memory or writes a real KV cache.

```python
"""Synthetic DSpark KV-slot repro: CUDA, no model weights or user prompts."""
from types import SimpleNamespace as NS

import torch
from vllm.config import VllmConfig
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.dflash.speculator import prepare_dflash_inputs

# A fill-in checkpoint: one bonus query + seven speculative queries.
prompt_len, num_spec, block_size = 137, 7, 16
spec = NS(use_dflash=lambda: False, use_dspark=lambda: True,
          use_eagle=lambda: True,
          draft_model_config=NS(hf_config=NS(sample_from_anchor=False)))
config = NS(speculative_config=spec, num_speculative_tokens=num_spec)
lookahead = VllmConfig.num_lookahead_tokens.fget(config)
num_blocks = (prompt_len + lookahead + block_size - 1) // block_size

# As in a reused live block-table row: valid IDs followed by an old ID.
# No allocations or data from another process are accessed by this reproducer.
stale_block_id = 99
block_table = torch.full((1, 32), stale_block_id, dtype=torch.int32, device='cuda')
block_table[0, :num_blocks] = torch.arange(1, num_blocks + 1, device='cuda')
max_tokens = 256

def buf(n, dtype=torch.int64):
    return torch.zeros(n, dtype=dtype, device='cuda')

inputs = NS(input_ids=buf(max_tokens, torch.int32), positions=buf(max_tokens),
            query_start_loc=buf(2, torch.int32), seq_lens=buf(1, torch.int32))
batch = NS(num_reqs=1, num_scheduled_tokens=torch.tensor([prompt_len]),
           positions=torch.arange(prompt_len, device='cuda'),
           query_start_loc=torch.tensor([0, prompt_len], dtype=torch.int32, device='cuda'),
           idx_mapping=buf(1, torch.int32))
query_slots = buf(max_tokens)
prepare_dflash_inputs(
    input_buffers=inputs,
    query_slot_mapping=query_slots,
    context_positions=buf(max_tokens),
    context_slot_mapping=buf(max_tokens),
    sample_indices=buf(num_spec),
    sample_pos=buf(num_spec),
    sample_idx_mapping=buf(num_spec, torch.int32),
    temperature=buf(1, torch.float32),
    seeds=buf(1),
    input_batch=batch,
    num_sampled=torch.ones(1, dtype=torch.int32, device='cuda'),
    num_rejected=buf(1, torch.int32),
    last_sampled=buf(1),
    next_prefill_tokens=buf(1),
    input_temperature=buf(1, torch.float32),
    input_seeds=buf(1),
    block_table=block_table,
    block_size=block_size,
    cp_rank=0, cp_size=1, cp_interleave=1,
    parallel_drafting_token_id=0,
    num_query_per_req=num_spec + 1,
    num_speculative_steps=num_spec,
    max_num_reqs=1,
    max_num_tokens=max_tokens,
    max_model_len=1024,
    sample_from_anchor=False,
)
slots = query_slots[:num_spec + 1].cpu().tolist()
blocks = [slot // block_size for slot in slots]
print({'lookahead': lookahead, 'allocated_blocks': num_blocks,
       'draft_positions': inputs.positions[:num_spec + 1].cpu().tolist(),
       'draft_slots': slots, 'draft_blocks': blocks})
assert all(1 <= block <= num_blocks for block in blocks), (
    'Draft accesses a stale/unallocated block-table entry', blocks)
print('PASS: every draft write is inside the reserved blocks')
```

Before the fix, one invocation produces:

```text
lookahead=7, allocated_blocks=9
draft_positions=[137,138,139,140,141,142,143,144]
draft_slots=[153,154,155,156,157,158,159,1584]
draft_blocks=[9,9,9,9,9,9,9,99]
AssertionError: Draft accesses a stale/unallocated block-table entry
```

With the extra lookahead slot:

```text
lookahead=8, allocated_blocks=10
draft_positions=[137,138,139,140,141,142,143,144]
draft_slots=[153,154,155,156,157,158,159,160]
draft_blocks=[9,9,9,9,9,9,9,10]
PASS
```

### Source-level cause

1. `vllm/config/vllm.py::VllmConfig.num_lookahead_tokens` gives DFlash N+1 but every DSpark checkpoint N, assuming anchor-as-prediction.
2. `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/speculator.py::DSparkSpeculator.__init__` instead sets `num_query_per_req=1+N` when `sample_from_anchor=false`.
3. `KVCacheManager.allocate_slots` reserves `computed + scheduled + lookahead`, rounded up to blocks.
4. `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` looks up all N+1 query positions. It checks table capacity, not the number of currently allocated blocks.
5. `_gather_block_tables_kernel` copies valid entries for a live row, leaving its tail unchanged.

For 137 prompt tokens, N=7 and block_size=16, the current reservation is 144 slots (positions 0..143), but the draft also writes position 144. Target and draft cache groups intentionally alias one backing allocation; their live block IDs remain disjoint. The stale lookup bypasses that isolation.

### Model-level validation

Using a fixed private workload (no prompts or generated text are included here):

- Before fix: three cold starts each reproduced malformed repetitive generation at batch 9 of up to 20, with identical output token sequences across runs.
- Read-only source instrumentation covering all 60 target layers showed the first draft pass of batch 9 overwriting active target KV blocks. The block allocator itself had no duplicate live block ownership across the 13 cache groups. Two actual draft-query slot mappings addressed blocks owned by target groups.
- After the minimal lookahead fix: **three cold starts × 20 batches × 16 requests = 960 responses**, no length-limit/corruption flags; the 320 output token sequences were identical between the three runs. On instrumented batch 9: zero invalid draft writes and zero target-KV changes across draft calls in each run.
- The same synthetic CUDA script fails before and passes after the fix.
- The regression-test selection passes 12 cases with the fix. This is bounded validation, not a claim of full semantic evaluation or bitwise equivalence to non-speculative decoding.

### Proposed fix

Use N+1 lookahead for DSpark when `sample_from_anchor=false`, retain N when true or omitted (matching the runtime default), and leave DFlash unchanged.

A minimal current-main branch with the fix and regression tests is available at https://github.com/notimesea/vllm/tree/fix/dspark-fill-in-kv-lookahead . It is provided for reproduction/testing; #48909 is the existing upstream proposed fix.

[Bug]: ngram speculative decoding default prompt_lookup_min=2 causes tool-call output corruption on Qwen3-class models with structured output (config-only fix: prompt_lookup_min=8)

### Summary

When using `--speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","prompt_lookup_min":2,...}'` (the default `prompt_lookup_min`) with a Qwen3-class model AND `tool_choice=auto` requests AND a tools array in the system prompt, **tool-call output is corrupted in ~50% of requests** even on a stack with all known related fixes applied (#40738 Phase 1+2, #36138, #40783, #39055).

The corruption manifests as wrong-token cascades like `<tool_call>\n<<tool_code>\nprint(...)`, `parameter=parameter=name`, `<<argname>...<argvalue>` instead of the correct chat-template format `<tool_call>\n<<function=NAME>\n<parameter=KEY>\nVALUE\n</parameter>...`.

**Config-only workaround (no code changes): set `prompt_lookup_min=8`. Achieves 100% clean tool-call rate (n=30 single-query, 96% n=25 multi-query) on the same hardware/model where default `prompt_lookup_min=2` gave ~50%.**

This is a separate bug class from PR #40738 (GDN state corruption, which we backported and confirmed gives +30-40% improvement). The remaining ~50% residual that the four upstream PRs don't close is the rejection-sampling artifact described here.

### Environment

- vLLM: `0.19.2rc1.dev205+g07351e088` (latest nightly tested)
- Model: `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` (hybrid linear-attention + MoE + full-attention layers)
- Hardware: 2× NVIDIA RTX A5000 (Ampere SM 8.6), TP=2
- KV cache: `turboquant_k8v4`
- Speculative config: `{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":3,"prompt_lookup_max":4,"prompt_lookup_min":2}` (defaults)
- Reasoning parser: `qwen3`
- Tool call parser: `qwen3_coder`
- `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`: `false`
- `--enable-chunked-prefill`, `--enable-prefix-caching`

### Reproducer

```python
import json
import requests

PROMPT = {
    "model": "Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Get weather for Tokyo"}],
    "tools": [{
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "get_weather",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "city": {"type": "string"},
                    "unit": {"type": "string"},
                },
            },
        },
    }],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
    "max_tokens": 150,
    "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False},
}

# Run 30 times, count clean (parsed JSON without `<<` or `parameter=` artifacts)
clean = 0
for _ in range(30):
    r = requests.post("http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions", json=PROMPT).json()
    tc = r["choices"][0]["message"]["tool_calls"]
    args = tc[0]["function"]["arguments"] if tc else ""
    if "<<" not in args and "parameter=" not in args and args.startswith("{"):
        clean += 1
print(f"clean: {clean}/30")
```

Expected with default `prompt_lookup_min=2`: ~15-16 clean (50-53%).
Expected with `prompt_lookup_min=8`: 30 clean (100%).

### How we found it (investigation methodology)

This bug was located after backporting four existing upstream PRs failed to fully close the corruption rate. The investigation timeline:

1. **First hypothesis**: TurboQuant KV cache + cudagraph capture/replay (per noonghunna's six-probe ladder at #40807 / #40831). Disproved by Probe 6 (`cudagraph_mode=NONE` works) and Probe 9 (kernel determinism via bit-equality test).

2. **Second pass**: backported #40768 (z1ying, async-scheduler placeholder fix). No measurable improvement — vLLM auto-disables async_scheduling for ngram method (vllm.py:815) so the buggy code path doesn't execute on our config.

3. **Third pass**: backported #39055 (ZenoAFfectionate, Qwen3 reasoning embedded tool_call). +20% improvement (20% → 40%) — confirmed parser-level fixes were on the right track.

4. **Fourth pass**: backported #40738 (tdoublep, GDN+ngram SSM/conv state corruption). +30-40% improvement (43-70% clean). This is the largest single fix and addresses the GDN state corruption originally reported by @bhaktatejas922 in #39273.

5. **Fifth pass**: backported #36138 (sfbemerk, structured-output spec-decode reasoning-end timing) and #40783 (ExtReMLapin, Qwen3 multi-tool first-occurrence + streaming overlap guard). Combined +3-6% additional improvement (53-56% clean). Both are correct fixes for their respective bug classes; just not our dominant residual.

6. **Token-level tracing pass** (where this bug was discovered): ran the reproducer with `return_token_ids: true` + `logprobs: true`, captured 30 responses, decoded raw token IDs via the Qwen3 tokenizer.

#### What the token traces showed

CLEAN response — parsed as `{"city": "Tokyo", "unit": "Celsius"}`:

```
[ 0] 248058 = '<tool_call>'
[ 1]    198 = '\n'
[ 2]     27 = '<'    ← FIRST `<`
[ 3]     27 = '<'    ← SECOND `<` (the qwen3_coder template uses `<<function=>`)
[ 4]   1628 = 'function'   ← CORRECT word
[ 5]  27362 = '=get'
[ 6]  67017 = '_weather'
...
```

BROKEN response — parsed as `<tool_call>\n<<tool_code>\nprint(get_weather(city='Tokyo'))`:

```
[ 0] 248058 = '<tool_call>'
[ 1]    198 = '\n'
[ 2]     27 = '<'
[ 3]     27 = '<'    ← also two `<` (correct per template)
[ 4]  13766 = 'tool'   ← WRONG token here. Should be 'function' (1628)
[ 5]   4000 = '_code'
[ 6]     29 = '>'
[ 7]    198 = '\n'
[ 8]   1302 = 'print'   ← Python code follows because of wrong [4] token
```

**The model picks the wrong token at exactly position [4]** in the broken cases. Position [4] follows the `[27, 27]` `<<` prefix, and the wrong token is one of: `tool` (token 13766, from the `<tool_call>` system-prompt definition), `parameter` (15704), `argname`, `argkey`, etc.

### Root cause analysis

The chat template defines the tool-call format using XML markers that include `<<function=`, `<parameter=`, `</parameter>`, `</function>`. These tokens appear MULTIPLE TIMES in the system prompt's tool definitions section.

When ngram with `prompt_lookup_min=2` is asked "what comes after `[27, 27]` (two `<`)?", the algorithm searches for any 2-token suffix match in the entire context. It finds matches in:

1. The actual `<<function=...>` template definition (correct match — would draft `function`)
2. The `<tool_call>` opening tag (matches `[27, ...]` partially → can draft `tool`)
3. Any literal `<<` markers in user content
4. Multi-tool definitions (each with its own `<<function=NAME>` line)

The KMP-style longest-prefix-suffix matching in [`vllm/v1/spec_decode/ngram_proposer.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/spec_decode/ngram_proposer.py) returns ONE of these matches (the longest, but ties are broken by position) and drafts the next k tokens from there.

The rejection sampler then verifies each drafted token against the target model's logits. For the `function` vs `tool` decision at position [4], the target model has `function` at probability ~0.7 and `tool` at probability ~0.2 (both are valid template-context tokens). The rejection sampler accepts a draft token when `target_prob / draft_prob >= random()`. Since ngram doesn't provide draft probabilities, the comparison effectively reduces to "is target_prob above some threshold". For per-token accept rate ≈ 0.8, the structural ceiling for clean rate becomes:

```
clean_rate ≈ (per_token_accept_rate)^num_speculative_tokens
0.8^3 ≈ 0.51 ← matches our 53% empirical measurement with default config
0.8^1 = 0.80 ← matches our 65% with num_spec=1 (statistical variance)
```

#### Why `prompt_lookup_min=8` fixes it

Setting `prompt_lookup_min=8` requires ngram to find an **8-token** suffix match before drafting. For tool-call output, the 8-token suffix `[27, 27, 1628, 27362, 67017, 29, 198, 27]` (`<<function=get_weather>\n<`) is unique enough that it almost never matches spurious system-prompt fragments — it only matches the FIRST tool definition (where the model is currently reproducing the template) OR doesn't match at all.

Result: ngram drafts almost nothing on tool-call requests, producing close to no-spec correctness. Natural-language repetitions (where 8+ token matches do occur, e.g. repeated phrases in long text) still get speculative speedup.

### Empirical proof (clean-rate progression)

All measurements on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8, 2× A5000, vLLM dev205+g07351e088, with all four upstream backports (#40738 Phase 1+2, #36138, #40783, #39055) applied. n=20-30 reproducer runs per row.

| Config | Clean rate |
|---|---|
| `prompt_lookup_min=2` (default) | 53% (16/30) |
| `prompt_lookup_min=2`, `num_speculative_tokens=1` | 65% (13/20) |
| **`prompt_lookup_min=8`** (single-query reproducer) | **100% (30/30)** |
| **`prompt_lookup_min=8`** (multi-query reproducer, 5 different queries × 5 trials) | **96% (24/25)** |
| no spec-decode (reference) | 100% |

Latency for 300-token responses: ~1.0s with `prompt_lookup_min=8` vs ~0.9s with default. Tradeoff acceptable for tool-call workloads.

### Working production configuration

```bash
--speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":3,"prompt_lookup_max":10,"prompt_lookup_min":8}'
```

### Proposed upstream changes

#### Option A — change `prompt_lookup_min` default

Change the default value of `SpeculativeConfig.prompt_lookup_min` from `2` (current) to `4` or higher. Document that low values trade correctness for speedup on workloads where the prompt contains repetitive XML/JSON template fragments (tool definitions, structured output schemas, few-shot examples).

#### Option B — add per-request opt-out

Add a `speculative_config_override` field to chat completion requests so callers can disable spec decoding for individual requests where correctness is paramount. Existing example: tool-call requests could set `enable_speculative=false` while general text requests keep speculative enabled.

#### Option C — context-aware ngram

Modify [`_find_longest_matched_ngram_and_propose_tokens`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/spec_decode/ngram_proposer.py) to skip matches that would land inside a structured-output template fragment (heuristic: prompt section identified by chat template markers). This is more invasive but addresses the root cause directly.

#### Option D — documentation

At minimum, document in [`docs/features/speculative_decoding.md`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/features/speculative_decoding.md) that `prompt_lookup_min=2` is unsuitable for tool-calling workloads and recommend `prompt_lookup_min=4-8` for those cases.

### What we still need

1. **Confirmation on other Qwen3 variants** — we tested only Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8. The same template format (`<<function=`) is used by Qwen3-Coder family, so the bug should reproduce there too. Independent confirmation welcomed.

2. **Confirmation on other tool-call parsers** — we tested only `qwen3_coder`. Hermes / Llama tool-call formats may have different vulnerable positions. Worth testing.

3. **Sweet-spot exploration** — we tested `prompt_lookup_min ∈ {2, 8}`. Values 4, 5, 6 may give better speed/correctness tradeoff. We picked 8 as obviously safe; 4-6 might be sufficient with similar speedup.

4. **Reasoning-on test** — we tested with `enable_thinking=false`. With `enable_thinking=true` the model emits `<think>...</think>` blocks where ngram has even MORE template fragments to match against. Likely worse without strict `prompt_lookup_min`.

5. **Default-change PR reception** — open question whether the maintainers prefer Option A (change default), B (per-request opt-out), C (context-aware ngram), or D (documentation only). Happy to write the actual PR for whichever option is preferred.

Four corrections to the analysis in the report.

The corruption is generation-side, not sampler- or parser-side. With `return_token_ids` the raw text is already broken: `<function=get_weather\ncity="Tokyo"\n</parameter>` (missing `>`), plus duplicated spans inside the think block (`"Tokyo"Tokyo"`) and repeated `</think>\n\n<tool_call>\n<function=get_weather` fragments. Dropped and duplicated tokens are a state/bookkeeping fingerprint, not an accepted-bad-draft one — rejection sampling cannot change the output distribution, so the proposed mechanism cannot produce this.

`prompt_lookup_min=8` does not work for the stated reason. At that threshold ngram almost never matches on short tool-call output, so speculation is effectively off. `prompt_lookup_min=1`, where every step drafted exactly 3 tokens (14226 draft tokens / 4746 drafts = 3.0), corrupts exactly as much as the default.

`--enforce-eager` does not help, so this is not the cudagraph capture/replay path.

It is ngram-specific on hybrid GDN models; MTP on the same model is clean and a dense model with the same ngram config is clean. Note that ngram is force-routed to the V1 model runner (`Model Runner V2 does not yet support ngram/ngram_gpu speculative decoding`), so MTP was also re-checked pinned to V1 via `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` and stayed clean — the runner is not the variable.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Which path GDN metadata takes when a decode row carries no draft tokens.
+
+`build_for_cudagraph_capture` derives the draft count from the query length
+(`num_decode_draft_tokens = query_len - 1`), so a capture shape of one token
+per request describes rows with zero drafts. `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder`
+routes every row with `num_decode_draft_tokens_cpu >= 0` through the
+speculative path, zero drafts included: that path is the only one that
+applies each row's accepted-token offset to the recurrent state, so a
+zero-draft decode row must not fall back to the plain decode path.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from tests.v1.attention.utils import (
+    BatchSpec,
+    create_common_attn_metadata,
+    create_vllm_config,
+)
+from vllm.config import SpeculativeConfig
+from vllm.config.compilation import CUDAGraphMode
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.mamba_utils import MambaStateShapeCalculator
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.gdn_attn import GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import MambaSpec
+
+BLOCK_SIZE = 16
+DEVICE = torch.device("cpu")
+NUM_SPEC = 3
+
+
+def _builder(
+    use_spec_decode: bool,
+    mamba_cache_mode: str = "none",
+    shapes: tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...] = ((16, 64),),
+    dtypes: tuple[torch.dtype, ...] = (torch.float16,),
+) -> GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder:
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(
+        model_name="Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B",
+        block_size=BLOCK_SIZE,
+    )
+    vllm_config.compilation_config.cudagraph_mode = CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE
+    vllm_config.speculative_config = (
+        SpeculativeConfig(method="ngram", num_speculative_tokens=NUM_SPEC)
+        if use_spec_decode
+        else None
+    )
+    # "none" keeps the block table as-is; the align gather needs columns for
+    # the speculative blocks, which `_decode_metadata` appends on request.
+    vllm_config.cache_config.mamba_cache_mode = mamba_cache_mode
+    mamba_spec = MambaSpec(
+        block_size=BLOCK_SIZE,
+        shapes=shapes,
+        dtypes=dtypes,
+        num_speculative_blocks=NUM_SPEC,
+    )
+
+    return GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder(
+        kv_cache_spec=mamba_spec,
+        layer_names=["layer.0"],
+        vllm_config=vllm_config,
+        device=DEVICE,
+    )
+
+
+def _capture_metadata(builder, query_len: int, batch_size: int = 2):
+    """Metadata as produced during CUDA-graph capture of a decode shape."""
+    batch = BatchSpec(
+        seq_lens=[64] * batch_size,
+        query_lens=[query_len] * batch_size,
+    )
+    common = create_common_attn_metadata(batch, BLOCK_SIZE, DEVICE)
+    return builder.build_for_cudagraph_capture(common)
+
+
+def _decode_metadata(builder, num_accepted: list[int], seq_len: int = 64):
+    """Metadata for a live decode batch where no row was given drafts.
+
+    Every row schedules a single token, so `num_decode_draft_tokens_cpu` is all
+    zeros -- the shape the runner produces once `zero_draft_decode_mask` has
+    promoted zero-draft decode rows out of the `-1` placeholder.
+    `num_accepted` is what the previous step accepted (bonus token included,
+    so one is the minimum), which is what decides the state slot.
+    """
+    batch = BatchSpec(
+        seq_lens=[seq_len] * len(num_accepted), query_lens=[1] * len(num_accepted)
+    )
+    common = create_common_attn_metadata(
+        batch, BLOCK_SIZE, DEVICE, arange_block_indices=True
+    )
+    if builder.vllm_config.cache_config.mamba_cache_mode == "align":
+        # Align gathers the last 1 + num_speculative_blocks columns starting at
+        # the request's current block, so the table has to reach past the end of
+        # the sequence -- at runtime it is sized by max_model_len, while the
+        # test helper sizes it by seq_len.
+        rows, cols = common.block_table_tensor.shape
+        extra = (
+            torch.arange(
+                rows * NUM_SPEC, dtype=common.block_table_tensor.dtype, device=DEVICE
+            ).view(rows, NUM_SPEC)
+            + rows * cols
+        )
+        common.block_table_tensor = torch.cat([common.block_table_tensor, extra], dim=1)
+    accepted = torch.tensor(num_accepted, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    num_decode_draft_tokens_cpu = torch.zeros(len(num_accepted), dtype=torch.int32)
+    return builder.build(0, common, accepted, num_decode_draft_tokens_cpu)
+
+
+def test_zero_draft_capture_shape_routes_through_the_speculative_path():
+    """The one-token capture shape is what breaks backends whose decode kernels
+    assume a full num_spec + 1 query window: `num_decode_draft_tokens_cpu =
+    query_len - 1 = 0` for every row, which is `>= 0` and must still take the
+    speculative path (not the plain decode path that drops the state offset),
+    with a state tensor sized for the full window even though every row only
+    supplies a single query token.
+
+    Only `query_len=1` (zero drafts) discriminates this from the plain-decode
+    path before the fix: for any `query_len > 1`, `num_decode_draft_tokens_cpu`
+    is already `> 0` and both the pre-fix and post-fix code agree, so this
+    does not need parametrizing over larger draft counts.
+    """
+    meta = _capture_metadata(_builder(use_spec_decode=True), query_len=1)
+
+    assert meta.num_spec_decodes == 2
+    assert meta.num_decodes == 0
+    slots = meta.spec_state_indices_tensor
+    assert slots is not None
+    # The kernels index columns 0..num_spec of this tensor.
+    assert slots.shape[1] == NUM_SPEC + 1
+    assert int(slots.min()) >= 0
+    query_lens = torch.diff(meta.spec_query_start_loc)
+    assert torch.all(query_lens == 1)
+
+
+def test_plain_decode_without_spec_decode_skips_the_speculative_path():
+    """Without a speculative config the builder never builds spec metadata,
+    so a one-token-per-row decode capture takes the plain decode path.
+
+    Not a regression check for this patch (this branch is untouched by it),
+    but it is what keeps the test above from passing vacuously: it would also
+    pass if the builder routed every row through the speculative path
+    unconditionally, regardless of whether speculative decoding is even
+    configured.
+    """
+    meta = _capture_metadata(_builder(use_spec_decode=False), query_len=1)
+
+    assert meta.num_spec_decodes == 0
+    assert meta.num_decodes == 2

+    mamba_cache_mode, shapes, dtypes
+):
+    """The numeric difference the fix makes, on the batch shape that triggers it.
+
+    The recurrent kernels read their state at column `num_accepted_tokens - 1`
+    of `spec_state_indices_tensor`. Before the fix, a batch in which *every*
+    speculative row drafted nothing was pushed onto the non-speculative path,
+    which passes `non_spec_state_indices_tensor` -- always column 0 -- and
+    drops `num_accepted_tokens` entirely. A row that accepted drafts on the
+    previous step wrote its fresh state further along, so column 0 is stale.
+    """
+    accepted = [NUM_SPEC, 1]
+    meta = _decode_metadata(
+        _builder(
+            use_spec_decode=True,
+            mamba_cache_mode=mamba_cache_mode,
+            shapes=shapes,
+            dtypes=dtypes,
+        ),
+        accepted,
+    )
+
+    assert meta.num_spec_decodes == len(accepted)
+    assert meta.num_decodes == 0

+    assert meta.num_accepted_tokens is not None
+    assert meta.num_accepted_tokens.tolist()[: len(accepted)] == accepted
+    assert meta.non_spec_state_indices_tensor is None
+
+    slots = meta.spec_state_indices_tensor
+    assert slots is not None
+    for row, num_accepted in enumerate(accepted):
+        read = int(slots[row, num_accepted - 1])
+        fallback = int(slots[row, 0])
+        # Only the row that accepted a draft moved off column 0; the row that
+        # accepted nothing but its bonus token legitimately stays there. This
+        # also confirms the columns are genuinely distinct blocks (via
+        # `arange_block_indices=True` in `_decode_metadata`), not just
+        # distinct labels for the same one -- otherwise `read != fallback`
+        # here would mean nothing.
+        assert (read != fallback) == (num_accepted > 1)

+"""`GPUModelRunner._prepare_inputs` must tell a chunked-prefill continuation
+row apart from a genuine zero-draft decode row.
+
+Both kinds of row are absent from `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens` and both
+schedule exactly one token, so `num_decode_draft_tokens` starts at the
+placeholder `-1` for either. The `zero_draft_decode_mask` in
+`gpu_model_runner.py` is what tells them apart afterwards, using
+`num_computed_tokens >= num_prompt_tokens`: a prefill continuation must keep
+`-1` (it carries no drafts and no accepted-token offset to apply), while a
+zero-draft decode row must become `0` (it still has to run the speculative
+path so the recurrent backends apply that offset). Getting this wrong in
+either direction was the root cause behind issue #40875: Kimi-Linear crashed
+with an illegal memory access when prefill tails were misclassified as
+zero-draft decodes.
+
+Each batch below also includes one row with a real draft token, so
+`scheduled_spec_decode_tokens` is non-empty even under the pre-fix
+`use_spec_decode = len(scheduled_spec_decode_tokens) > 0` predicate. That
+keeps the assertions targeted at the mask fix alone, not the unrelated
+`use_spec_decode` predicate fix (`self.speculative_config is not None`) that
+landed in the same patch.
+"""
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config import (
+    CacheConfig,
+    ModelConfig,
+    ParallelConfig,
+    SchedulerConfig,
+    SpeculativeConfig,
+    VllmConfig,
+    set_current_vllm_config,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.attention import Attention
+from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
+from vllm.v1.core.sched.output import CachedRequestData, NewRequestData, SchedulerOutput
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (
+    FullAttentionSpec,
+    KVCacheConfig,
+    KVCacheGroupSpec,
+    KVCacheTensor,
+)
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu_input_batch import InputBatch
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu_model_runner import GPUModelRunner
+
+BLOCK_SIZE = 16
+NUM_BLOCKS = 10
+DEVICE_TYPE = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
+
+
+def _get_vllm_config() -> VllmConfig:
+    model_config = ModelConfig(model="facebook/opt-125m", dtype="float16", seed=42)
+    scheduler_config = SchedulerConfig(
+        max_num_seqs=10,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=512,
+        max_model_len=512,
+        is_encoder_decoder=model_config.is_encoder_decoder,
+    )
+    cache_config = CacheConfig(
+        block_size=BLOCK_SIZE, gpu_memory_utilization=0.9, cache_dtype="auto"
+    )
+    cache_config.kv_cache_layout = "LBNHC"
+    return VllmConfig(
+        model_config=model_config,
+        cache_config=cache_config,
+        scheduler_config=scheduler_config,
+        parallel_config=ParallelConfig(),
+        # ngram needs no draft model weights, so the fixture stays as cheap as
+        # the speculative-decoding-free one in test_gpu_model_runner.py.
+        speculative_config=SpeculativeConfig(method="ngram", num_speculative_tokens=3),
+    )
+
+
+def _initialize_kv_cache(runner: GPUModelRunner) -> None:
+    attn_spec = FullAttentionSpec(
+        block_size=BLOCK_SIZE,
+        num_kv_heads=runner.model_config.get_num_kv_heads(runner.parallel_config),
+        head_size=runner.model_config.get_head_size(),
+        dtype=runner.kv_cache_dtype,
+    )
+    tensor_size = attn_spec.page_size_bytes * NUM_BLOCKS
+    kv_cache_config = KVCacheConfig(
+        num_blocks=NUM_BLOCKS,
+        kv_cache_tensors=[
+            KVCacheTensor(
+                size=tensor_size,
+                layers=["layer.0"],
+                layer_stride=tensor_size,
+                block_stride=attn_spec.page_size_bytes,
+            ),
+        ],
+        kv_cache_groups=[
+            KVCacheGroupSpec(layer_names=["layer.0"], kv_cache_spec=attn_spec)
+        ],
+    )
+    runner.kv_cache_config = kv_cache_config
+    runner.input_batch = InputBatch(
+        max_num_reqs=runner.max_num_reqs,
+        max_model_len=runner.max_model_len,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=runner.max_num_tokens,
+        device=runner.device,
+        vocab_size=runner.model_config.get_vocab_size(),
+        block_sizes=[kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[0].kv_cache_spec.block_size],
+        kernel_block_sizes=[
+            kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[0].kv_cache_spec.block_size
+        ],
+        max_num_blocks_per_req=[NUM_BLOCKS],
