+@pytest.fixture
+def spec_decode_model_runner(dist_init):
+    vllm_config = _get_vllm_config()
+    with set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config):
+        model_config = vllm_config.model_config
+        num_heads = model_config.get_num_kv_heads(vllm_config.parallel_config)
+        head_size = model_config.get_head_size()
+        vllm_config.compilation_config.static_forward_context["layer.0"] = Attention(
+            num_heads, head_size, 0.1
+        )
+        runner = GPUModelRunner(vllm_config, DEVICE_TYPE)
+        _initialize_kv_cache(runner)
+        yield runner

+def _new_request(
+    req_id: str, prompt_len: int, num_computed_tokens: int
+) -> tuple[NewRequestData, int]:
+    """A request with `prompt_len` prompt tokens, `num_computed_tokens` of
+    which are already computed (e.g. a prefix-cache hit), scheduled for the
+    single remaining/next token this step."""
+    return (
+        NewRequestData(
+            req_id=req_id,
+            prompt_token_ids=list(range(prompt_len)),
+            mm_features=[],
+            sampling_params=SamplingParams(),
+            pooling_params=None,
+            block_ids=([0],),
+            num_computed_tokens=num_computed_tokens,
+            lora_request=None,
+        ),
+        1,
+    )
+

+def test_prefill_continuation_keeps_placeholder_decode_zero_draft_becomes_zero(
+    spec_decode_model_runner,
+):
+    """One request has one token left to prefill (`num_computed_tokens ==
+    num_prompt_tokens - 1`); another has already finished its prompt and is
+    now decoding with no draft tokens proposed this step; a third is decoding
+    with a real draft. `decode_with_draft` gives the batch a non-empty
+    `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens`, so this also exercises the `-1`-vs-`0`
+    distinction on the pre-fix definition of `use_spec_decode` (`len(sched
+    uled_spec_decode_tokens) > 0`), isolating the mask fix from the unrelated
+    `use_spec_decode` predicate fix that landed in the same patch."""
+    runner = spec_decode_model_runner
+
+    prefill_req, prefill_sched = _new_request(
+        "prefill_tail", prompt_len=11, num_computed_tokens=10
+    )
+    decode_req, decode_sched = _new_request(
+        "decode_zero_draft", prompt_len=3, num_computed_tokens=3
+    )
+    drafted_req, _ = _new_request(
+        "decode_with_draft", prompt_len=3, num_computed_tokens=3
+    )
+    num_scheduled_tokens = {
+        "prefill_tail": prefill_sched,
+        "decode_zero_draft": decode_sched,
+        "decode_with_draft": 2,  # 1 draft token + 1 bonus token
+    }
+    scheduler_output = SchedulerOutput(
+        scheduled_new_reqs=[prefill_req, decode_req, drafted_req],
+        scheduled_cached_reqs=CachedRequestData.make_empty(),
+        num_scheduled_tokens=num_scheduled_tokens,
+        total_num_scheduled_tokens=sum(num_scheduled_tokens.values()),
+        scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={"decode_with_draft": [99]},
+        scheduled_encoder_inputs={},
+        num_common_prefix_blocks=[],
+        finished_req_ids=set(),
+        free_encoder_mm_hashes=[],
+    )
+
+    runner._update_states(scheduler_output)
+    runner._prepare_inputs(
+        scheduler_output,
+        np.array(
+            [num_scheduled_tokens[r] for r in runner.input_batch.req_ids],
+            dtype=np.int32,
+        ),
+    )
+
+    prefill_idx = runner.input_batch.req_id_to_index["prefill_tail"]
+    decode_idx = runner.input_batch.req_id_to_index["decode_zero_draft"]
+    drafted_idx = runner.input_batch.req_id_to_index["decode_with_draft"]
+    assert runner.num_decode_draft_tokens.np[prefill_idx] == -1
+    assert runner.num_decode_draft_tokens.np[decode_idx] == 0
+    assert runner.num_decode_draft_tokens.np[drafted_idx] == 1
+
+
+def test_prefill_tail_of_two_or_three_tokens_also_keeps_the_placeholder(
+    spec_decode_model_runner,
+):
+    """A chunked-prefill tail can be 1, 2, or 3 tokens (`long_prefill_token_

+    )

+        scheduled_new_reqs=[tail_2_req, tail_3_req, drafted_req],

+        num_scheduled_tokens=num_scheduled_tokens,

+        scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={"decode_with_draft": [99]},
+        scheduled_encoder_inputs={},
+        num_common_prefix_blocks=[],
+        finished_req_ids=set(),
+        free_encoder_mm_hashes=[],
+    )
+
+    runner._update_states(scheduler_output)
+    runner._prepare_inputs(
+        scheduler_output,
+        np.array(
+            [num_scheduled_tokens[r] for r in runner.input_batch.req_ids],
+            dtype=np.int32,
+        ),
+    )

+    tail_2_idx = runner.input_batch.req_id_to_index["tail_2"]
+    tail_3_idx = runner.input_batch.req_id_to_index["tail_3"]
+    assert runner.num_decode_draft_tokens.np[tail_2_idx] == -1
+    assert runner.num_decode_draft_tokens.np[tail_3_idx] == -1

+def _mamba_hybrid_state(num_speculative_tokens: int) -> MambaHybridModelState:
+    state = object.__new__(MambaHybridModelState)
+    state.vllm_config = SimpleNamespace(num_speculative_tokens=num_speculative_tokens)
+    state.model_config = SimpleNamespace(max_model_len=8192)
+    state._align_mode = False
+    state.recoverssm = None
+    # A request that accepted 3 drafts (plus the bonus token) on the previous
+    # step; the others have never had a draft accepted.
+    state.num_accepted_tokens_gpu = torch.tensor([4, 1, 1], dtype=torch.int32)
+    return state
+
+
+def _input_batch(
+    num_scheduled_tokens: list[int],
+    num_draft_tokens_per_req: list[int] | None,
+    is_prefilling: list[bool],
+    num_reqs_after_padding: int | None = None,
+) -> SimpleNamespace:
+    """`num_draft_tokens_per_req=None` is a batch where nobody proposed a
+    draft this step, e.g. because ngram found no match for anyone."""
+    num_reqs = len(num_scheduled_tokens)
+    query_start_loc = np.zeros(num_reqs + 1, dtype=np.int32)
+    query_start_loc[1:] = np.cumsum(num_scheduled_tokens)
+    num_tokens = int(query_start_loc[-1])
+    seq_lens = torch.full((num_reqs,), 10, dtype=torch.int32)
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        num_reqs=num_reqs,
+        num_reqs_after_padding=num_reqs_after_padding or num_reqs,
+        num_tokens=num_tokens,
+        num_tokens_after_padding=num_tokens,
+        query_start_loc_np=query_start_loc,
+        num_scheduled_tokens=np.array(num_scheduled_tokens, dtype=np.int32),
+        max_query_len=None,
+        seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound=seq_lens,
+        is_prefilling_np=np.array(is_prefilling),
+        prefill_runs_as_decode_np=None,
+        num_draft_tokens_per_req=None
+        if num_draft_tokens_per_req is None
+        else np.array(num_draft_tokens_per_req, dtype=np.int32),
+        idx_mapping=torch.arange(num_reqs),
+        query_start_loc=torch.from_numpy(query_start_loc),
+        seq_lens=seq_lens,
+        dcp_local_seq_lens=None,
+        positions=torch.zeros(num_tokens, dtype=torch.int64),
+        prompt_lens=None,
+    )
+
+
+def _prepare_attn_metadata(
+    state: MambaHybridModelState,
+    monkeypatch,
+    input_batch: SimpleNamespace | None = None,
+    cudagraph_mode: CUDAGraphMode = CUDAGraphMode.NONE,
+) -> SimpleNamespace:
+    captured = {}
+
+    def fake_build_attn_metadata(**kwargs):
+        captured.update(kwargs)
+        return Mock()
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        "vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_states.mamba_hybrid.build_attn_metadata",
+        fake_build_attn_metadata,
+    )

+    if input_batch is None:

+    state.prepare_attn(

+        block_tables=(),
+        slot_mappings={},

+def test_prepare_attn_keeps_the_accepted_offset_when_the_batch_drafted_nothing(
+    monkeypatch,
+):
+    """`num_accepted_tokens` must reach the attention builders whenever the
+    speculative config is on, even when *this* batch scheduled no draft
+    tokens at all. Before the fix, `use_spec_decode` was gated on this step's

+    """A decode row that got no drafts still has to reach the speculative path.

+    path, and a row that accepted drafts on the previous step keeps that offset
+    even when the current step proposes nothing (the scheduler drops drafts
+    whenever the token budget truncates the step). Marking such a row with the
+    -1 sentinel sends it to the plain decode path, which reads the state at
+    column 0 and ignores the offset.
+    """
+    state = _mamba_hybrid_state(num_speculative_tokens=3)
+    input_batch = _input_batch([3, 1, 1], [2, 0, 0], [False, False, True])

+        0,  # decode row with no drafts: speculative path, offset applied
+        -1,  # one-token prefill tail: no offset to apply, stays a plain row

+    state = _mamba_hybrid_state(num_speculative_tokens=3)
+    input_batch = _input_batch([1, 1], None, [False, True])

+
+    assert metadata.num_decode_draft_tokens_cpu.tolist() == [0, -1]

+
+def test_padded_rows_keep_the_sentinel(monkeypatch):
+    """Full CUDA-graph capture pads the batch; padded rows describe no request

+    input_batch = _input_batch([1, 1], [0, 0], [False, False], num_reqs_after_padding=4)
+

+    )

+    assert metadata.num_decode_draft_tokens_cpu.tolist() == [0, 0, -1, -1]

+
+def test_chunked_prefill_tail_of_two_or_three_tokens_keeps_the_sentinel(
+    monkeypatch,
+):

+    input_batch = _input_batch([2, 3], [0, 0], [True, True])

+
+    assert metadata.num_decode_draft_tokens_cpu.tolist() == [-1, -1]

[Qwen4Exp] PLE pinned-host FP8 lookup will not compile on sm_86, so --engram-config cpu_offload is unusable on consumer Ampere

# [Qwen4Exp] PLE pinned-host FP8 lookup will not compile on sm_86, so `--engram-config cpu_offload` is unusable on consumer Ampere

## Summary

On four RTX 3090 (sm_86), v0.30.0 gets all the way to the first forward pass of the PLE n-gram
lookup and then dies compiling the Triton kernel, because `fp8e4nv` is not a supported fp8 dtype on
this architecture. The model cannot run without host offload, and the host offload path is the one
that does not compile, so this is a hard stop rather than a performance question.

## What worked, so the scope is narrow

Stock `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0`, no patches of any kind, serving a Qwen3.8-Flash-Next checkpoint
whose main body is AutoRound W4 (`quantization_config.quant_method: auto-round`) and whose PLE table
is a separately quantized FP8 e4m3 sidecar. Everything up to the first model forward succeeded:

- `Resolved architecture: Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`, `model_type: qwen4_exp`, max model len
  262144 accepted
- `INCConfig.override_quantization_method` returned `inc` for the auto-round config, so the W4 body
  was claimed natively, no overlay
- the FP8 PLE method was selected from the checkpoint's own config, with no `Fp8Config` involved,
  because `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config` tests `embedding_dtype` before it looks at
  the quantization config. I set `"ple_embedding_dtype": "float8_e4m3fn"` in `text_config` and got:

```
INFO [ngram_embedding.py:720] Initialized PLE embedding language_model.model.layers.1.ple.ple_embedding.ngram_embedding:
  quantization_method=Qwen4ExpPLEFp8EmbeddingMethod, weight_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn,
  weight_device=cpu, pinned=True
```

on all four ranks, which is the behaviour `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'` is supposed to
produce.

- the table itself loaded. I converted a per-row-scaled FP8 sidecar to the upstream layout
  (`...ngram_embedding.shard_N.weight` for N in 0..127 at F8_E4M3 [2500012, 160], plus one
  `weight_scale` at BF16 [1]) and the loader accepted it without complaint:

```
INFO [default_loader.py:430] Loading weights took 445.36 seconds
INFO [model_runner.py:428] Model loading took 18.56 GiB memory and 462.17 seconds   (all four ranks)
```

## The failure

First `profile_run`, so no user traffic and nothing exotic:

```
(Worker_TP1_EP1) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1055] WorkerProc hit an exception.
  File "vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py", line 470, in _lookup
    _lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel[(flat_ids.numel(),)](
  File "triton/runtime/jit.py", line 884, in _do_compile
  File "triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 307, in compile
  File "triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 80, in make_ir
triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 1:0:
def _lookup_ple_embedding_from_pinned_kernel(
ValueError("type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture. The supported fp8 dtypes are ('fp8e4b15', 'fp8e5')")
```

`fp8e4nv` is the e4m3fn spelling, and the kernel's own dtype annotation is what rejects it. The
engine then reports `RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed` and the container exits.

## Why this matters more than it looks

The PLE table is 51B parameters. At FP8 e4m3 it is 47.68 GiB, which does not fit across four 24 GB
cards alongside a W4 body of about 63 GiB, and at BF16 it is roughly 95 GiB, which fits nowhere on
this box. So host offload is not an optimisation for this hardware, it is the only way the model
runs at all, and `cpu_offload` with an FP8 table is exactly the combination that will not compile.

This is also, as far as I can tell, the reason a fork exists. The deployment I am replacing carries
its own PLE offload worker and its own E4M3 gather routine, and the note in its Dockerfile is that
the 64-wide BF16 profiles spill registers under decode and run about 22x slower, so FP8 mode selects
a 16-wide 4-warp profile that stays within 2 percent of BF16. Whoever wrote that hit this wall and
worked around it in software.

## Questions

1. Is sm_86 in scope for `--engram-config cpu_offload` at all, or is the pinned-host FP8 path
   deliberately Hopper/Blackwell-only? If it is out of scope, a config-time refusal would save a
   10-minute load before the first forward pass tells you.
2. Is there a supported way to keep the table in host RAM in a dtype that Triton will compile here?
   The obvious candidate is the unquantized pinned path, but that needs about 95 GiB of host RAM,
   which is why the fork quantized it to 47.68 GiB in the first place.
3. Would a non-Triton gather for the pinned lookup be acceptable upstream, or is the intent that
   consumer Ampere uses device-resident tables only?

## Environment

4x RTX 3090 (sm_86), TP4 with expert parallel, `--distributed-executor-backend mp`, no speculative
decoding, `--max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.965`,
`--kv-cache-memory-bytes 2147483648`, BF16 KV cache (upstream still refuses FP8 main KV for QSA on
this arch, `models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/qsa.py:110`), `--compilation-config '{"mode":0,
"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'`, `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`, vLLM 0.30.0 release image,
PyTorch 2.x as shipped in it, Triton as shipped in it.

Secondary observation, not diagnosed and offered only in case it is familiar: while the shards were
still loading, the allocator logged

```
[rank1] CUDACachingAllocator.cpp:508 expandable_segments: memory mapping failed with OOM on device 1
while trying to map 20971520 bytes (free: 8781824, total: 25295323136)
```

a handful of times per rank, and then the load completed normally at 18.56 GiB per rank. I do not
know what was holding the memory at that moment and I am not claiming it is the cause of the failure
above, which is unambiguous.

query:
[Bug]: Token truncation leaves stale Request.block_hashes and can cause incorrect KV cache hits

### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

Not environment-dependent: this is a code-level invariant break in the scheduler / prefix-hashing path, reproduced against `main` @ `f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1` with the pure-Python script below (no GPU required).

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Summary.** When a request's tokens are truncated in place while `Request.block_hashes` is not, the retained hashes keep fingerprinting the replaced tokens. Prefix-cache, event, and offload consumers treat these hashes as authoritative identities, so the prefix cache can serve KV under a wrong identity: a later request whose prefix matches the OLD tokens gets a cache hit on KV computed from the NEW tokens — silently incorrect output — while the NEW token sequence misses blocks that are actually resident. The trigger reproduced deterministically below is the resumable streaming session path; the Mooncake/NIXL token-pop paths can violate the same invariant when the popped token is already hash-covered (see Related work).

**Root cause** (permalinks pinned to `main` @ `f25953cc5`):

1. `Scheduler._update_request_as_session` discards the last sampled token(s) by truncating `_all_token_ids` past `num_computed_tokens` on the live `Request`, then extends it with the next input chunk and calls `update_block_hashes()` ([`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:1282-1314`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L1282-L1314)).
2. `Request.update_block_hashes` only appends ([`vllm/v1/request.py:244-260`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/request.py#L244-L260)); nothing in the tree ever truncates `request.block_hashes`.
3. The block hasher resumes from `start_token_idx = len(request.block_hashes) * hash_block_size` ([`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:691-748`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L691-L748)), so a block whose hash already exists is never recomputed.

If a discarded sampled token had completed a hash block (for a single discarded token: `num_computed_tokens % hash_block_size == hash_block_size - 1`), the hash chained over the now-replaced token persists, and all later hashes chain from it.

**Deterministic reproduction** (mirrors the statements `_update_request_as_session` executes at `scheduler.py:1293-1314`):

```python
from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
from vllm.utils.hashing import sha256
from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import get_request_block_hasher, init_none_hash
from vllm.v1.request import Request

init_none_hash(sha256)
hash_block_size = 4

req = Request(
    request_id="session",
    prompt_token_ids=[1, 2, 3],
    sampling_params=SamplingParams(),
    pooling_params=None,
    block_hasher=get_request_block_hasher(hash_block_size, sha256),
    resumable=True,
)
req.append_output_token_ids(99)  # completes hash block [1, 2, 3, 99]
assert len(req.block_hashes) == 1
stale_hash = req.block_hashes[0]

req.num_computed_tokens = 3  # sampled token 99 was never computed

# --- what _update_request_as_session runs for the next streaming chunk [4] ---
del req._all_token_ids[req.num_computed_tokens :]  # scheduler.py:1297
req._output_token_ids.clear()                      # scheduler.py:1298
req._all_token_ids.append(4)                       # next input chunk
req.update_block_hashes()                          # scheduler.py:1314

assert list(req.all_token_ids) == [1, 2, 3, 4]
# block_hashes[0] still fingerprints [1, 2, 3, 99]: the hasher resumes at
# len(request.block_hashes) * hash_block_size == 4 and never revisits block 0.
assert req.block_hashes[0] == stale_hash

# Explicit identity check: the retained hash is the OLD sequence's, not the new one's.
import vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils as kcu
assert req.block_hashes[0] == kcu.hash_block_tokens(sha256, kcu.NONE_HASH, [1, 2, 3, 99])
assert req.block_hashes[0] != kcu.hash_block_tokens(sha256, kcu.NONE_HASH, [1, 2, 3, 4])
```

**Consequence (source derivation; the wrong cross-request hit requires prefix caching to be enabled).** At session-update time the boundary block has not yet been cached as a full block (its last token was never computed). The corruption lands when the resumed session is next scheduled: `allocate_slots()` commits the block under `request.block_hashes[0]` — the identity of `[1, 2, 3, 99]` — **before** the forward pass runs; the insertion chain is [`kv_cache_manager.py:493-503`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py#L493-L503) -> [`kv_cache_coordinator.py:283-287`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py#L283-L287) -> [`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:443-450`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L443-L450) -> the insertion at [`block_pool.py:280-297`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py#L280-L297) (fine-grained hash-block configurations go through the partial-block callers at [`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:787`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L787) / [`:1674`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py#L1674) into [`block_pool.py:490-512`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py#L490-L512)); the subsequent forward then writes the KV computed from `[1, 2, 3, 4]` into that block. On lookup, `get_computed_blocks` matches `request.block_hashes` under the `num_tokens - 1` cap ([`kv_cache_manager.py:237-241`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py#L237-L241)) and resolves cached blocks via [`block_pool.py:198-223`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py#L198-L223): a later request continuing past that block with actual prefix `[1, 2, 3, 99, …]` (it must extend beyond the block because of the `num_tokens - 1` cap, so an exactly-four-token request does not hit) computes that same hash and gets the block — a prefix-cache hit on KV computed from different tokens, i.e. silently wrong output — while a later `[1, 2, 3, 4, …]` request computes a hash absent from the map and misses a resident block. The stale identities also flow into KV cache events (`BlockStored` payloads are emitted from the same pool paths, e.g. [`block_pool.py:331`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py#L331) and [`:527-528`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py#L527-L528)) and into offload keys (the offloading connector derives `OffloadKey`s from `request.block_hashes` in `update_offload_keys`, [`offloading/scheduler.py:306-316`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py#L306-L316)), so external indexers and offloaded copies inherit the wrong fingerprints. (The script pins the request-side invariant break; the pool-side consequence is derived from the cited paths — no end-to-end wrong-output run is included here.)

**Candidate fix direction (text-only; see limitations).** In `_update_request_as_session`, invalidate hashes past the kept prefix before extending — `del session.block_hashes[num_computed_tokens // self.hash_block_size :]` (the scheduler holds `hash_block_size`): hashes of blocks fully inside `[0, num_computed_tokens)` remain valid, and the resumed hasher recomputes the boundary block. On this path that is also sufficient for the pool side, because the boundary block was never cached as a full block. Two limitations to be explicit about: (i) this is correct for **text-only** requests — with multimodal inputs the incremental hasher restarts its feature scan from the last MM feature in the request's current list — including newly appended ones (`curr_mm_idx = -1`) — not from the first feature overlapping the recomputed range ([`kv_cache_utils.py:713-748`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L713-L748)), so deleting the hash suffix alone can still yield wrong hashes — when the suffix recomputation starts from a non-zero boundary and the recomputed range overlaps earlier MM features while a later feature exists in the current list (confirmed by fresh-vs-incremental hash comparison for such cases; deleting all hashes and recomputing from token 0 does not hit this); covering multimodal requires also rewinding the MM scan start plus regression tests, or scoping the streaming fix to text-only sessions; (ii) a general fix for truncating already-computed tokens would additionally have to keep the `BlockPool` side consistent (`KVCacheBlock` block-hash state and the `cached_block_hash_to_block` mapping). Both are out of scope for the minimal fix here. I'm happy to send a fix PR for the text-only path unless the streaming-sessions folks would rather take it.

**Related work (checked, not duplicates).**

- #43372 (open) adds an explicit per-session KV-cache truncation API and clears `Request.block_hashes` on that new path; it does not touch `_update_request_as_session`, and clearing the request-side list alone does not cover the pool side for already-computed truncated tokens. Related — neither a duplicate nor a complete fix precedent.
- Adjacent paths that can violate the same invariant (not reproduced end-to-end; should not block this fix): the Mooncake and NIXL connector token-pop paths for hybrid/Mamba models — NIXL's `_truncate_mamba_request_for_prefill` ([`nixl/base_scheduler.py:341-365`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_scheduler.py#L341-L365)) and the Mooncake connector's last-token pop ([`mooncake/mooncake_connector.py:701-707`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f25953cc59f9b4ba9b04b16228d2b86dcfbcbdb1/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py#L701-L707)) — can leave stale `block_hashes` when the removed token is already covered by a computed hash (e.g. the pre-pop length lands exactly on a hash boundary). They warrant separate fixes/audits.

[Bug]: cudagraph_mode=FULL crashes on prefill with FlashInfer sparse MLA on SM100

### Your current environment

vLLM main @ `2a52715ef7`, 1× B200 (SM100), Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `cudagraph_mode=FULL` and the FlashInfer sparse MLA backend on SM100 (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`), the engine crashes as soon as a prefill chunk replays a FULL CUDA graph. `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, the default, works.

`FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMMetadataBuilder` declares `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS` (added in #52783), so `FULL` mode captures FULL graphs for mixed/prefill batches too. Neither MLA prefill backend can replay those:

| MLA prefill backend | Result |
|---|---|
| FlashAttention (default for DeepSeek-V3.2) | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` during FULL-graph replay |
| TRTLLM ragged (default for larger MLA dims, e.g. GLM-5.3) | `ValueError: TRTLLM ragged prefill contains mixed active and empty query rows: query_lens=[512, 0, 0, 0]`: the FULL graph pads the batch with empty requests |
| FlashInfer | not valid for these MLA dimensions |

In both failing cases, a 512-token prefill chunk is dispatched to a request-padded FULL graph. The variable-length verification FULL graphs that adaptive DSpark (#52783) needs may be what `ALWAYS` was meant for. If so, a lower support level plus the varlen-decode hook might cover that without capturing prefill.

**Repro** (DeepSeek-V3.2 shrunk to 4 layers, dummy weights; no HiSparse or KV connector). Pass `TRTLLM_RAGGED` or `FLASH_ATTN` as the argument to pick the prefill backend:

```python
# cudagraph_mode=FULL with FlashInfer sparse MLA (SM100) crashes when a
# prefill chunk replays a FULL graph. Usage: python repro.py [MLA_PREFILL_BACKEND]
import os
import sys

os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER", "1")

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

SHRINK = {"num_hidden_layers": 4, "hidden_size": 256, "intermediate_size": 512,
          "moe_intermediate_size": 128, "num_attention_heads": 8,

          "n_shared_experts": 1, "first_k_dense_replace": 1, "index_topk": 128}


def shrink(config):
    config.update(SHRINK)
    if hasattr(config, "quantization_config"):
        delattr(config, "quantization_config")
    return config


def main() -> None:
    attention_config = {"backend": "FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE"}
    if len(sys.argv) > 1:
        attention_config["mla_prefill_backend"] = sys.argv[1]
    llm = LLM(
        "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2",
        load_format="dummy",
        hf_overrides=shrink,
        max_model_len=8192,
        max_num_seqs=4,
        max_num_batched_tokens=512,
        attention_config=attention_config,

With `"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"` the same script prints `OK 16`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug A JSON schema that uses `allOf` with more than one branch is silently ignored by the default `auto` structured output backend. xgrammar 0.2.3 compiles a multi-branch `allOf` into a grammar that does not enforce the branches. The model can emit JSON that violates the schema, and vLLM reports no error. `auto` does not fall back to a backend that works, because the xgrammar feature gate `has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features` does not list `allOf`. The `guidance` backend (llguidance 1.7.6) enforces the same schema correctly. Multi-branch `allOf` is common. Pydantic and OpenAPI emit it for model inheritance, for example `allOf: [{"$ref": "#/$defs/Base"}, {...}]`. ### Reproduction ```python import json import xgrammar as xgr from transformers import AutoTokenizer from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams, StructuredOutputsParams from vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_xgrammar import ( has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features, validate_xgrammar_grammar, ) schema = { "$defs": { "Base": { "type": "object", "properties": {"x": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 10}}, "required": ["x"], } }, "allOf": [ {"$ref": "#/$defs/Base"}, {"type": "object", "properties": {"y": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["y"]}, ], } print(has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features(schema)) # False validate_xgrammar_grammar( SamplingParams(structured_outputs=StructuredOutputsParams(json=schema)) ) # no exception tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("openai-community/gpt2") info = xgr.TokenizerInfo.from_huggingface(tokenizer) ctx = xgr.GrammarCompiler(info).compile_json_schema(json.dumps(schema)) for instance in ['{"x":15,"y":"a"}', '{"x":5,"y":"a"}', '{"x":15}', '"hello"']: print(instance, xgr.GrammarMatcher(ctx).accept_string(instance)) ``` ```text False {"x":15,"y":"a"} True {"x":5,"y":"a"} True {"x":15} True "hello" True ``` The first row is valid. The next three violate `minimum: 10`, the `required` fields, or the object type, yet the grammar accepts all of them. ### Expected behavior In `auto` mode, vLLM enforces the schema, or rejects the request with a clear error. It must not return output that violates the schema without any signal. ### Workaround Start the server with `--structured-outputs-config.backend guidance`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

[Bug] `ep_gather` output store overflows int32 with DeepEP v2 expanded layout (IMA in `_fwd_kernel_ep_gather`)

## Summary

`_fwd_kernel_ep_gather` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/deep_gemm_utils.py` computes the output row offset as `cur_token * output_tensor_stride0` in int32. With hidden size K = 6144, this wraps once the output has more than 2^31 / 6144 = 349,525 rows. The store then lands out of bounds and faults with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`.

#53914 (fe284ea17d) fixed the matching **input** read (`source_token_index_i64 * input_tensor_stride0`). The **output** store is still int32 on main (9ed81581, line 410):

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9ed81581a896a5bf0448b26d43f52486a435f799/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/deep_gemm_utils.py#L405-L413

```python
        tl.store(
            output_tensor
            + cur_token * output_tensor_stride0   # int32 * int32
            + cur_block * BLOCK_D
            + off_d,
            ...
```

With the DeepEP v2 all2all backend, the gather receives an **expanded** layout: `recv_topk_ids` is `(rows, 1)`, with one row per (token, local expert) pair. So the output has as many rows as the permuted input, and both offsets hit the same limit. When `topk_ids` is `(tokens, topk)`, the output has one row per received token and normally stays far below the limit, which is presumably why this hasn't shown up before.

## Setup

- GLM-5.2-FP8 (K = 6144, 256 experts, top-8), `--moe-backend deep_gemm`, `--all2all-backend deepep_v2` (hybrid mode)
- 4 nodes × 8 × H100, DP4 × PCP8 (DCP8), TP1, EP32, eager
- vLLM from #57075 at bf0dca88, with the #53914 `ep_gather` input fix applied on top
- `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096` (8192 fails the same way, sooner)

## Evidence

With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, the first memory-profiling forward (`determine_available_memory` → `profile_run`) faults in the gather on the busiest EP rank:

```
deep_gemm_moe.py:385 apply → deepgemm_unpermute_and_reduce → ep_gather
  → _fwd_kernel_ep_gather
RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

A host-side bounds check added in front of the launch shows valid inputs and an output past the limit:

```
[EP_GATHER DEBUG] input=(393216, 6144) stride0=6144 elems=2415919104
  out=(393216, 6144) topk_ids=(393216, 1) expert_map_len=256 valid=393216
  inv_perm_min=0 inv_perm_max=393215 bad_expert_ids=0
```

393,215 × 6144 = 2,415,912,960 > 2^31 − 1.

Before the #53914 input fix was applied, the same config faulted at the same place. At 2048 batched tokens (busiest rank ≈ 196,608 rows), startup completes. With both the #53914 input fix and the output fix below applied, the same 4096-token config starts up cleanly.

## Fix

Widen the output offset the same way #53914 widened the input offset:

```diff
-            + cur_token * output_tensor_stride0
+            + cur_token.to(tl.int64) * output_tensor_stride0
```

The other offsets in the kernel (`cur_token * recv_topk_ids_stride0` etc.) have strides of `topk` and stay small.

A regression test in `tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py`, alongside #53914's, could call `ep_gather` with an expanded `(rows, 1)` `topk_ids` and `rows * K > 2^31`.

diff --git a/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/deep_gemm_utils.py b/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/deep_gemm_utils.py
index 624aa9ce86..1dee9bad54 100644
--- a/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/deep_gemm_utils.py
+++ b/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/deep_gemm_utils.py
@@ -415,7 +415,7 @@ def _fwd_kernel_ep_gather(
 
         tl.store(
             output_tensor
-            + cur_token * output_tensor_stride0
+            + tl.cast(cur_token, tl.int64) * output_tensor_stride0
             + cur_block * BLOCK_D
             + off_d,
             accumulator.to(output_tensor.dtype.element_ty),

[Performance]: WSL2: `VLLM_WSL2_ENABLE_PIN_MEMORY=1` makes the default V2 runner ~12% faster per decode step

### Proposal to improve performance

On #54655, @njhill suggested evaluating "whether we want to change the default of [`VLLM_WSL2_ENABLE_PIN_MEMORY`] generally." Here's that evaluation on one WSL2 machine, default (off) vs on, runs alternated:

- **Batch-1 decode, Qwen3-8B-AWQ: 8.7-9.0 → 7.7-7.8 ms per token (−12%)**, pip install and Docker image alike. BF16 saves the same ~1.1 ms per step (21.3-21.9 → 20.2-20.4 ms).
- **Throughput** (`vllm bench serve`, random 256/256): +13-14% at concurrency 1, +8% at 16, +3.8% at 64.
- **Why:** in a torch profile, GPU-busy time per step is unchanged (7.56 vs 7.61 ms). With the default, the trace shows pageable host-to-device copies and the GPU idles 1.29 ms per step; with pinned memory on, 0.16 ms.

#41496's review measured a <2% throughput cost for pinned memory on WSL2 (RTX 5080, a 4B model). With today's V2 runner it goes the other way here. Happy to test a default change on this setup.

<details><summary>Setup and reproduction</summary>

Greedy, 64 output tokens, median gap between streamed tokens; 3 requests per run, 2 runs per arm, arms alternated (off, on, off, on). KV cache pinned so both arms get the same capacity. The desktop was idle (a GPU-engine monitor showed only VS Code, at ~2% of the 3D engine).

| Batch-1 time per output token | Default | `VLLM_WSL2_ENABLE_PIN_MEMORY=1` |
|---|---|---|
| Docker image, AWQ | 8.69-8.88 ms | 7.65-7.79 ms |
| pip install, AWQ | 8.81-9.02 ms | 7.75-7.81 ms |
| Docker image, BF16 | 21.30-21.93 ms | 20.18-20.38 ms |

Correctness:
- **Greedy outputs.** Comparing across restarts doesn't work here: default vs default already differs between restarts, because Inductor re-tunes reductions by timing (#58899). So I kept one engine alive (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`) and swapped `NonUvaBuffer.uva` between the current and patched copy (blocking, non_blocking, blocking, non_blocking), with 16 prompts x 128 tokens per round. Token ids and top-5 logprobs were bitwise identical in every round, in two separate engines. The profiler confirms the swap took effect (2222 vs 0 stream syncs per round).
- **Stream ordering.** On main, every reader of a `NonUvaBuffer` GPU slot runs on the copy's stream, or on a side stream that calls `wait_stream` on it first (async output, spec decode and PP copy streams). This is a static read; ubatch/DBO, PP and DeepSeek-V4.1 paths were not exercised.
- **Overwriting the host buffer right after the copy.** I issued a `non_blocking` pageable copy behind a ~7.5 ms GPU sleep, then overwrote the CPU source immediately: 0/200 corrupted results from 4 B to 16 MiB (pinned control: 200/200 corrupted). On this driver, pageable copies up to 64 KiB are staged at call time and return immediately; larger ones wait for the stream, so they stay correct and keep today's cost. `NonUvaBuffer` copies are far below 64 KiB. That threshold is driver behavior, not a CUDA guarantee, so native Linux is not covered.

[Bug] Hybrid mamba prefix-cache hit reads out of bounds: add_request seeds the state index with cache_config.block_size after it was lowered below mamba_block_size (Xid 31 / illegal memory access)

**Summary.** `MambaHybridModelState.add_request` seeds the running mamba state slot as
`(num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size`, but by the time it runs, `EngineCore._initialize_kv_caches` has already reassigned `cache_config.block_size` to `min(block_size of prefix-cacheable groups)`. For hybrid models that carry an extra attention group with a small block size (here: a DFlash2/EAGLE-style drafter group with sliding-window spec, block 64 or 1024), that minimum is far below `cache_config.mamba_block_size` (7168 here). The seed therefore indexes the mamba block table in the wrong units, and `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel` → `_copy_mamba_state_block` reads `block_table[src_col]` past the row width without a bounds check. Above the row width this is an illegal memory access (Xid 31, `FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`); below it, the request silently restores the KDA/mamba state from an unrelated block.

**Where.**
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py`, `add_request`: `(new_req_data.num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size` (main, ~L70-77).
- `vllm/v1/engine/core.py`, `_initialize_kv_caches`: `vllm_config.cache_config.block_size = min(participating ...)` (main, ~L298-305). The comment there already notes that a small-block group "would otherwise drag the global block_size below the real allocator block size and desync it from mamba"; the min still includes any prefix-cacheable attention group with a smaller block.
- `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py`: `preprocess_mamba_align_fused_kernel` uses the seed as `src_col`; `_copy_mamba_state_block` loads `block_table_base + src_col` with no check against the row width. Mamba state blocks and the block-table row width (`cdiv(max_model_len, mamba_block_size) + num_speculative_blocks`) are in units of `mamba_block_size`.

**Environment.** vLLM `v0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187` (container image from github.com/gitcommit90/glm-5.3-one-spark), GLM-5.3-Flash (hybrid: MLA sparse attention + KDA linear attention), DFlash2 speculative decoding (`num_speculative_tokens=5`), `--enable-prefix-caching` (so `mamba_cache_mode=align`), `max_num_seqs=1`, `max_num_batched_tokens=7168`, `mamba_block_size=7168`, V2 model runner, TP=1 (UniProcExecutor, so the worker sees the reassigned config), DGX Spark GB10.

**Reproduction (deterministic).** Threshold model `crash ⇔ (hit_tokens - 1) // small_block >= row_width` matched 8/8 observations:

| max_model_len | drafter block | row width | cached prefix (tokens) | seed | result |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 262144 | 64 | 42 | 7168 | 111 | crash |
| 262144 | 1024 | 42 | 7168 / 28672 / 43008 | 6 / 27 / 41 | no crash, wrong state restored |
| 262144 | 1024 | 42 | 57344 | 55 | crash |
| 524288 | 1024 | 79 | 93184 | 90 | crash |

Steps: send prompt A (>= 8 full mamba blocks, e.g. 57k tokens), then A + a different question. The second request fails within <1 s with `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` (reported at the first sync point, e.g. `flash_linear_attention/ops/index.py prepare_chunk_indices .tolist()` or `np_to_pinned_tensor`), and `dmesg` shows `NVRM: Xid 31 ... MMU Fault ... FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`.

**Fix (verified).** Divide by the mamba block size:

```diff
-                (new_req_data.num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size
+                (new_req_data.num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.mamba_block_size
```

`mamba_attn.py` already computes the same quantity from `kv_cache_spec.block_size`. With the one-line change: 8-, 13-, 34- and 63-block prefix hits complete, needle-in-a-haystack answers on warm (cached) requests are identical to cold ones at 100k and 250k tokens (5/5 needles each), and warm TTFT drops from 139 s to 8.7 s at 100k. A needle placed inside the last partial scheduler chunk before the block boundary is also retrieved on warm requests.

Alternatively/additionally, `core.py` could exclude sliding-window drafter groups from the `min(...)` (as it already excludes opt-out groups), which would also stop `_mamba_block_aligned_split` from chunking prefill at multiples of the drafter block (6144 instead of 7168 here).

**Why this is easy to miss.** With `max_num_seqs >= 2` the out-of-range read often lands in another request's row (a valid block id), so there is no fault, only a silently wrong recurrent state; with TP >= 2 the workers keep a config copy from before the reassignment. Symptoms then look like "model loops / degrades after a while under load" rather than a crash.

**Before/after on the same input.** Prompt A of 57 344 tokens (8 full mamba blocks), then A + a different question:
- without the fix: HTTP 500 after 0.2 s, `Xid 31` in dmesg (02:43, `crash-BLOCKS8-*.log`);
- with the fix: warm request completes in 11.7 s, 50 176 tokens served from cache.

**Validation with the fix (same container build, `max_model_len` 262144 and 524288):** 13-, 34- and 63-block prefix hits complete; multi-needle recall on warm (cached) requests equals cold at 100k, 250k and 450k tokens (5/5 each; warm TTFT 8.7 s vs 139 s cold at 100k); a needle placed inside the last partial scheduler chunk before the block boundary is also retrieved on the warm request; a 3-hour soak with 57 multi-turn conversation turns (every turn a prefix hit, contexts up to 184k tokens) plus fresh 41k–354k-token prompts: 133/133 requests OK, zero Xid, no memory drift.

- vLLM Python source: `c723a831a81cb4ff89ea6d61b2d15109306ed1bc` on `main`, tested on 2026-09-22.

- PyTorch `2.13.0+cu132`, Transformers `5.16.1`.

- `nixl` / `nixl-cu13` `1.3.2`.

A normal `OffloadingConnector` configuration with `TieringOffloadingSpec` and a `kvcr` secondary tier fails during engine initialization:

No backpressure option is configured. The factory now passes `backpressure_detector=None` unconditionally, but the KVCR adapter does not accept this keyword. The server exits before becoming healthy or serving any request.

KVCR's [official developer guide](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/kvcr/blob/317e62f301300c101bf9c911e020fb89b35f1583/docs/dev-guide.md) documents this secondary-tier configuration. The integration is experimental, but it is an in-tree registered adapter. The failure affects the normal factory construction path for KVCR; ordinary primary-only CPU offloading still starts and generates successfully in the same environment.

[Bug]: DeepStream video backend raises ZeroDivisionError on MP4s with moov at the end, and truncates fragmented MP4s

### Your current environment

- vLLM 0.28.0 (`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0` image), with `nvidia-deepstream-videodecode-cu13==9.0.2` and the GStreamer packages from the docs installed on top
- 8x NVIDIA L20, TP=2, Qwen3.5-family model (`Qwen3VLVideoProcessor`)
- `--media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"fps": 1, "backend": "deepstream"}}'`

Full `vllm collect-env` output available on request.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `backend: "deepstream"`, video requests fail with `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero` for ordinary MP4s that store the `moov` box after `mdat`. That is ffmpeg's default layout and common in phone recordings. Fragmented MP4s don't crash, but the probe only sees the first fragment, so frames get sampled from the first few seconds only.

`probe_metadata()` in `nvidia-deepstream-videodecode` pushes the bytes through `appsrc` with `stream-type=0` (push mode, not seekable) into `parsebin`. In push mode qtdemux can't reach a trailing `moov`, no video caps get negotiated, and the probe returns `(0, 0.0, 0.0, 0, 0, '')` without raising. The DeepStream branch of `VideoBackend.load_bytes` passes that straight through (`vllm/multimodal/video.py:1194` in v0.28.0), and `Qwen3VLVideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample` then computes `int(total_frames_num / original_fps * fps)` (`video.py:1286`).

`main` behaves the same: `vllm/multimodal/video_decoders/deepstream.py` passes the probe result through unchanged, and the Qwen3-VL sampler still divides by `original_fps`. The decode pool's source (`_reset_source` in `_ds_dec.py`) uses the same non-seekable `appsrc`, so fixing only the probe may not be enough.

Repro, probe only (no GPU needed):

```bash
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=1280x720:rate=30 -t 60 -c:v libx264 -b:v 4M -pix_fmt yuv420p moov_at_end.mp4
ffmpeg -i moov_at_end.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart moov_at_start.mp4
ffmpeg -i moov_at_end.mp4 -c copy -movflags frag_keyframe+empty_moov fragmented.mp4
```

```python
from nvidia.deepstream_videodecode import probe_metadata

[Bug][CPU] V1 CPU sampling (fused_gumbel_argmax) is biased: the 2^20 noise table makes about half of a 152K vocabulary unreachable

### Your current environment

vLLM main `98b29aa99` (also `e6674262f`, `4056c8ac1`, `015497965`), CPU build (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`), torch 2.13.0+cpu. Linux x86_64 (Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz, AVX512), Python 3.12. Also reproduced on macOS arm64 (Apple M1 Pro).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Since #53913, the V1 CPU sampler (`TopKTopPSampler.forward_cpu`) samples with `torch.ops._C.fused_gumbel_argmax`. Its Gumbel noise comes from a fixed table of 2^20 entries (`csrc/cpu/sampling_kernels.cpp`), generated once by `mt19937(42)`. Token `i` of a row with seed `s` gets `g_gumbel_table[(s + i) & (2^20 − 1)]`, and `forward_cpu` draws `s` uniformly from [0, 2^31). So every row's noise is one of only 2^20 windows of the same table. The sampling distribution is exactly the fraction of windows on which each token wins, and enumerating them shows it is biased:

```python
import numpy as np, torch
import vllm._C  # noqa: F401

T, V = 1 << 20, 151_936
row = torch.tensor(-1.1 * np.log(np.arange(1, V + 1)), dtype=torch.float32)  # Zipf(1.1)
counts = torch.zeros(V, dtype=torch.int64)
for s0 in range(0, T, 256):
    seeds = torch.arange(s0, s0 + 256, dtype=torch.int64)
    tok = torch.ops._C.fused_gumbel_argmax(row.view(1, -1).expand(256, V).contiguous(), seeds)
    counts += torch.bincount(tok, minlength=V)
q = counts.double().numpy() / T
p = torch.softmax(row.double(), -1).numpy()
print("TV(kernel, softmax) =", 0.5 * np.abs(q - p).sum())
print("unreachable tokens  =", int(((q == 0) & (p > 0)).sum()), "of", V, "mass", p[q == 0].sum())
print("top-1 prob kernel   =", q[0], "exact", p[0])
```

```
TV(kernel, softmax) = 0.06979336957267332
unreachable tokens  = 79078 of 151936 mass 0.03745368388499906
top-1 prob kernel   = 0.1411447525024414 exact 0.13242019650725323
```

So about half of a Qwen-sized vocabulary can never be sampled, and the head is over-sampled. Tokens with p < 2^-20 hold 5.0% of the mass here but get 3.3%. On a confident row (top logit 10 above an N(0, 2) background), TV is 0.004. For V ≤ 32, TV is 1e-4 to 1e-3.

The bias reaches the engine. We used a tiny random-weight Llama and a custom logits processor that writes the Zipf row into every step, then drew 20,000 one-token requests at `temperature=1.0`:

| runner | samples on the 79,078 unreachable tokens (exact: 749) | P(top-1) (exact 0.132) |
|---|---|---|
| V1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) | **0** | 0.144 |
| Model Runner V2 | 768 | 0.134 |

Model Runner V2 samples with its own Triton Gumbel and is fine. V2 is the default only when `HAS_TRITON` is true, and the triton-cpu wheel in `requirements/cpu.txt` is x86_64-only. So V1, and this table, is the default on every non-x86 CPU build: arm64, s390x and ppc64le. On macOS arm64 we got 0 of 2,000 samples on unreachable tokens, against 75 expected.

`test_cpu_fused_sampling.py::test_distribution_chi_squared` doesn't catch it, because it caps the vocabulary at 100 (`small_vocab = min(vocab_size, 100)`).

### Expected

Samples from softmax(logits), up to RNG quality. Possible directions:
- Fresh per-call uniforms from a counter-based generator keyed on (seed, position, token), as #54143 proposes and as Model Runner V2 already does.
- Or keep the table only for greedy or very low-entropy rows.

Related: #53913, #54143.

[Question][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer: does the 640-token block table reach 32-pool pages on gfx942/gfx950 too?

We found this on hardware vLLM doesn't support (gfx1030, Radeon Pro V620), running GLM-5.3-Flash without aiter. The code path involved is shared with gfx942/gfx950, and we have no MI300/MI355 to check it on. Could someone with one confirm or rule it out?

**What we see.** `Glm5NextIndexerCache` stores pooled keys in pages of 32 pools (storage block 128 tokens at `index_kpool=4`). The hybrid KDA page rule makes the attention block 640. On ROCm the sparse-MLA and indexer backends accept `MultipleOf(16)` (`get_supported_kernel_block_sizes`), so `select_common_block_size` keeps kernel block 640. The indexer metadata builder only converts the table when the storage block is a multiple of the kernel block (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`, prefill and decode branches; unchanged on main):

```python
if (
    kernel_block_size is not None
    and self.kv_cache_spec.block_size != kernel_block_size
    and self.kv_cache_spec.block_size % kernel_block_size == 0
):
    factor = self.kv_cache_spec.block_size // kernel_block_size
    indexer_block_table = (block_table[:, ::factor] // factor).contiguous()
```

128 % 640 ≠ 0, so the 640-token table goes to `get_compressed_slot_mapping` (the kpool writer) and to `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache_triton` as if each entry named one 32-pool page. With per-chunk block allocation:
- pools written before their block exists land in padding;
- positions past the allocated blocks alias block 0;
- positions past the 52-column table (at `max_model_len` 32768) are masked by the gather.

On NVIDIA the kernel block is 64, so the `// factor` branch applies. As far as we can tell nothing here is aiter-specific: the kpool path uses `forward_cuda` on ROCm whether aiter is on or off.

**Reproducer.** One GPU, stock vLLM only, no model: [`repro_rocm_kpool_table.py`](https://github.com/Omnicef/vllm/blob/glm53-v030/tests/local/repro_rocm_kpool_table.py). It writes a 9,432-token prompt in the served prefill chunks with the real ROCm kpool writer and slot mapping, gathers it back with the real gather, and compares against the writer's own output. The two arms are the table as the builder produces it and a page-granular table (block `b` → pages `5b … 5b+4`). On gfx1030, identical over two runs:

```
table as the builder produces it  : ooo000000000000xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm  (3/74 pages correct)
page-granular table               : oooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooo  (74/74 pages correct)
```

(`o` correct, `0` all-zero, `x` wrong keys, `m` masked.) Above `index_topk`, where the indexer actually selects, this breaks long-context retrieval: a two-fact needle at ~9k tokens failed for us until the table was expanded. If it reproduces on MI300, the fix we use expands each kernel-block id into its storage pages when the kernel block is a multiple of the storage block (about 20 lines in the builder, happy to send).

**Secondary note (tile order).** With aiter off (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` unset), the decode logits fall back to `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch`. It reads each page token-major, while two ROCm writers store values in 16×16 tiles when `block_size > 1`: `indexer_k_quant_and_cache_triton` and the GLM-5.3 kpool writer. DeepSeek-V4's C4A compressor (`compress_norm_rope_store_triton`) writes token-major, so its pages are unaffected. See the correction on #51555 for numbers. aiter's reader passes `Preshuffle=block_size > 1` and isn't affected.

+    monkeypatch.setattr(indexer_mod.current_platform, "is_cuda", lambda: False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(indexer_mod.current_platform, "is_rocm", lambda: True)

+            cache_config=SimpleNamespace(block_size=manager_block),

## 🐛 Describe the bug **Expected:** with `tool_choice="required"` or a named tool, GLM returns the tool call, also when it goes straight from reasoning to `` without writing `` (the glm45/glm47 parsers accept that as the end of reasoning). **Actual:** the structured-output manager starts the tool grammar one token after that ``. The grammar never sees it, so it forces a second ``. The model writes `Write...`, the parser drops the call, and the response has `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` with no `tool_calls`. This happens in normal agent use. When a tool result quotes GLM's own tags, the prompt contains the real `` special token (id 154843), and the model sometimes copies it into its reasoning. On the prompt below, 7 of 40 seeds lost the call under `required` and 8 of 40 under a named tool. ### Reproduction Server: ```bash vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 32768 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 ``` (`--max-model-len 32768` only keeps startup short.) **1. Agent reads a file that mentions GLM's tags, then must call `Write`.** ```bash curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4", "temperature": 0.7, "seed": 8, "max_tokens": 1500, "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Read docs/parser.md and save a one-sentence summary of it to /tmp/summary.md."}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "Read", "arguments": "{\"file_path\": \"docs/parser.md\"}"}}]}, {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": "# Parser notes\n\nGLM-5.3 wraps every function call in ... tags; each argument is kv.\n"}], "tools": [ {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "Read", "description": "Read a file.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "required": ["file_path"], "properties": {"file_path": {"type": "string"}}}}}, {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "Write", "description": "Write a file.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "required": ["file_path", "content"], "properties": {"file_path": {"type": "string"}, "content": {"type": "string"}}}}}], "tool_choice": "required", "parallel_tool_calls": false}' | jq '.choices[0] | {finish_reason, tool_calls: .message.tool_calls, reasoning: .message.reasoning[-60:]}' ``` Expected: one `Write` call with `file_path` and `content`. Actual, in 4 of 4 runs: `"finish_reason": "tool_calls"`, `"tool_calls": null`. The reasoning stops mid-sentence at `...GLM-5.3 wraps every function call in`, which is where the model wrote ``. The raw output (from logprobs, `toolresult_repro.py`, seed 8) is: ``` ...GLM-5.3 wraps every function call in Readfile_pathdocs/parser.md<|obser... ``` Under `required` the doubled call is sometimes `Read` and sometimes `Write` (seed 17: `Writefile_path/tmp/summary.md...`). Either way the parser reads the name as `Read` or `Write`, drops it as unknown, and returns no call. Which seeds trigger varies between runs, so a loop over seeds is more reliable than one seed. Seed 8 with `required` triggered in every run we made. `toolresult_repro.py` (in the details below) loops over 40 seeds and counts a seed only if the first `` comes before any ``, the next output is a second `` (the special token or its text pieces), and the response has no complete `Write` call. Results on a fresh `e5e38ba9` server: | `tool_choice` | seeds lost to this bug (run 1) | (run 2) | |---|---|---| | `required` | 7 of 40 | 5 of 40 | | named `Write` | 8 of 40 | 4 of 40 | Under a named tool the response has no tool calls and `finish_reason` `"stop"` or `"length"`. Without `"parallel_tool_calls": false`, `required` keeps opening calls after the doubled tag: in 5 runs of the request above, 3 returned no call, one returned 15 calls (14 of them `Write({})`), and one looped until `finish_reason="length"`. **2. Deterministic variant with `logit_bias`.** `154842` is `` and `154843` is ``. The bias makes the model end its reasoning with ``. ```bash curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4", "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 400, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Paris?"}], "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "description": "Get the current weather for a city.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}}], "tool_choice": "required", "parallel_tool_calls": false, "logit_bias": {"154842": -100, "154843": 10}}' | jq '.choices[0] | {finish_reason, tool_calls: .message.tool_calls}' ``` Actual: `{"finish_reason": "tool_calls", "tool_calls": []}`. With `"tool_choice": "auto"` and no `parallel_tool_calls`, the same request returns `get_weather({"city": "Paris"})`. `parallel_tool_calls: false` only stops the +10 bias from opening extra calls. A small script that sends this request four ways gave the same result in 3 of 3 attempts:
live_repro.py output ``` [0] A auto (no grammar) tool_calls=[('get_weather', '{"city": "Paris"}')] finish_reason='tool_calls' | stream: ['get_weather'] 'tool_calls' raw output: ...'th the city "Paris".get_weathercityParis<|observation|>' [0] B required tool_calls=[] finish_reason='tool_calls' | stream: [] 'stop' raw output: ...'th the city "Paris".get_weathercityParis<|observation|>' [0] C named tool_calls=[] finish_reason='stop' | stream: [] 'stop' raw output: ...'th the city "Paris".get_weathercityParis<|observation|>' [0] D auto, parallel=off tool_calls=[] finish_reason='stop' | stream: [] 'stop' raw output: ...'th the city "Paris".get_weatherget_weathercityParis<|observation|>' ... 3/3 attempts: control A has the call, B, C and D lost it BUG PRESENT ``` A has no grammar. In B and C the grammar never saw the first ``, so it forced a second one. In D the `auto` grammar treated `get_weather` as free text and waited for its `` trigger. The same applies to `auto` with a `strict` tool, which we also saw lose the call (5 of 32 seeds on the tool-result prompt).
**3. CPU only.** A short script drives `StructuredOutputManager.accept_tokens` with the structural tag the server builds for `tool_choice="required"`: ``` model wrote: 'I need the weather.' grammar was fed: '' next tokens the grammar allows: ['<', ''] forced output: 'get_weathercityParis' parsed: tool_calls=None content=None BUG PRESENT: skipped by the grammar, required call lost ``` ### How often it happens On simple prompts GLM-5.3 almost always writes `` first: 0 of 128 `required` requests on a weather prompt at temperature 1 ended reasoning with ``. The trigger is a prompt that contains GLM's tool tags, for example a tool result or file that quotes them. There, 10 to 20% of seeds at temperature 0.7 lost the call. Separately, when this bug is fixed the request in (1) can still return `Write({})` on some seeds. That is a different bug: the reasoning ends with ``, then the `content` argument quotes `...` and the call is mangled. The seed counts above exclude it. ### Root cause Line numbers are on `e5e38ba9`. - `vllm/parser/glm47_moe.py:173-176` ends reasoning on `(REASONING, TOOL_START)`, emitting `REASONING_END` and `TOOL_CALL_START`. `ParserEngine._derive_reasoning_end_token_ids` (`vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py:615-635`) therefore puts both `` and `` into `reasoning_end_token_ids`. - `StructuredOutputManager._get_constraint_start` (`vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py:260-267`) returns `find_reasoning_end_offset(...) + 1`. The `+ 1` is right for ``, which is not part of the answer. It is wrong for ``, which is both the end of reasoning and the first token of the tool-call grammar. - `accept_tokens` (`vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py:444-466`) feeds `new_token_ids[constraint_start:]` to the grammar, so the `` is skipped. The frontend already treats this token as content. `ParserEngine.extract_content_ids` (`parser_engine.py:674-699`) returns `input_ids[i + 1:]` for `` but `input_ids[i:]` for the other reasoning-end ids. So the parser and the grammar gate disagree about where the answer starts. This came in with #55223 (merged 2026-09-08), which added `find_reasoning_end_offset` to `_get_constraint_start`. The refactor in #48200 kept the `+ 1`. A fix PR that links this issue follows. It lets the grammar consume a reasoning-end token that `extract_content_ids` keeps as content, while the bitmask still starts after that token, so speculative decoding does not force the end of reasoning early. With it, the seed loop in (1) finds 0 of 40 in both modes and the `logit_bias` request returns `get_weather({"city": "Paris"})`. ### Other parsers likely affected Only GLM was run live. For the other `ParserEngine` configs, we derived the reasoning-end token sets from the code. These also contain a tool-start token, which `_get_constraint_start` skips the same way: | Parser | Tool-start token in `reasoning_end_token_ids` | |---|---| | glm47_moe, qwen3, nemotron_v3, granite_thinking | `` | | seed_oss | `` | | gemma4 (thinking) | `<\|tool_call>` | | kimi_k2 | `<\|tool_calls_section_begin\|>` | | minimax_m2 | `` | | deepseek_v4 (thinking) | `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` | | mistral (special-token reasoning) | `[TOOL_CALLS]` | Whether a model actually ends reasoning this way, and whether its grammar starts with that token, varies per model. We did not check that live. ### Related No existing issue or PR covers this, as far as we found. Related but different: - #57714: kimi_k3, structured output never engages when the completion skips the think channel. Its fixes do not change the `+ 1`. - #44676: `thinking_token_budget` does not treat `` as an implicit reasoning end (Qwen3.5). Same implicit end, different component. - #58315: the GLM `required` grammar accepts split marker tokens that the streaming parser treats as content. - #39056: Qwen3.5 tool calls lost when the XML `` is emitted inside ``. - #44006 / #46149 (closed): the same reasoning/grammar boundary, under speculative decoding and for the structural-tag reasoning prefix.

The same build accepts normally for two metric windows early in the run, so the drafter itself is functional. ## Environment - Model: `local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (`qwen4_exp` architecture) - 2x DGX Spark GB10 (sm_121), one prefill + one decode instance - `kv_connector: NixlConnector`, `kv_load_failure_policy: fail` - `speculative_config.method: mtp`, `num_speculative_tokens: 3` - `mamba_cache_mode: align`, `max_num_seqs: 1`, concurrency 1 - Synthetic acceptance disabled (`specdec_rejection_sample_method` not set), so these are real acceptance numbers ## Symptom Over a 1-hour run: 149 requests, 149 successful KV transfers (avg ~400-490 ms), 360 SpecDecoding metric windows. **358 of 360 windows report:** Mean acceptance length: 1.00, Accepted: 0 tokens, Drafted: 333 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.000, 0.000, 0.000, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 0.0% Drafted throughput stays at ~33 tokens/s throughout, so the drafter is running and proposing; only acceptance is zero. **The 2 exceptions are consecutive, early, and healthy:** 19:13:33 Per-position acceptance rate: 0.204, 0.118, 0.054 (12.5%) 19:13:43 Per-position acceptance rate: 0.551, 0.326, 0.191 (35.6%) The second is a textbook MTP profile, decaying with position. After 19:13:53 it is `0.000, 0.000, 0.000` for 356 consecutive windows and never recovers, while KV transfers keep succeeding for every subsequent request. ## Why "exactly zero" is the interesting part With ~300 drafted tokens per window, a merely mis-conditioned drafter would still match the target by chance now and then, especially at position 0. Exactly `0.000` across all three positions, for 356 consecutive windows, looks like the acceptance test failing categorically rather than draft quality degrading. ## What has been ruled out **PR #58784** (placeholder draft tokens in the padded first step after a P/D remote KV load) is **not** the cause. The patched `rejection_sampler.py` was hot-copied into the running container and its application verified in the server log; the symptom was unchanged. ## Inconclusive Raising `kv_recompute_threshold` to 1e9 via `kv_connector_extra_config`, to force the decode instance to re-prefill locally instead of trusting transferred state, did not change the symptom. The parameter name and placement were verified correct (read through `get_from_extra_config` in `base_scheduler.py`, and `NixlPullConnector` confirmed in use), but `External prefix cache hit rate` stayed at 100%, so it is not clear the knob took effect. This experiment should be considered unperformed rather than negative. ## Leading hypothesis Qwen3-Next works in PD and it's a GDN MoE. The only difference is QSA. NIXL transfers the KV cache; if the decode instance resumes with KV but without — or with stale — recurrent and side state, the target's logits need not agree with what the drafter expects. The MTP drafter is itself a `full_attention` layer consuming hidden states, so it is sensitive to exactly that mismatch. This is a hypothesis, not a diagnosis. It has not been tested. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

## Status update: what we tried so far (progress and dead ends)

**Setup.** vLLM `109b5363fc` (Sept 21), Dynamo frontend, `NixlConnector` (`kv_producer`/`kv_consumer`, 1 prefill + 1 decode worker, TP=1 each), `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (`qwen4_exp`: QSA sparse indexer + GDN + MoE), MTP `num_speculative_tokens` k ∈ {1,2,3}, `max_num_seqs=1`, concurrency 1, 200 requests via aiperf (synthetic prompts, real acceptance). Reproduced on DGX Spark (GB10, two nodes) and on GB200 (both workers on the same host, GPU 0/1).

### Symptom, measured per request

Decode-side `SpecDecoding metrics` plus per-request latency from the client give the same picture on every run:

| run | req #1 | **req #2** | req #3 … #200 |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB10, k=3, 2048/256 | 25.1 s, acc. 0 | **13.8 s, mean acc. len 2.07** | ~24.2 s, acc. 0 |
| GB10, k=2, 2048/256 | 22.8 s, acc. 0 | **10.7 s, 1.89** | ~22.0 s, acc. 0 (req #3 starts healthy for ~100 tokens, then collapses mid-request) |
| GB200, k=3, 64/64 | 1909 ms, acc. 0 | **487 ms, ~1.3** | ~1010 ms, acc. 0 |
| GB200, k=3, 64/64, `indexer_budget=8192` | 2051 ms | **414 ms** | ~1045 ms, acc. 0 |

So: **exactly one request out of 200 — always the second — gets a healthy acceptance rate; everything after it proposes at full rate and accepts nothing** (all positions 0.000, incl. position 1). Request #1 is also at zero for every k, including k=1 (cold start of the remote-prefill path; k=1 recovers from request #2 on and never collapses: 4671/8147 accepted, 57%). The drafter keeps drafting; it is the verification that rejects everything. The collapse depends on the *number of requests served*, not on tokens generated (3 × 128-token requests on GB200 vs ~2.5 × 2300-token requests on GB10).

**Healthy controls** (same image, same k=3): aggregate TP=1 and TP=2 (~2.07–2.09), Qwen3.8-27B in P/D (hybrid, no QSA), Qwen3-Next-80B in P/D (GDN+MoE+MTP, no QSA). The discriminant is **QSA (`qwen4_exp`) + disaggregated prefill**.

### Dead ends (experiments; all still collapse unless noted)

- **Network**: identical on a single GB200 host, two GPUs.
- **Prefix caching** off (`--no-enable-prefix-caching`).
- **Sampling**: `temperature=0` (greedy).
- **Prompt alignment**: `isl=2050` (breaks `isl % compress_ratio == 0` and `isl == indexer_budget`); also `isl=64`. `prompt_len % 4` does not separate healthy from collapsed requests either (req #2 is healthy with 115 and with 116 prompt tokens).
- **Sparse indexer path**: `indexer_budget=8192` (the kernel maximum: `cooperative_topk supports k=512, 1024, 2048` blocks) with 64/64 prompts, so pruning can never trigger (32 blocks ≪ 2048). `index_share_for_mtp_iteration=true` (`skip_topk`/`compact_topk_indices` path).
- **CUDA graphs**: decode with `--enforce-eager`.
- **KV transfer knobs**: `block_size` 64/128, `kv_recompute_threshold` (inert here: 100% external hit), LMCache (not usable with these hybrid models anyway), CPU offload (not possible on GB10 unified memory).
- **PR #58784** (rejection sampler fix) hot-patched into the image: no change, not even on request #1.
- **Asymmetric k** (prefill k=1, decode k=3): not possible — the scheduler block size depends on k (LCM 3152 with k=1 vs 3200 with k=3) and Nixl asserts `Local block size 3200 is not divisible by remote block size 3152`.
- `indexer_budget=32768`: engine fails at init (`cooperative_topk … got k=8192`); the default 2048 tokens (= 512 blocks) is also the kernel's *minimum*.

### What we excluded by reading the code at `109b5363fc`

- The QSA ring (`CircularBufferSpec`, block_size = `cr·cdiv(cr+k, cr)` = 8) **is transferred whole and with the right geometry**: own NIXL region (page = 8 slots, one descriptor per block, `_scratch_region_indices`), `block_size_ratio = 1`, no clipping (`get_exchange_clipped_blocks` only touches SWA/SSM groups), no prefix-cache trimming of that group. The compressed key cache (`MLAAttentionSpec`) is transferred whole too.
- Ring blocks are **never zeroed** (`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:118-124` excludes `CircularBufferSpec`; the scheduler also skips zeroing of blocks the async load overwrites) and are reused **LIFO** (`block_pool.py:787-796`: unhashed → prepended to the free queue), so every request gets the same physical ring block. Since the decode-side ring is overwritten by the transfer, this alone cannot explain the pattern.
- **Per-request probe inside `QSAIndexer`** (dumping `QSAForwardMetadata` for both side caches at the first 6 verify steps of each request, decode in eager mode): positions, logical positions, ring/compressed `slot_mapping`, `visible_blocks`, `k_work_metadata` and block tables are **identical** between the healthy request #2 and the collapsed ones, apart from block ids. The indexer addressing is correct; the fault is in cache *contents* or in drafter/verifier state.

### Current hypothesis / next step

Some per-request state on the **decode** side (MTP drafter state, rejection-sampler / draft-token buffers, `req_index` slot reuse in the model runner) that is correct only on the second request: initialised on request #1 (broken), right on #2, and from #3 on contaminated by what #2 left behind (#1 leaves nothing because it never accepts; k=1 does not accumulate). Next: instrument the rejection sampler / drafter the same way (hot-patched module + `--enforce-eager`) and compare request #2 vs #3 token by token. Pointers to the exact per-request state reset in the MTP + QSA path would be very welcome.

### Your current environment

vLLM main @ bf13ecc (also reproduced on v0.28.0 and v0.29.0 source), 4x NVIDIA L4, CUDA 13.0 torch 2.13, Python 3.12.

`EagleLlama4ForCausalLM` and `EagleMistralLarge3ForCausalLM` implement `SupportsMultiModalEmbeddings` by aliasing the method object `SupportsMultiModal.embed_input_ids`:

```python
embed_input_ids = SupportsMultiModal.embed_input_ids  # type: ignore
```

That method calls `self._embed_text_input_ids(...)` and reads `self._has_oov_mm_tokens`, which are defined on `SupportsMultiModal`, a class these drafters do not inherit. As soon as the target is multimodal (so `supports_mm_inputs` is True and the draft prefill embeds a batch), the engine dies in the profile run:

```

    self.inputs_embeds[:num_input_tokens] = self.model.embed_input_ids(
File "vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py", line 507, in embed_input_ids
    inputs_embeds = self._embed_text_input_ids(
AttributeError: 'EagleLlama4ForCausalLM' object has no attribute '_embed_text_input_ids'. Did you mean: 'embed_input_ids'?
```

Model Runner V1 calls the same `embed_input_ids`, so it is not runner specific. `--enable-mm-embeds` does not change the outcome.

vllm serve RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-quantized.w4a16 \

What goes wrong for each field: - `lora_bias=True`: PEFT saves a `lora_B.bias` tensor. Since #53555 (which allowed `.bias` for the `score` / `classifier` heads of classification adapters), `parse_fine_tuned_lora_name` also accepts `lora_A.bias` / `lora_B.bias` and maps them to the same module as the weight, so whichever tensor is loaded last becomes `lora_b`. With safetensors the bias comes first in key order, so lora_B's weight survives and the bias is dropped; with a `.bin` adapter the ordering can differ and lora_B can end up as the 1-D bias. Before #53555, such adapters were rejected with `... is unsupported LoRA weight`. #53555 is in v0.31.0 but not in v0.30.0, so this is a regression in the v0.31.0 release. - `init_lora_weights` = `"pissa"` / `"pissa_niter_*"` / `"olora"` / `"corda"` / `"loftq"` / `"lora_ga"`: when PEFT loads such an adapter it rewrites the base layer weights (for example `pissa_init` and `corda_init` in `peft/tuners/lora/layer.py` assign `get_base_layer().weight.data`), so the adapter is only correct on the modified base. vLLM serves it on the unmodified base. PEFT's own `path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` produces a regular adapter and resets the field to `true`, so converted adapters are unaffected. PiSSA was measured above; OLoRA was measured on CPU (similar gap); CorDA, LoftQ and LoRA-GA follow from the PEFT code, not measured. - `layer_replication`: PEFT builds extra layers by sharing base weights and gives each its own LoRA; vLLM's model has no such layers, so those LoRAs are skipped. - `alora_invocation_tokens` (Activated LoRA): PEFT applies the adapter only from the invocation tokens on; vLLM applies it to every token (support was proposed in #19710, closed unmerged). - `use_bdlora` (BD-LoRA) and `use_qalora`: the stored A or B matrices are narrower than the layer (block-diagonal / pooled input). `set_lora` copies them into the top-left corner of the zero-padded slot without a shape check, so they load as a different matrix. Measured for BD-LoRA (mean diff 0.44 on a tiny Llama); QALoRA follows from the same code path. This also affects published adapters. A search of the Hugging Face Hub finds about 100 PEFT adapters whose config still has `init_lora_weights` set to `"pissa"` / `"olora"` or uses aLoRA. For one of them, `AkameV6p5/qwen2.5-3b-agent-pissa-sft` on `Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B`, vLLM differs from PEFT by 3.44 in mean prompt logprob (PEFT's own run-to-run difference is 1.55, from its randomized SVD) and matches PEFT with `init_lora_weights` forced to `true` (0.06), so it is served as a plain LoRA on the unmodified base. Not affected (checked to match PEFT): `use_rslora`, `layers_to_transform`, `exclude_modules`, `init_lora_weights` = `true` / `"gaussian"` / `"eva"` / `"orthogonal"` / `"mica"`, embedding and `lm_head` LoRA. ## Proposed fix Reject these adapters with a clear error, the same way DoRA is rejected: read the fields in `PEFTHelper` and add them to `_validate_features`, and only accept `.weight` for `lora_A` / `lora_B` in `parse_fine_tuned_lora_name` (keeping `.bias` for `score` / `classifier`).
